news.Title: 'A cyclical downturn is inevitable' in an AI crash: Strategist Dario Perkins
news.Content:
If the weakness in tech stocks continues to gain steam , it could end up being really ugly for investors, given how aggressively they have gone into tech stocks in recent years.

That's the warning in a new paper making the rounds on Friday from TS Lombard strategist Dario Perkins titled "Wargaming the AI Crash."

"The reality, of course, is that it is hard to identify the exact trigger for an AI crash. But we can model the fallout. In terms of financial markets, the impact is likely to be sizable. US stocks would be hit hard, with (at least) a 30% decline. That would wipe out around $20 trillion in market cap," Perkins said. Across debt markets and private credits, he estimated "$125–200 billion in losses. Spreads would blow out, and we should expect a wave of tech-related defaults."

"The weakest players in the AI ecosystem — the neoclouds , Oracle ( ORCL ), standalone model developers and construction/equipment suppliers — would face acute distress," he added. "The hyperscalers would suffer serious revenue downgrades; and even the promise of lower capital spending (the return of free cash flow) would offer scant consolation. The traditional banking sector would not be immune."

In terms of how this would affect the US economy on a broader level, Perkins said, "A cyclical downturn is inevitable. Capital spending would plunge and confidence evaporate. There would be sizeable job losses in the construction sector. But as far as recessions go, we don't think this one would be particularly severe (at the milder end of historical norms). Not only is the macro footprint of the AI boom smaller than people think, but there is plenty of room for the Fed to cut rates. Ultimately, this policy response would be successful, especially for the bottom of America's K-shaped economy."

The backdrop for tech stocks has become increasingly fraught as October has played out.

Concerns began earlier this month with neocloud company CoreWeave ( CRWV ).

The company's corporate bonds across maturities continued to be dumped amid fears of an AI slowdown and its implications for the company's precarious balance sheet. That has triggered a subsequent sharp sell-off in the stock.

CoreWeave stock has been crushed in October to the tune of 35%.

Meta ( META ) then dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results this week, posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive spending on AI.

The company said it would issue a new tranche of stock to help fuel its AI build-out.

Tesla ( TSLA ) also slashed its capital expenditures plan for the year by $5 billion to $20 billion.

Story Continues

Thursday was an absolute bloodbath for Big Tech as all of these issues collided in a perfect storm, with the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) getting slammed nearly 2.6% in its worst single-day beatdown since June.

The sharp selling has persisted into Friday.

"The question going forward will be whether investors see any bounces over the coming weeks as an opportunity to take some more chips off the table in the tech sector … or if the 'dip buyers' will prevail once again. The problem is that those 'dip buyers' have been getting burned in the chip stocks," Miller Tabak strategist Matt Maley said. "So, we wonder if they are starting to get a little gun shy … and whether they'll continue to be as aggressive as they have been throughout much of this year."

news.Title: Apple and Alphabet are sending Wall Street different signals
news.Content:
The two biggest AI bets on Wall Street are not making the same one. One company is writing checks that would strain most national budgets. The other is letting partners do the heavy lifting while it sells the hardware everyone else needs.

Retirement savers feel that split most. A portfolio that is meant to last decades has different needs than a trade meant to pay off next quarter, and the debate comes down to Alphabet versus Apple. Both report earnings this month, so the timing is hard to ignore.

How the Alphabet and Apple gap opened up

Alphabet has lost about $860 billion in market value since its peak, close to Walmart's $937.1 billion, according to 24/7 Wall St., citing an October 17 post by Charlie Bilello of Creative Planning that put Apple at an all-time high and Alphabet 17% below.

Apple is worth $4.95 trillion and Alphabet is worth $4.21 trillion. Apple leads the Magnificent Seven this year at 25.26%, against 6.47% for Alphabet, which has also fallen 4.84% in the past month.

Also read: Apple just made a surprising move with a popular product

Apple's run is real. The stock touched an all-time high of $345.34 in September, weeks after John Ternus became CEO on September 1, and was up 25% for the year with a market value just under $5 trillion, according to TheStreet . The iPhone 18 lineup went on sale September 19 with prices raised by $100, and the $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo ships October 23.

Alphabet went the other way after July's earnings. Revenue beat estimates and Google Cloud grew 82% to $24.8 billion, but the company lifted its 2026 capex outlook to $195 billion to $205 billion, up from $180 billion to $190 billion, and the stock sank.

The next test arrives on October 28. Alphabet brought in $119.8 billion in second-quarter sales, up 24%, yet Bank of America expects about $199 billion of capex this year and $301 billion in 2027, plus a $12.4 billion free cash flow loss in the third quarter. The bank also expects Search growth to cool from 17% to 14% while Cloud accelerates to 93%.

What Alphabet's spending is doing to its cash

Alphabet spent $44.9 billion on capital expenditures in the second quarter, double the year-earlier amount, and posted its first negative free cash flow since going public in 2004, according to Axios , citing FactSet. Net income got a lift from roughly $99 billion in net gains on equity securities.

Alphabet was the first hyperscaler to report this season, Axios noted, so investors read its spending as a signal for the group.

To pay for the buildout, Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion in equity in June, including a $10 billion private placement to Berkshire Hathaway at $351.81 per Class A share and $348.20 per Class C share, Bloomberg reported . The company said demand for its AI services exceeds the supply it can deliver.

Story Continues

Plainly, Alphabet is funding growth partly with new shares rather than only cash from operations. For existing holders, that means dilution while the spending keeps climbing. A company known for generating its own cash substantially now turns to the market for funding.

That spending picture does not cancel out what Alphabet is actually building. Revenue climbed 24% last quarter and Cloud jumped 82%, according to Reuters . Investors are not questioning the growth. They are questioning when the bills stop growing faster than the returns do.

How Apple stays out of the spending race

Apple's June quarter showed what its model delivers. iPhone sales jumped 22% year over year, according to TheStreet . Tim Cook said Apple had underestimated demand, while calling on-device AI a competitive weapon. The redesigned Siri was still in public beta and not yet a proven source of new revenue.

Apple is not skipping AI so much as sourcing it. It overhauled Siri in part by tapping Google's AI technology behind the scenes. That arrangement helps explain why Apple's capital spending sits far below Alphabet's. Analysts say a successful Siri revamp by year-end could put Apple on even footing with Google's Gemini assistant.

More Apple:

Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge

Apple secret new device is a challenge to Amazon

Bank of America warns Apple investors because of Meta's Muse

Wall Street watched the strategy at the June 8 developer conference, where Apple unveiled Siri AI and deeper AI features across its devices. Bank of America had called the event an important marker for Apple's AI future.

Apple also sells the hardware AI builders need. Meta's newest model was optimised for Apple's M5 Ultra chip. Apple shares slipped to $342.00 on October 15. Developers building AI tools need serious local hardware, so every purchase is revenue Apple books today.

What it means for a retirement portfolio

The two stocks have returned almost the same over twelve months, nearly 30% each. The difference is the path. Alphabet runs through larger bills, while Apple runs through iPhone demand and a valuation near 39 times earnings. A premium price leaves much less room for error.

A saver near retirement leans on the dependable payouts. Apple pays a $0.27 quarterly dividend. The dividend was raised 4% in May alongside a $100 billion buyback authorization. It also guided September-quarter revenue growth of 9% to 11%. That kind of cash return supports a steadier profile than a company spending beyond its free cash flow.

For a retirement account, the gap between these two companies is not just about AI. It is about what kind of risk you are paid to take. Both report within a day of each other this month. When the numbers land, the real question is whether the story each stock is telling still holds.

Related: The Fed has a new warning for Wall Street and the stock market

news.Title: Stocks mixed, day after AI-related selloff; oil prices rise again
news.Content:
By Caroline Valetkevitch and Marc Jones

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after ‌Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

The Nasdaq was up 0.2% after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1%.

An ‌index of semiconductors was up about 1%. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI ​trade.

It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity."

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned ‌fears over further disruption to energy supplies from ⁠the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.

US crude rose 2.56% to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74%. European natural gas prices jumped.

AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL

Investors were digesting corporate earnings ⁠news. American Express shares fell 3.5% after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.

Telecom company shares, including Verizon, dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

The ​Dow ​Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9%, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 ​eased 11.14 points, or 0.14%, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq ‌Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21%, to 26,062.75.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15%, to 1,121.29.The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4%.

Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4% earlier. [.T]

US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992%. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and ‌on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since ​June.

Story Continues

EURO FALLS

The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both ​the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized ​after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.

French yields, which were down 5 basis points ‌at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, ​the most of any major euro zone ​country and the most in a week since late May.

A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.

France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units ​for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez ‌said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody's later on Friday.

The euro was last down 0.12% at $1.12, ​set to end the week 0.35% lower.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Marc Jones in London; Additional reporting ​by Stella Qiu in Sydney; Editing by Elaine Hardcastle and Rod Nickel)

news.Title: Mark Zuckerberg Faces $11 Billion Question With Unexpected Answer
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

California's proposed billionaire tax is already having consequences in Silicon Valley before voters decide its fate on Nov. 3.

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) recently struck an agreement with CEO Mark Zuckerberg designed to keep him in California for eight years while giving him greater flexibility to sell non-voting shares if Proposition 40 leaves him facing a multibillion-dollar tax bill.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with RIVN.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The ballot measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on Californians worth at least $1 billion , based on residency at the beginning of 2026. CalMatters estimates roughly 200 billionaires could be affected. Supporters say the money would primarily fund healthcare, along with education and food assistance.

Zuckerberg, whose net worth is estimated at about $240 billion , had considered moving his primary residence outside California if the proposal passes, according to Reuters.

Meta's solution involves its newly authorized Class C non-voting shares .

The arrangement allows Zuckerberg to sell a portion of those shares to potentially meet the tax obligation without surrendering the voting control he holds through Meta's Class B stock. He can immediately sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives, equivalent to 10% of his overall economic stake.

In return, Zuckerberg has committed to remain in California, or wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, and continue leading the company for eight years.

The debate extends beyond Zuckerberg.

Supporters of Proposition 40 argue that the tax could raise tens of billions of dollars for public services. Opponents argue it could encourage wealthy residents to relocate, reducing future income-tax collections and potentially affecting investment. Estimates of the ultimate fiscal impact vary widely and depend heavily on how billionaires respond.

Investor Takeaway

I think the investor significance is less about the politics of the tax itself and more about how wealth taxes can spill directly into corporate decisions .

Meta has effectively redesigned part of its capital structure partly to give Zuckerberg greater liquidity while preserving his control.

That makes Proposition 40 relevant not only to California tax policy, but also to executive retention, share issuance and corporate governance at some of the world's largest technology companies.

For Meta investors, the key things to watch are the Nov. 3 vote, Zuckerberg's share sales, the new Class C structure and whether similar arrangements emerge at other California companies.

Whatever voters ultimately decide, Meta's response shows that the proposal is already affecting boardroom decisions.

news.Title: Cathie Wood Makes Surprise Move Across Three Popular Tech Stocks
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought heavily into Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) after the stock's post-earnings selloff, while reducing exposure to Palantir ( NASDAQ:PLTR ) and Roblox (RBLX).

ARK funds purchased 38,110 Meta shares worth about $24.7 million on Thursday, Oct. 22, after the stock plunged roughly 7% and erased its gains for the year.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with RIVN.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

At the same time, Wood sold 7,936 Palantir shares worth about $1.55 million and unloaded 33,793 Roblox shares valued at roughly $1.8 million .

The moves come as the three stocks sit in very different places.

Meta's selloff followed a quarter in which revenue jumped 26% year over year to $64.6 billion , helped by stronger advertising and engagement. But investors focused heavily on rising AI spending after the company lifted the lower end of its 2026 capital-expenditure outlook to $135 billion , leaving the range at $135 billion to $145 billion.

That spending pressure has become harder to ignore, particularly with Meta's free cash flow turning negative for the first time since 2012, according to TipRanks.

Palantir, meanwhile, remains one of the market's strongest AI winners.

Second-quarter revenue increased 93% to $1.94 billion , while U.S. commercial revenue surged 149%. The company also raised its full-year revenue outlook to roughly $8.15 billion to $8.158 billion .

But after a roughly 1,111% three-year rally , expectations are already extraordinarily high.

Roblox presents a very different setup.

The stock remains down about 58% over the past year , with investors still questioning profitability, growth and monetization. Second-quarter bookings increased just 8%, while the company guided for a 14% to 18% decline in Q3 bookings .

Investor Takeaway

I think the interesting part of ARK's move is the contrast in valuation and sentiment.

Meta was bought immediately after investors punished the stock for rising AI costs, while Palantir was trimmed after one of the strongest multiyear rallies in the market.

That does not necessarily mean Wood has turned bearish on Palantir or Roblox.

But the size difference is notable: ARK bought nearly $25 million of Meta while selling only about $3.3 million combined across the other two names.

That makes the trade look more like a meaningful buy-the-dip move in Meta than a wholesale exit elsewhere.

For investors, the key things to watch are Meta's AI spending and monetization, Palantir's ability to keep beating elevated expectations, and whether Roblox can stabilize bookings and improve monetization .

Cathie Wood appears willing to lean into Meta while much of the market is focused on the cost of its AI ambitions.

news.Title: Micron, Sandisk gain as SK Hynix scraps Solidigm IPO, LYNX says
news.Content:
Investing.com -- SK Hynix's decision to scrap plans for a U.S. initial public offering of its Solidigm business could benefit Micron Technology and Sandisk by reducing the risk of additional NAND flash supply entering the market, according to LYNX Equity Strategies.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The analyst team led by KC Rajkumar said in an Oct. 23 note that a U.S. IPO would have provided Solidigm with capital to finance additional NAND manufacturing capacity in the United States. That expansion could have increased global supply in three or more years, potentially putting pressure on prices and competing suppliers.

With the IPO scrapped, that potential source of funding has disappeared, reducing the prospect of a capacity expansion that could have weighed on NAND prices. "The overhang of new capacity addition to the global supply of NAND flash has been eliminated," LYNX wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The proposed U.S. facility was expected to involve a joint venture between SK Hynix and Intel, potentially at Intel's Ohio campus. A U.S.-based operation would also have faced fewer trade restrictions than Solidigm's existing fabrication facility in China, according to LYNX, potentially allowing a faster expansion of production.

LYNX said the news would ordinarily represent a material positive for Micron and Sandisk, both NAND suppliers, as a lower risk of future capacity growth could support industry pricing and valuations. However, the team cautioned that the current market environment could limit any share-price gains despite the favorable supply implications.

Intel, meanwhile, could face a minor negative from the decision, as the abandoned plan removes a potential manufacturing project for its Ohio campus.

The broader implication for memory stocks is that the cancellation reduces a potential source of future competition, rather than immediately changing existing NAND supply. Any benefit to Micron and Sandisk will depend on how the industry's capacity plans and supply-demand balance evolve.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500 drop, Nasdaq rises after sharp tech sell-off
news.Content:
US stocks were mixed on Friday as worries over the AI trade lingered, following this week's steep sell-off in Tech ( XLK ) that triggered a flight to bonds.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1.1%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 0.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) inched 0.1% higher after semiconductors and Big Tech sold off on Thursday.

The 10-year Treasury (^ TNX ) yield held below the 5% threshold as investors flocked to bonds.

The AI trade attempted a rebound following concerns over rising financing costs and a potential slowdown in capex, which weighed on already-battered neocloud stocks like CoreWeave ( CRWV ). Shares of AI chip giants Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ) edged higher, along with other infrastructure plays, after Thursday's sell-off.

Shares of this week's earnings headliners, SpaceX ( SPCX ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Meta ( META ), stabilized in Friday trading after declining in the previous session.

Oil prices remained near a five-month high amid fears of escalating tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude ( BZ=F ) hovering near $112 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) climbing to $102 per barrel.

Apple is taking Wall Street's top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time

Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reports:

Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.

Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.

Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Shares of American Express ( AXP ) fell 3% Friday after the credit card giant delivered third quarter results and said it plans to eliminate roughly 5% of its workforce globally as part of a restructuring effort.

American Express CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts the cuts are part of a restructuring effort to make the company a "more agile and efficient organization." As part of the effort, the firm recognized a $336 million restructuring charge in the third quarter.

A company spokesperson told Yahoo Finance the reduction will eliminate 3,500 roles globally.

Squeri added that earlier this year he asked senior executives to find ways to cut corporate bloat across the company in order to refocus on American Express' biggest priorities.

Earlier this month, federal bank regulators fined the credit card giant $350 million over widespread failures in its anti-money laundering controls.

In the third quarter, American Express reported revenue climbed 9% to $14.5 billion from a year ago while adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $4.68. Analysts were expecting $14.8 billion in revenue.

news.Title: OpenAI Makes Stunning Financial Move Ahead of Potential IPO
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) backed OpenAI has reportedly lowered its valuation target to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion as some investors push back against the price of its latest funding round.

The AI company is now seeking up to $30 billion in fresh capital at the lower pre-money valuation, according to a report cited by TipRanks. Investors from the United Arab Emirates are expected to lead the round, while Coatue is also expected to participate.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with MSFT.

Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The change represents a $150 billion reduction from OpenAI's previously reported target, though the new figure remains well above the company's roughly $852 billion valuation in March 2026 .

The reason appears to be a more cautious funding environment.

TipRanks said investor demand has been weaker than in previous rounds as concerns grow around the enormous cost of building AI infrastructure and whether those investments will ultimately generate sufficient returns. Some investors may also be dealing with funding fatigue after pouring large sums into AI companies over the past several years.

That concern is showing up elsewhere in the market.

Meta Platforms recently came under pressure despite beating revenue estimates after increasing the lower end of its 2026 capital-spending outlook to $135 billion from $130 billion , while keeping the upper end at $145 billion.

OpenAI itself has told investors it expects to spend roughly $600 billion on computing by 2030 , highlighting just how capital-intensive its growth plans have become.

The company is also reportedly exploring additional computing capacity through a commercial arrangement with the UAE.

Investor Takeaway

I think the valuation cut matters less because OpenAI is suddenly worth dramatically less and more because it shows AI investors are becoming more price-sensitive .

A $1.25 trillion valuation is still enormous.

But the fact that OpenAI reportedly had to move down from $1.4 trillion suggests investors are no longer willing to fund AI growth at almost any price.

That is particularly important when the company could spend around $600 billion on compute through 2030.

For investors, the key things to watch are how much OpenAI ultimately raises, the final valuation, the terms of the round, compute spending and whether the company can show operating leverage before a potential 2027 IPO .

The AI funding boom is not disappearing.

But the cost of capital is starting to matter a lot more.

news.Title: Prediction: A $10,000 Investment in This Memory Stock Will Double by 2030 (Hint: It’s Not Micron or Sandisk)
news.Content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom has supercharged the memory market, leading to a phenomenal surge in the share prices of Micron Technology and Sandisk .

Memory demand has significantly outpaced supply, leading to a sharp increase in prices of both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash. Notably, the memory shortage may not end until 2030 despite attempts by manufacturers to bring more supply online. So, the favorable market conditions driving Micron and Sandisk's growth are here to stay.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, there is another memory industry participant that's benefiting from the market's boom. Shares of Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX), which sells chipmaking equipment, have jumped 64% over the past year. The company released its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (for the three months ending Sept. 27) on Oct. 21, and its performance clearly indicates that the incredible demand for memory from AI data centers could send the stock even higher.

Let's see why this semiconductor stock has room for more upside.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lam Research is winning big from the AI infrastructure build-out

Lam Research reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $8.22 billion, up nearly 55% from the year-ago period. What's more, the company's non-GAAP operating margin increased by 5.2 percentage points year over year to 40.2% last quarter. This explains why Lam's adjusted earnings per share jumped by almost 75% from the year-ago period to $2.20.

Wall Street was looking for $2.18 in earnings per share on revenue of $8.14 billion. Additionally, Lam's guidance for the current quarter suggests that its red-hot growth is here to stay. The company anticipates $8.6 billion in revenue and $2.33 in adjusted earnings per share in the current quarter at the midpoint of its guidance range.

The guidance implies a 52% year-over-year increase in revenue, and a stronger year-over-year jump of 84% in earnings per share. However, Lam stock fell more than 8% following its quarterly report, as the company's guidance was in line with Wall Street's expectations. Investors were probably expecting Lam's guidance to crush consensus estimates, and that wasn't the case.

I think that the slide is an opportunity for savvy investors to buy a top growth stock, considering that Lam is sitting on a massive growth opportunity that could fuel its growth until the end of the decade. After all, the company sells wafer and fabrication equipment (WFE), and the memory industry accounts for 46% of its revenue.

Story Continues

Industry association SEMI noted in July that global semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales will increase 23% in 2026 to $166 billion. Even better, the market's revenue could hit $201 billion in 2027 and $229.5 billion in 2028. Memory will play a central role in this market's expansion.

SEMI points out that DRAM equipment sales could increase by 39% in 2026, 27% next year, and 15% in 2028. Meanwhile, NAND flash equipment sales are on track to increase by 31% in 2026 and 2027, followed by a 14.5% increase in 2028. So, Lam's addressable market is on track to grow sizably by 2028.

However, I won't be surprised to see strong WFE spending beyond 2028. Bank of America estimates that WFE spending could hit $360 billion in 2030, more than double this year's projected spending. Not surprisingly, analysts have been increasing their revenue expectations for the next couple of fiscal years.

LRCX Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Here's why it is a good idea to invest $10,000 in this stock right now

If you have $10,000 in investable cash right now, and you're looking to diversify your portfolio, then buying this AI stock with that money could be a smart move. That's because Lam will not only help investors capitalize on the memory market's growth but also enable them to benefit from the broader semiconductor equipment industry's growth.

Lam's earnings per share could increase by 64% in the current fiscal year to $9.57, according to consensus estimates. The forecast for the next couple of years points to robust double-digit growth.

LRCX EPS Estimates for Next Fiscal Year data by YCharts

However, as the chart below shows, analysts are becoming bullish on the company's long-term earnings growth potential.

LRCX EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

Assuming Lam's bottom line jumps by even 20% in fiscal 2030, its earnings per share could reach $17.11 after four years (using fiscal 2029's projected EPS of $14.26 as the base). If Lam trades at 30 times earnings at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple, its stock price will reach $513. That implies a potential upside of 116%, meaning a $10,000 investment in this stock could be worth more than $21,600 after four years.

So, buying Lam Research stock following its post-earnings slide could be a profitable move, as the secular growth of the memory and semiconductor equipment markets will be a long-term tailwind for the company.

news.Title: Meta Plans What Amounts to a 2-for-1 Stock Split. Is the Stock a Buy?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) gave investors two things to absorb on Oct. 21. Its third-quarter revenue grew 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, above the top of management's guidance. And the social media giant plans to hand shareholders one new non-voting Class C share for every Class A and Class B share they hold, which it expects to act like a 2-for-1 stock split.

Earlier this month, I argued for buying the stock before the report, if revenue landed in the top half of the range management had guided for ($61 billion to $64 billion). It cleared the whole range.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Shares closed at around $698 that day, right before the results came out, which put them about 11% under their 52-week high of almost $780. Is Meta a buy now?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

More shares, same business

A split gives each shareholder more shares, but the total value of what they hold stays the same. Meta said it expects its Class A stock price to reflect a 2-for-1 split after the new shares are paid out as a dividend. And because the new shares have no votes, no one's voting power changes.

The charter change takes effect Jan. 19, 2027. Meta's board hasn't set the record and payment dates yet.

What's more interesting is why Meta wants a publicly traded share with no vote at all.

The company said the Class C stock can be used for raising money, paying employees, and making acquisitions, all while preserving the voting power of current Class A and Class B shareholders. It also said the setup helps keep founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg running the company.

"We don't have any specific financing plans to announce at this time," CFO Susan Li said on the third-quarter earnings call.

Spending is cutting into Meta's cash

Still, the timing makes sense. Meta's capital expenditures (including principal payments on finance leases) rose to $34.9 billion in the third quarter, up from $31.1 billion in the second quarter and $19.8 billion in the first. So, free cash flow (the cash left after these investments) swung to negative $2.1 billion. It was $784 million in the second quarter and $12.4 billion in the first.

Meta also didn't buy back any stock in the first nine months of 2026, after repurchasing $26.2 billion of shares over the same stretch of 2025. And it expects "to continue investing aggressively" next year.

Story Continues

A share Meta can sell without diluting anyone's vote gives it another way to pay for all this. Of course, if it ever does sell Class C shares to raise money, current shareholders would own a smaller part of the business.

Advertisers are paying more

Showing how much advertisers value Meta's ads, the average price per ad climbed 14% year over year in the third quarter -- a pickup from 12% growth in both previous quarters and 6% in the fourth quarter of 2025. Ad impressions grew 10%, down from 19% in the first quarter and 14% in the second. Total revenue growth cooled from 28% in the second quarter to 26%, a far smaller fall than the five-point drop a quarter earlier. Meta expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, or growth of about 22% to 27% from $59.9 billion a year ago.

Put another way, Meta's ad volume is growing slower, but each ad is fetching a higher price. That suggests advertisers are getting results worth paying for. It's also the trend I wanted to see most in this report.

But profits didn't keep up. Operating income dropped 37% to $13 billion because of a $9.9 billion legal charge linked to an agreement with state attorneys general. Without the charge, operating income climbed 11% to $22.9 billion, far behind revenue growth.

The price still looks fair

At around $698, Meta shares trade at about 21 times 2027 earnings estimates. Meta's premium over the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), which trades at about 19 times forward earnings, looks small for a company growing revenue at more than 25%.

Next year's spending plan still isn't known, and Meta might one day sell a meaningful amount of Class C stock. Either could weigh on the shares.

But I still think Meta stock is a buy, and the split has little to do with it. Advertisers keep paying more for each ad even while Meta pumps money into its AI build-out, and the shares cost just a bit more than the market's average. I'd be comfortable buying shares at today's price.

news.Title: Gemini Latest Stock Portfolio: Top 4 Stock Picks
news.Content:
In just two to three years, the debate around AI and stock picking has shifted drastically. Not long ago, many said there was no point in letting AI chatbots pick stocks, and that you could only use them for research. Today, many firms and companies are handing portfolios over to AI agents amid a fast rise in AI learning and context memory. We have followed that shift through the AI portfolios that Claude, ChatGPT and others run with real money. See Claude's best-performing picks here.

Retail Investors Are Handing Over Control

Wall Street is moving fast. Brokerages including Robinhood and Webull now let customers connect their portfolios to AI agents such as Claude and Codex, which can then buy and sell on their own, The Wall Street Journal reported in September. Moomoo, an online brokerage and trading platform, made agentic trading available in April, and its U.S. chief executive estimates that about 20% of its trading volume could come from agents by the end of the year, the Journal reported.

The Journal gave several examples of everyday investors who are already doing this. It mentioned an investor who runs a team of Claude agents which scan the market for stocks and ETFs, check open positions before the close and write a weekly performance report. The investor reportedly said the agents are beating most of the accounts he runs himself.

Claude runs its own portfolio in the Rallies arena too, and it has put 14.5% of it into a data center contractor. See why Claude made that bet here.

Researchers see risks too. A National Bureau of Economic Research working paper found that AI models asked to build an investment strategy picked concentrated portfolios, high-valuation stocks and the companies with the most media coverage, and did not beat passive benchmarks, the Journal reported. Irene Aldridge, a former quant trader who studies AI in markets, told the Journal that investors do this at their own risk and that many agents using the same data could crowd into the same trades and add volatility.

Photo by Adam Nowakowski on Unsplash

Gemini Is Beating the S&P 500

That is the backdrop for Gemini's run in the Rallies AI Arena. Rallies is an AI investing app that gives several leading AI models money to trade stocks. Models like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok each manage a $100,000 portfolio. Rallies told them to beat the S&P 500. Rallies Arena said on X on Oct. 20 that Gemini is up 26% since the contest began in late November, compared with a 13.9% return for the S&P 500 over the same period. ChatGPT is also ahead, with its portfolio up 75.6% since March, according to Rallies Arena. Check ChatGPT's latest 10 picks here.

Story Continues

Methodology

We ranked the 4 stocks in Gemini's portfolio in ascending order based on the number of hedge fund investors at the end of the second quarter of 2026. The data comes from Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds. The performance figure for each stock shows its gain or loss since Gemini bought it, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 22. Today's price is the closing price on Oct. 22.

#4 Intuitive Surgical, Inc. (NASDAQ:ISRG)

Number of Hedge Fund Investors: 100

Stock Price When Gemini Bought: $433.22

Today's Price: $443.85

Intuitive Surgical is up 2.2% since Gemini bought it, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 22. It makes up 11.7% of the portfolio. Intuitive Surgical makes the da Vinci robotic systems that surgeons use for minimally invasive procedures. The company reported third-quarter results on Oct. 20 that beat estimates for revenue and adjusted earnings per share, and it narrowed its full-year procedure growth forecast to 14% to 15%. Investors focused on margin pressure, a litigation settlement and planned price cuts on instruments. The stock rose 3.7% on Oct. 22. Jim Cramer has told viewers to buy Intuitive Surgical every time the stock sells off. See what else Cramer said here.

Bulls say Intuitive Surgical's strength sits in the robots already installed in hospitals. In the recently reported quarter, instrument and accessory revenue rose 18% and service revenue rose 22%. The company is planning price cuts. Bulls think the planned price cuts will widen its customer base. The cuts focus on common, high-volume procedures such as hernia repair, where cost keeps many hospitals from using a robot, and about 1 million hernia repairs happen in the U.S. each year. After early pricing programs, customers in Germany, the U.K., India and Japan expanded their use beyond urology and cancer surgery. Management said wider use is worth more than the revenue lost on each procedure, and the payoff should build over time, with little effect in 2027.

#3 ServiceNow, Inc. (NYSE:NOW)

Number of Hedge Fund Investors: 115

Stock Price When Gemini Bought: $93.24

Today's Price: $157.00

ServiceNow is up 68.7% since Gemini bought it, the best result in the portfolio, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 22. It makes up 9.4% of the portfolio. ServiceNow sells cloud software that helps companies automate IT, HR and customer service work. The stock gained 10% in the month through Oct. 20, and ten firms raised their price targets ahead of third-quarter results on Oct. 28. The stock also dropped 4.4% in one day this month when enterprise software sold off on worries about AI financing.

Back in July, the stock was down about 28% this year on fears that AI would hurt software, and some value investors called that a buying setup. Read what the bulls argued here.

ServiceNow is down about 16% over the past year amid fears that AI will make software companies obsolete, but the company is changing and bulls are hopeful. The new model is how ServiceNow charges customers. For years it charged a fee for each employee seat, so its revenue grew only as customers added more people to the software. Now it also charges for "assists," each one a unit of work its AI completes. Bulls like this because revenue grows with how much customers use the AI, and a single AI agent can do the work of many people. If AI means fewer people use the software, the old seat model would have cut ServiceNow's revenue. The assist model pays ServiceNow more as AI takes on more work.

#2 Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL)

Number of Hedge Fund Investors: 275

Stock Price When Gemini Bought: $342.04

Today's Price: $324.22

Alphabet is down 5.1% since Gemini bought it, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 22. Gemini put only 0.6% of the portfolio into the stock, even though Alphabet is the company that makes Gemini. The shares fell 3.15% on Oct. 22 as AI stocks sold off, and Alphabet reports third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28. Claude's AI portfolio named Alphabet its best performer this year. Find out what drove the gain here.

Under the splashy headlines about new models like Gemini 4 Argon and cloud growth, the market is missing something. Alphabet's bread and butter is Search, and nobody has a clear answer for what happens as people stop clicking links. A SparkToro study found that 68% of US Google searches in the first four months of 2026 ended without a click. A randomized experiment published in April found that when an AI Overview shows, clicks to outside websites fall about 40%.

Bulls say Alphabet can diversify, and the numbers so far support them. Google Cloud revenue rose 82% in the second quarter, and its operating margin went to 36.5% from 17.8% a year earlier. Alphabet now sells its own AI chips, called TPUs, straight to customers' data centers, and Waymo is giving about 500,000 paid rides a week. Search has held up too. Search revenue rose 17% in the second quarter, and clicks on paid results stayed flat in the same experiment that measured the drop in free clicks.

#1 NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)

Number of Hedge Fund Investors: 285

Stock Price When Gemini Bought: $183.28

Today's Price: $212.21

NVIDIA is up 16.2% since Gemini bought it, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 22. It makes up 14.6% of the portfolio. The stock fell 4.4% on Oct. 22 as investors worried about power-grid limits and chip supply constraints. NVIDIA reports earnings on Nov. 17. The stock has slipped after a rough two weeks for AI stocks, and two billionaires still like it. See who they are here.

Bulls say NVIDIA's lead now reaches well beyond its chips. The company sells the networking gear, the processors and the software that run AI data centers. It now lets other companies' custom chips plug into its systems, so a customer that builds its own chip can still end up buying from NVIDIA. NVIDIA also bought Hugging Face, a popular home for open AI models, which puts its software in front of millions of developers.

Bears worry that NVIDIA's growth depends on customers who borrow heavily to buy its chips. Newer AI cloud companies such as CoreWeave are paying more to borrow, and NVIDIA is in talks with large insurers to back those chip loans. If the insurers say no, chip spending could slow.

The fund outperformed the Russell 1000 Growth Index in the third quarter of 2026, as investors began distinguishing between businesses vulnerable to artificial intelligence disruption and those positioned to benefit from AI adoption. The Portfolio returned 4.46% net of fees, outperforming the Index's 0.92% gain by 3.54 percentage points. However, its year-to-date net return remained negative at 8.11%, compared with a 6.30% gain for the benchmark. Strong relative contributions from software and services holdings helped offset weakness among semiconductor and other direct AI-capital-expenditure beneficiaries, which faced valuation pressure as investors reconsidered spending levels, financing, and future returns on infrastructure investment. The managers continued rebalancing the Portfolio toward businesses with attractive long-term growth prospects, stronger current momentum, and more visible demand, initiating positions in selected semiconductor equipment, power infrastructure, payments, and data-storage companies while trimming or exiting other holdings. The Portfolio also added to selected infrastructure and technology investments and maintained exposure to established software, services, internet, and information-based businesses. Looking ahead, Polen aims to maintain a balanced portfolio of competitively advantaged companies that can withstand shifts in market leadership. The managers remain constructive but cautious about persistent inflation, higher interest rates, energy costs, and valuations, particularly for businesses whose earnings potential lies further in the future. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500 slip, Nasdaq stabilizes after sharp tech sell-off
news.Content:
US stocks were mixed on Friday as worries over the AI trade lingered, following this week's steep sell-off in Tech ( XLK ) that triggered a flight to bonds.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1.1%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 0.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) edged 0.3% higher after semiconductors and Big Tech sold off on Thursday.

The 10-year Treasury (^ TNX ) yield held below the 5% threshold as investors flocked to bonds.

The AI trade sank on Thursday as concerns over rising financing costs and a potential slowdown in capex weighed on already-battered neocloud stocks like CoreWeave ( CRWV ). AI chip giants Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( SPCX ) also retreated, along with other infrastructure plays.

Shares of this week's earnings headliners, SpaceX ( SPCX ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Meta ( META ), stabilized in Friday trading after declining in the previous session.

Oil prices remained near a five-month high amid fears of escalating tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude ( BZ=F ) hovering near $111 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) climbing to $102 per barrel.

LIVE 7 updates

9 mins ago David Hollerith

American Express shares fall after credit card giant announces workforce reduction

Shares of American Express ( AXP ) fell 3% Friday after the credit card giant delivered third quarter results and said it plans to eliminate roughly 5% of its workforce globally as part of a restructuring effort.

American Express CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts the cuts are part of a restructuring effort to make the company a "more agile and efficient organization." As part of the effort, the firm recognized a $336 million restructuring charge in the third quarter.

A company spokeswoman told Yahoo Finance the reduction will eliminate 3,500 roles globally.

Squeri added that earlier this year he asked senior executives to find ways to cut corporate bloat across the company in order to refocus on American Express' biggest priorities.

Earlier this month, federal bank regulators fined the credit card giant $350 million over widespread failures in its anti-money laundering controls.

In the third quarter, American Express reported revenue climbed 9% to $14.5 billion from a year ago while adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $4.68. Analysts were expecting $14.8 billion in revenue.

11 mins ago

Meta stock pares losses following yesterday's 7% decline

Yahoo Finance's Daniel Howley reports:

Meta ( META ) stock pared losses in premarket action Friday, following a dismal Thursday trading session. Shares of the social media giant plunged 7%, despite reporting better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue on Wednesday as AI bubble fears reemerged across Wall Street.

Investors have been pulling back on semiconductor and other AI stocks across the board on questions about whether massive investments in AI data centers will pay off in the long run.

Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimates to between $135 billion and $145 billion from $130 billion and $145 billion. The company also has $825 billion in various spending commitments related to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products.

Read More:

Today at 1:34 PM UTC

Stocks open lower as investors search for stability in tech

US stocks opened lower as investors reassessed technology stocks following the Nasdaq Composite's worst day since June.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1%, while those for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) decreased 0.3% after semiconductors and Big Tech sold off on Thursday.

At Friday's open, major indices are on pace for a clear split in weekly performance after all three traded lower on Thursday.

The Nasdaq is on pace for its second consecutive week of losses, while the Dow is poised for its third straight week of gains. The S&P 500 is hovering near the flatline for the week.

Meanwhile, oil prices rose early Friday as momentum builds around renewed tensions in the Middle East conflict.

Today at 12:46 PM UTC Ines Ferré

SpaceX may not follow Meta's bold plan to raise money for AI

Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports:

Don't expect SpaceX ( SPCX ) to surprise investors like Meta ( META ) did this week by announcing it would issue a new class of nonvoting stock to help fund its AI build-out.

"Importantly, in our discussion w/management, SPCX also said that it is not considering raising equity," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth wrote in a new post-earnings note on Friday. "Capital requirements are front and center across the market, and SPCX indicated it has a number of available pools of capital on the debt side."

SpaceX gave investors a taste of what could be to come on the debt funding front in its earnings report this week.

Today at 11:26 AM UTC Ines Ferré

SpaceX could be on the cusp of buying 80,000 cell towers in a bid to really challenge Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile

Yahoo Finance' Brian Sozzi reports:

Elon Musk's SpaceX ( SPCX ) may be close to sending another message to the telecom giants: we are seriously coming for you.

The company is eyeing the purchase of 80,000 cell sites across the US, Bloomberg reported on Friday. SpaceX is reportedly in talks with two of the companies, Crown Castle and American Tower, among the largest owners of cellular towers.

"Committing ~$30 billion into spectrum is serious enough. Committing to 80K macro sites could be a point of no return," Bernstein analyst Laurent Yoon said. "That is a meaningful number, broadly consistent with the scale required for a nationwide terrestrial wireless network. Whether SpaceX ultimately leases anything close to that figure remains uncertain, but the reported scope suggests a far greater level of commitment than spectrum accumulation alone."

Shares of AT&T ( T ), Verizon ( VZ ), and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) traded sharply lower in pre-market trading.

Today at 10:20 AM UTC Ines Ferré

Investors' flight to bonds sends Fed rate hike bets tumbling

The tech sell-off on Thursday sent investors rushing into bonds, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) to its biggest one-day drop in more than two years and back below 5%.

Behind the move was a shift in rate expectations as longer-term yields fell. With the Federal Reserve set to meet next week, on Oct. 28, investors had been bracing for a rate hike to combat fears of oil-driven inflation.

But those bets faded quickly with the Fed funds futures market putting the odds of an October hike at about 5%, according to Bloomberg data, down from 15% earlier this week, and 37% at the end of September.

Today at 9:31 AM UTC Ines Ferré

This level-headed Tesla bull still expects something huge from the Cybercab

Tesla's ( TSLA ) surprise $5 billion haircut to its capital expenditure plans in its latest earnings call hasn't shaken investor confidence in the long-term potential of a large Cybercab network.

Maybe some near-term confidence was lost in the Optimus humanoid as Tesla deals with design challenges, but not in Cybercabs.

Case in point: Even the reasonable modeling assumptions on the Cybercab from Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco, who has an Equal Weight rating on the stock, still have the fleet size hitting 5 million by the end of 2040.
