news.Title: Q3 Earnings Season: Strong Base, Higher Revision Trends, and Promising 2027 Outlook
news.Content:
We have a third of S&P 500 members on deck to report Q3 results this week, including three Mag 7 members – Alphabet GOOGL and Microsoft MSFT on Wednesday and Amazon AMZN on Thursday. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from more than 50% of S&P 500 members.

With results from about a quarter of S&P 500 members already out, we see a continuation of the broad-based strength we've seen in the last few reporting cycles. While the growth pace remains strong, it does not compare favorably with other recent periods, particularly when some of the outlier numbers are excluded. Most importantly, the revisions trend remains positive, with estimates for 2026 Q4 and full-year 2027 continuing to rise.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 121 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +26.2% from the same period last year on +12.2% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector continues to be a major growth contributor, but the momentum is broad-based, with 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track to enjoy positive earnings growth and 6 generating double-digit earnings growth in Q3.

The quarterly chart below details actual results alongside Q3 2026 growth expectations and forward projections.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates, as the chart below shows.

This positive revision behavior is not new; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the favorable estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Industrials, Basic Materials, Finance, Aerospace and Conglomerates alongside Tech and Energy since the start of October.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates have come down since the start of October for 9 sectors, with the major declines at the Transportation, Autos, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Construction, and Utilities sectors.

Story Continues

It is important to note that estimates for full-year 2027 have also been similarly trending higher, which we show a little later in this note.

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

This week's reporting line-up, comprising 172 S&P 500 members, is a representative sample of the index as a whole, ranging from the aforementioned Mag 7 members to Coca-Cola, Boeing, Caterpillar, Visa, Eli Lilly, and a host of Finance and other companies.

The 6 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit earnings growth in Q3 are Aerospace (up +186.7%), Energy (+128%), Tech (+45.3%), Basic Materials (+32.6%), Transportation (+11.1%), and Industrial Products (+14.4%).

Q3 earnings growth for the S&P 500 index drops to +21.6% from +26.2% once the Energy sector's contribution is excluded from the index. Excluding the Tech sector, Q3 earnings growth for the rest of the index drops to +16.1%.

For the Mag 7 group, we already have actual results from Meta META and Tesla TSLA, and this week will bring results from Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft. The expectation is that Q3 earnings for the Mag 7 will increase by +22.3% on +23.1% revenues, as the chart below shows.

Excluding the Mag 7 group's contribution, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would actually improve to +27.6% (from +26.2%).

The chart below shows quarterly earnings and revenue growth expectations for the Tech sector as a whole.

The Q3 earnings and revenue growth rate drops to +23.1% from +45.3% once the substantial contributions from Nvidia NVDA, Micron MU, and Alphabet GOOGL are excluded, as the chart below shows.

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, October 23rd, we have seen Q3 results from 121 S&P 500 members, or 24.2% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +31.5% from the same period last year on +12.2% higher revenues, with 80.7% beating EPS estimates and 69.7% beating revenues estimates.

The comparison charts below show the earnings and revenue growth rates for these companies compared to other recent periods.

The very strong earnings and revenue growth pace for this group of 45 S&P 500 members is mostly due to Micron, whose Q3 earnings increased +1075.7% from the year-earlier level. Excluding the Micron contribution, Q3 earnings for the remaining 120 index members that have reported would be up +14%.

The chart below shows the Q3 earnings growth pace for the companies that have reported, with and without Micron, across recent periods.

The comparison charts below show the Q3 EPS and revenue beat percentages for these companies compared to other recent periods.

For the Finance sector, we now have Q3 results from 55.3% of the sector's market capitalization in the S&P 500 index. Total earnings for these Finance sector companies are up +10% from the same period last year on +8.7% higher revenues, with 80.6% beating EPS estimates and 52.8% beating revenue estimates.

The comparison charts below put the Q3 earnings and revenue growth rates in a historical context.

The comparison charts below show the Q3 EPS and revenue beat percentages in a historical context.

As you can see above, not only are the growth rates tracking below other recent periods, but Finance sector companies also seem to be struggling to beat consensus EPS and revenue estimates.

The Earnings Big Picture

The chart below shows the aggregate growth picture for the S&P 500 index on a calendar year basis.

As we noted earlier, estimates for full-year 2027 are experiencing the same positive and broad-based revisions trend that we noted earlier in the context of 2026 Q4. The chart below shows how aggregate 2027 earnings expectations have evolved since the start of July.

For a detailed view of the evolving earnings picture, please check out our weekly Earnings Trends report here >>>> Q3 Earnings Season Ramps Up, Outlook for Q4 and Full-Year 2027 Improves

news.Title: Facing Investing Fears
news.Content:
In this podcast, Motley Fool contributors Jon Quast, Matt Frankel, and Rachel Warren discuss:

Risks from S-1 filings for Amazon , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms .

Anthropic's unusual risk factor section.

What's driving the Fear and Greed Index lower.

Three stocks that have dropped that are worth buying.

When higher bond yields can help investors.

To catch full episodes of all The Motley Fool's free podcasts, check out our podcast center . When you're ready to invest, check out this top 10 list of stocks to buy .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

A full transcript is below.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

This podcast was recorded on Oct. 5, 2026.

Jon Quast: Facing our fears with the stock market, Motley Fool Hidden Gems investing starts now. Welcome to Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing. I'm your host today, Jon Quast. I am joined by Rachel Warren and Matt Frankel. We're kicking off this spooky October with an episode filled with investor fears. We're going to be talking about bond yields and stocks that are plummeting. But first, we want to talk about risk factors. Every publicly traded company does include risk factors in their filings, and that includes the S1 filing. This is a filing that companies release right before they go public on the stock market, and we got one from Anthropic that was a little bit over the top as far as the risk goes normally. We don't have the full document, but the leaked version that is out there says that its technology poses a catastrophic or existential risk to humanity, potentially. That's quite a doomsday scenario. That actually gave us a question from our mailbag that was worth considering here at the top. This comes from a listener named Patrick. Given the recent S1 filing from Anthropic and how it paints a rather bleak picture of the risks for AI, I was wondering if we could have a little fun and dig into a few S1s from 10, 15 or 20 years ago. Maybe you look at the S1s from Google , Amazon , or even MongoDB to see if they've been able to execute or come up against the risks that they've outlined and how they've navigated it. We're going to bit on this. We're going to take a stroll down memory lane with some old S1s. We're going to not talk about MongoDB today, but let's talk about S1 risks from Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta . If you invested in any of these at IPO, you're doing quite well today. Matt, kick us off here with Amazon and its S1 risks.

Story Continues

Matt Frankel: Amazon's a great example of one that did list some scary risk factors. The question said 10, 15 or 20 years. Really aging myself because I remember Amazon's S1, and it was 30 years ago, almost 30 years ago. It happened in '96 or '97, I think '97. But it warned of better funded rivals specifically named Barnes and Noble and Borders. It also listed capacity constraints, system failure as risk factors, but solving those problems created what would eventually become AWS. They're perhaps the best example of how a company navigated some "scary risk factors" and really used it to their advantage.

Jon Quast: It's almost hilarious to consider Barnes and Noble as an existential threat to Amazon now in hindsight. But indeed, at the time, it was a little bit like, how is Amazon going to come up against this huge and powerful company Barnes and Nobles? It was able to do it. It's similar Rachel with Google and Microsoft . Microsoft having that distribution and Google saying, hey, maybe they're going to be able to prevent us from growing in Search.

Rachel Warren: It is funny to think about now when we look at how much these companies have grown to the giants they are today. But the sort of often boring section of the S1, not so much an Anthropics case, the risk factor section, I can obviously as an investor, tell you a lot about the business, help you really form your own risk thesis and by assessment of a particular company. Now, there's a key point to be made here. There's obviously a fundamental difference between Alphabet warning 20 plus years ago that Microsoft might crash a search engine and Anthropics warning in it's filing that an autonomous AI model could pose an actual "existential risk to humanity." But the key takeaway here is back in the day, Alphabet or Google's core risk was structural. They were a single revenue engine at the time, at the mercy of desktop operating systems controlled by their rivals. A lot of the concern at that point was this idea that Yahoo, Microsoft could destroy Google, of course, that in fact, was anything but the case. I do think what we see in the at least leaked version of Anthropics S1 filing, it is a different story, but you can certainly look back in time at a lot of fear mongering around past S1s that never in fact came to fruition.

Jon Quast: I can remember a time when I didn't see how Google was going to displace Ask Jeeves, and I've certainly been proven wrong there. Matt closes out here with Meta. Of course, it wasn't called Meta when it went public, it was called Facebook back then.

Matt Frankel: Jon, I think you and I are the ones old enough to have actually used Ask Jeeves. I used Web Crawler and Licos as well, if you remember either of those. But yeah, Meta is another example. It was known as just Facebook at the time of its S1. The biggest concern from investors and from the company itself was being able to monetize Mobile. At the time, smartphones were still relatively new. Facebook's S1, don't quote me specifically on this. I think it was 2011. But at the time, the iPhone had only been out for a few years. Smartphones weren't what they were today. At the time, Facebook generated virtually all of its revenue from desktop ads. It's S1 specifically disclosed that it had no meaningful revenue from Mobile, and there was no clear strategy or pathway to changing that at the time. On a small screen, for example, there's really no room for a desktop style ad like they were using for the most part at the time. But by 2019, not even today. By 2019, Mobile made up 94% of Meta's ad revenue, and it fixed the problem in a few ways. I mean, number one, the most obvious one, Meta put ads in the newsfeed and directly in the news feed, not just sidebar ads, so they looked like posts. I remember being really annoyed at that at first, but it was a genius business strategy. They got far more attention in late 2012, shortly after it went public, Meta launched ads that let developers pay people to download their apps. Really great way to track what advertisers were getting for their money. Demand for that, handily exceeded expectations. The results came pretty quickly. This is from Tech Crunch. I found an article in 2014 that put Mobile at more than 50% of ad revenue by the end of 2013, and that was only about a year and a half after the IPO, so with Amazon and Meta, the key theme here is turning your worst business threats into your growth opportunities, and that's a rare quality that you can look for. I don't know, with Anthropic, I don't know how you turn an existential threat to humanity into a growth opportunity. I don't know. Maybe they could figure out ways to help regulate the industry, keep it safe and grow that way.

Jon Quast: What this reminds me of, I believe it's author Morgan Housel, who says, Everything worth doing in life has less than a 100% chance of success. There are risks in any business, but as we're pointing out these great investment opportunities, you have to be able to see through these clouds, as Motley Fool co-founder David Gardner puts it, "Clouds you can see through." There are clouds, but you got to see the sunshine on the other side. But of course, it's not all sunshine and roses, Rachel. There are real things to consider. We shouldn't be dismissive of the S1 risk factor sections.

Rachel Warren: No, quite the opposite, in fact. I mean, if anything, an S1, I mean, it's a great tool as an individual investor. It highlights vulnerabilities, often at a company's weakest point, often before they've built a protective moat. Of course, in Google's case, they navigated commercial threats by aggressively at the time, developing Chrome and Android to control its own destiny. Come quite a long way since then. That moat specifically within the AI space for the frontier labs, for Anthropic specifically, is still actively developing as is the regulatory landscape. That creates, I would say, an element of uncertainty that is a little bit differentiated here.

Matt Frankel: Of course, there are some that don't overcome their risk. It's really important to mention that. We're not saying that every risk is an opportunity. Think of WeWork, for example, if you remember that company, it's S1, which was originally filed in 2019, showed $47 billion in lease liabilities, which were backed by nothing but short term memberships. They called it out as a risk factor, and it turned out to be a little too much of a risk factor.

Jon Quast: I want to close out here talking about anthropic. We certainly don't want to be dismissive of its risk section either. Rachel, you had some interesting observations about the risk factor that we know of. Obviously, we don't have the full complete filing yet that is publicly available, but what we know so far.

Rachel Warren: There was a lot to go over there, but the thing that was very noticeable was Anthropic spent about 80 pages strictly on risk factors compared to just around 48 pages explaining its actual business operations, essentially dedicating nearly twice as much S1 real estate to explaining how the world might end as to how they're planning to justify a targeted $2 trillion valuation. Anthropics also introducing a somewhat unusual founder LLC model, essentially, where the seven co-founders will be pooling class F shares to lock down 50.1% of the total voting power, so it's effectively asking the markets for a historical amount of capital while insulating leaders from a lot of the market forces there. Still a lot to come out. Obviously, we have to see what the actual S1 looks like, but I think that there are a lot of very justifiable questions that investors have and will continue to as we move forward.

Jon Quast: Well, we'll certainly keep an eye on it when it finally does release to the public. After the break, we're going to be talking about fear and greed. You're listening to Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing.

Welcome back to Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing. There's a thing out there called the Fear in Greed Index from CNN and what is so interesting is that as we've kicked off October, this is the third trading day and it's the third straight day that it is marking fear in the stock market. Now, this index tracks a variety of factors, which is interesting in how it ascertains that investors are fearful. One of the things that it's looking at, for example, is the options. Are they bullish, bearish, et cetera, are they more bearish now than bullish? That's an interesting data point. But the two weakest factors right now in the index are the stock price strength and stock price breadth. Basically, there are more stocks making new lows than stocks making new highs. Which is counterintuitive with the market at an all time high or near an all time high. But that's actually what's happening. We're also seeing a concentration in volume among stocks that are going down more than stocks that are going up. What that tells us is there's actually a decent amount of pessimism in the market with a lot of the optimism concentrated in just a few names. I thought this would be a good chance to talk about some stocks that are actually making some new lows here. Warren Buffett talks about buying when others are fearful. Others are fearful, stocks are hitting some lows. What are some stocks guys that you would be buying and Matt we're going to let you go first here.

Matt Frankel: First of all, fear alone isn't a reason to buy. It's also important to really put into perspective whether a stock price fell just because of market sentiment or because there's something wrong with the business. I'll call out one that I'm not necessarily suggesting run out and buy. That's a homebuilder I own called Dream Finders Homes . I bought more in full disclosure, but it's not just down because of fear in the market. It's down because its earnings per share have been more than halved over the past year. It's because margins are under pressure and it's because the housing market is generally terrible right now. I could probably think of a worse word to describe the housing market. I bought more but that's a stock that's cheap for a very rational reason. Another one, on the other hand, think of a company like Brookfield Corporation . Ticker symbol BN. The giant asset manager, it's down 20% over the past year, just reached a new 52 week low. It's distributable earnings, which are not GAAP earnings. This is like their form of adjusted earnings was up 15% year over year in the latest quarter. Its fee bearing capital grew by 19% year over year, which is a great indicator of future revenue, and it's raising money at a faster pace than ever. This is a case where the business continues to grow, but the stocks price is down because of fear in the market. There are some real risks with Brookfield, don't get me wrong, but the company at 15 times earnings, that creates pretty impressive risk reward dynamics.

Jon Quast: Certainly a name that not everyone in our listening audience maybe have heard of they love ideas. We like to give ideas. Rachel, we'll pass it to you here. What's another idea that you have?

Rachel Warren: I think Shopify is a great example of a business that has been sold off a bit, particularly early this year. The stocks down still about 8% from a year ago. Certainly, the business went through quite a lot of volatility share price wise earlier in the year. The stock bottomed out under $100 a share. Now it's trading around a $150 a share. I'm a long term holder of Shopify, and I think a lot of this has been around the concerns of how commerce and agentic commerce is going to disrupt the ecommerce space broadly, and of course, Shopify, with its platform that helps merchants around the world is the epitome of, I think that fear that we're seeing. But again the point that Matt makes, looking for businesses where the growth story is still there, this is not about buying a business because the share price has dipped or the valuation looks low compared to a year ago. Obviously, that can be a favorable thing as a long term investor. You want to make sure, are the cash flows there? Is the profitability there? Is the growth story still holding, I think that's very much the case in the case of Shopify. I mean, they're really doing an exceptional job of continuing to monetize agentic commerce, building that into their platform. They're seeing tremendous growth with shop pay, and again, a lot of those AI innovations are actually driving their profitability and cash flow. I think that's a great example of a business that the market's been a little hard on, but in my view, the business thesis still holds.

Jon Quast: Maybe a nice, hidden aspect of Shopify that people haven't considered, just how AI really does help these smaller shops as opposed to large marketplace aggregators. Matt, close us out here with another little bit off the beaten path stock to talk about, but this is an interesting one.

Matt Frankel: I love the Shopify call, by the way. That's one that I bought when I was being greedy when everyone was fearful of the 2022 bear market, and it's paid off very, very well. But another one I was going to talk about is a real estate investment trust called Realty Income. Ticker symbol is just O. It's the largest real estate stock I have. It reached a 52 week low recently, primarily because it's so sensitive to interest rates. Real estate stocks in particular are very sensitive. They rely on borrowed money more than most companies, so borrowing costs are higher. The value of commercial properties is really derived by comparing the expected return to the risk free rate, which I don't want to turn this into economics 101, but the bottom line is that real estate stocks are very, very interest rate sensitive. Their business is doing great. They own about a little under 16,000 properties now, mostly freestanding retail, that's recession resistant, they have some data center properties, they have a joint venture with digital realty trust that's new, they have a few other property types, industrials are a focus of theirs. It could be a great time with some of these as to lock in a great yield on cost, meaning the yield on what you're paying for shares. These are great long term investments. I'm in my 40s, and this is a big component of my retirement strategy, and right now, realty income is paying over 6%, which is historically rare for the stock. It could be a good time to take a look at some of these real estate investment trusts.

Jon Quast: Well, thanks for those ideas. After the break, we're going to look at some bond yields and what it means for investors, you're listening to Motley Fool Hidden Gems Investing.

Welcome back to Motley Fool, Hidden Gems Investing. You know, we did take a question from our mailbag at the top, but I want to put in a plug. If you have a question for anyone on our show, you can send those in at podcast@fool.com. We would love to take it if it's a Foolish question, if it's short enough to read, and you remember that we don't give personalized investing advice, but that email is podcast@fool.com, podcast@fool.com. Now, we want to close off here with a topic that Matt brought to the table regarding bond yields, and bond yields, especially sovereign bond yields are surging. I saw in the news this morning that Japan's bonds are hitting an all time high yield, but in the US, they're hitting high yields as well. This is typically seen as a not good thing for the economy, but we want to flip this around on its head, and we want to talk about maybe where the benefit lies for some companies. Rachel, we're going to go with you first.

Rachel Warren: Yeah, I want to talk a little bit about all sides of this. When you hear that the ten year treasury yield is hitting its highest level since 2002, so 20 plus years, that means the underlying price of government bonds is falling. Yields and bond prices, they move in opposite directions. That means investors are aggressively selling off bonds for a few reasons. Now, we're still seeing a lot of resilience in the economy and the labor market that actually pushes out expectations in some cases for rate cuts, and obviously, we've seen that to be the case recently. Now, obviously, persistent inflation triggers, like oil prices due to the continued geopolitical friction in the Middle East are also keeping a lot of inflation fears alive. There's also a supply and demand imbalance. The US national debt is approaching about $40 trillion. We've got a federal budget deficit at around 6% of GDP. The government is flooding the market with a historic supply of new treasury bonds, and at the same time, big tech companies are issuing massive amounts of private corporate debt to fund the AI Data Center. There's a lot of debt entering the market. That means that buyers can demand a much higher return. That is what is forcing yields to multi decade peaks. Now, as a consumer, obviously, if the ten year treasury is spiking in this way, that's a benchmark for consumer and corporate borrowing costs. That has an impact. It can have a drag on the everyday economy. It pushes US mortgage rates up. It also pinches the federal budget. Now on the flip side of that, there are, of course, many businesses that are cash rich corporate compounders where higher yields are actually a competitive edge, if you will. The smaller companies might struggle with the high interest rates, but very cash rich businesses that are actually parking their capital cushions directly into treasuries are thriving. That is the case across a lot of industries. I'll name a couple in an industry I follow very closely, which is healthcare. You think of companies like Eli Lilly, companies like Regeneron. These are very heavily invested in treasuries. These are also very cash rich, and they will over the long run, probably benefit from what we're seeing right now.

Matt Frankel: I mean, Rachel did a really good job of covering the causes and the negatives. I love how I brought this, and Rachel got stuck with the boring economics 101 of bonds here. The ten years at 5.2 right before you were recording the 30 years around 5.5%. That's the highest in more than two decades, and there are some serious concerns, not just for the stock market, but right now, the US pays over $1 trillion in annual interest on its debt, and rising rates make this worse. Of course, this is bad for many industries. Don't think this is a good thing for your portfolio. Home Builders, I already mentioned one, real estate Investment Trust, any growth stocks with really long runways to profitability. I'm not talking about the Nvidia s that are making money hand over fist, but some of these NewYork Cloud companies that are losing money and things like that could be under pressure. The fact that there is a 5.5% yielding risk free alternative for investors, it just creates general downward pressure on the market. But there are some good things to mention here. I mean, for one thing, yields driven by strong growth, which is what this is. It's a lot of the AI investment and bonds related to that, that are driving rates up. Some areas of the market can win. Rachel correctly mentioned cash rich businesses. Hers were healthcare. But I would actually add to that by pivoting to the insurance companies. They have a lot of other people's money they get to invest and they invest their flow primarily in fixed income instruments. Berkshire Hathaway's at its core insurance business, but it invests in stocks but it also has $365 billion of cash that's mainly invested in short term treasuries. I just wrote an article on fool.com how the Fed essentially gave Berkshire $1 billion raise by raising rates. Banks generally benefit in terms of their margins when the yield curve steepens, meaning that the longer dated bonds start paying significantly more than the shorter dated bonds. There's my economics 101 for the day. But, there are winners and losers in general. Rising rates are a downward catalyst on the market, but not all parts of the market are the same.

Jon Quast: Well, I think it's just good to end on that little dose of optimism because we do believe in optimism here at The Fool, and so thank you for that. As always, people on the program may have interest in the stocks they talk about, and the Motley Fool may have formal recommendations for or against, so don't buy or sell stocks based solely on what you hear. For Matt, Rachel, and myself, thank you so much for listening to our show today, and we will see you again next time.

news.Title: Apple is taking Wall Street's top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
news.Content:
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.

Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.

Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.

For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.

Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.

Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.

Apple keeps knocking on the door

Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.

Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .

Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.

Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.

The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

news.Title: 台股跌到季線就是買點？ 他搬出去年走勢：先蹲後跳
news.Content:
近期台股屢經震盪，對於台股未來走勢的預測也成為熱門話題。有網友對照去年第四季情況，認為回測季線後就可望迎來下一波漲勢，「先跌後漲」的歷史會重演，引發熱議。

該名網友在論壇PTT上以「大盤歷史重演多」為題發文，回顧去年第四季的股市情況，表示2025年的第四季也是在2萬8千點附近起伏，當時眾人也都期盼台股攻上3萬點，期間卻遭遇震盪，11月底、12月中曾兩度測試季線，但之後仍迎來漲勢，直接一波突破超過3萬點 。他由此分析， 認為第四季是最容易漲的一季，加上今年又有選舉年的行情，樂觀評估像去年「先跌後漲」的歷史會重演，甚至樂觀預回測季線之後，台股可望繼續迎來下一波漲勢，並附上兩張台股日K線圖佐證自己的看法。

▼原PO認為第四季是全年最容易漲的一季，並佐證去年第四季「先跌後漲」的經驗，認為同樣的歷史可望在今年重演。（示意圖／AI生成）

此論點吸引許多網友留言討論，對於原PO看好歷史重演的預測，眾人看法不一，有網友認同現在是進場布局的好時機：「長線來看，這裏是買點」、「特價買一下不好嗎」、「現在全世界散戶都知道AI未來很好，無腦買放著就是賺」、「千點震盪摩擦上五萬，雜質本來就該被洗出場」。

▼對於原PO第四季「回測季線後就會上漲」的樂觀預測，眾人看法不一。（示意圖／AI生成）

但也有網友認為原PO的預測太過樂觀，認為目前情況不能完全和去年類比：「都知道會崩到11月底12月中了，怎麼會選現在進場」、「去年很難重演啦」、「股票最大的盲點就是以歷史經驗來推測未來的走向」，認為即使後續有反彈行情，但未必如去年一樣會在短時間內發生，現在進場可能太早。此外，也有網友提醒，台股可能受美股影響，擔心若美股科技股修正，台股就可能被拖累，甚至認為融資水位仍有調整空間：「如果要續漲要清融資倒是真的」，甚至人直接批評「走下一波下跌」、「又一個反指標」。

還有些網友認為只要維持「分批進場、長期持有」原則，就不必過度猜測短線高低點。

news.Title: California Wealth Tax Raises Stakes for Meta and Zuckerberg
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms Inc. ( META , Financials ), the social media and AI startup, is already prepping for a possible new California wealth tax before voters' Nov. 3 decision on the proposal.Proposition 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the global net worth of billionaires in California over a five-year period.The plan is estimated to collect around $100 billion from 2027 to 2031, mostly for health care, education and food assistance.For Meta, the problem has become inextricably linked to government.CEO Mark Zuckerberg has made a deal that would allow him greater freedom to sell nonvoting Class C shares yet retain control of the firm. In return, he committed to be a resident of California, or where ever Meta had its headquarters, for eight years.Other tech executives who might be impacted include Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and executives at Salesforce, Snap and Airbnb and DoorDash.It's not only a tax concern for investors.The idea may change where executives choose to live, company structures and capital distribution across California's technology industry.The next spark will be a vote on Nov. 3 and if Prop. 40 succeeds.

news.Title: Meta’s new non-voting shares aim to protect Zuckerberg’s control: Oppenheimer
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Oppenheimer said in a note Friday that Meta Platforms' plan to issue new non-voting Class C shares is likely designed to protect CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The firm maintained its Perform rating and $710 price target on the stock.

Meta announced this week that it will issue new non-voting Class C shares to all shareholders on Jan. 19, 2027.

"We believe this is to protect Mark Zuckerberg's voting rights in the face of a potential CA wealth tax (prop 40) and capital needs to fund AI investments," analyst Jason Helfstein wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The proposed California wealth tax is a one-time 5% levy on residents with a net worth above $1 billion. Oppenheimer estimates Zuckerberg could face a $10 billion to $15 billion tax bill in 2027. The firm added that there is a risk some form of wealth tax could continue in the future.

Oppenheimer also expects Meta to need to raise capital to fund its AI and data center buildout, which the company described in a filing as requiring "hundreds of billions of dollars." The firm expects any raise to be well below that level.

As of Oct. 1, Zuckerberg held 60.6% of Meta's voting power and 13.4% of shares outstanding. If he raised $15 billion personally and Meta raised $150 billion over time without non-voting stock, his voting power would fall to 56.3%.

"While still greater than 50%, creating non-voting stock creates a buffer if the company had to rely on a greater mix of equity vs. debt," Helfstein said.

The analyst added that if Zuckerberg raised $15 billion to $30 billion personally and Meta issued no equity, his voting power would remain at 56.6% to 58.7%. He said this suggests the company expects to issue a material amount of equity over time.

news.Title: 台股失守季線原因找到了！陳龍直言「5萬點前最後洗盤」黑夜過後是黎明
news.Content:
台北股市昨（22）日加權指數重挫 846.34 點，當天盤中開高走低，失守季線支撐位置。長假避險賣壓加上國際地緣政治動盪，讓不少看著綠油油盤面的股民心驚肉跳。 對此， 知名資深分析師陳龍 在最新財經節目中直言，台股失守季線的原因找到了，當前的非理性拋售絕非 AI 產業基本面轉弱或泡沫破裂，而是台股在回頭挑戰 「5萬點前的最後洗盤」 。隨著下週美股四大雲端巨頭財報即將登場，AI 產業的強勁動能將重現光芒，展現 「黑夜過後就是黎明」 的強勢回升契機。

【外部雜音齊發！長假避險引發市場過度恐慌】

面對大盤急跌，陳龍強調，這波回檔並非台灣科技產業出了問題，而是多重外部利空巧合交織。一方面，連續假期讓避險資金抱持「先賣再說」的心態離場觀望；另一方面，中東胡塞武裝攻擊沙烏地機場推升油價、歐洲局勢動盪，加上台幣走弱，使市場避險情緒急速升溫。值得注意的是，全球資金大舉湧入美債避險，帶動 10 年期美債殖利率從高點顯著回落，這反而替台積電（2330）、聯發科（2454）等核心科技股的長線評價帶來上修空間。

【不是泡沫更無斷頭潮！神似年初歷史的「假破底」】

許多散戶擔憂台股是否會引發融資斷頭潮，陳龍給出堅定的定心丸。他分析，當前市場籌碼結構相當穩健，並不存在連鎖斷頭風險，整體型態極度類似今年年初大漲前夕的深蹲修正。當時市場同樣充斥著危機論調，但在震盪整理後，台股隨即迎來驚人的噴發走勢。陳龍指出，這一次短暫的假破底，本質上依舊是主力在挑戰更高峰前的清洗浮額，藉此醞釀下一階段躍升的龐大動能。

【算力需求爆發！AI革命才在初升段】

「AI 絕不是泡沫，而是剛剛拉開序幕的工業革命。」陳龍引用輝達（NVDA.US）執行長黃仁勳的說法指出，未來十年 AI 效能將迎來百萬倍躍升，現在只是基礎建設期的前三年，算力供給永遠趕不上爆發的需求。從 Meta（META.US）擴大資本支出，到台廠供應鏈如日月光投控（3711）先進封裝大幅擴產、京元電子（2449）砸重金擴建新廠，都證明半導體硬體鏈的成長引擎依然轟鳴作響。

【靜待下週巨頭財報！黑夜過後就是黎明】

下週大型科技股財報將成為市場焦點。Alphabet（GOOGL）與微軟（MSFT）預計於10月28日公布財報，亞馬遜（AMZN）則預計於10月29日登場。投資人除了關注營收與獲利，也將檢視雲端業務成長、AI需求，以及龐大資本支出能否帶來相應回報。

面對盤面風雨，陳龍提醒投資朋友，投資最忌諱在恐慌時被情緒牽著鼻子走。下週美國四大雲端服務巨頭即將接棒公布最新財報，屆時亮眼的真金白銀數據，勢必為 AI 族群再度注入強心針。當短期利空在連假後逐漸被市場消化，回頭來看，這段令人難熬的下挫，就是台股奔向 5 萬點大關前，市場給予投資人最後一次從容布局的禮物。

news.Title: 只要台積電破月線「就買進這檔」？ 他喊全力做多：勝率逾6成
news.Content: 近期台股震盪劇烈，投資人也開始思考未來的投資策略。有網友表示整理資料後發現，當台積電（2330）跌破月線時，就是富邦科技(0052)進場的好時機，引發討論。 該名網友在論壇PTT上以「只要台積電跌破月線就進場0052」為題發文，分享自己回測富邦科技（0052）的投資策略，表示自己整理相關數據後，發現只要台積電（2330）跌破月線，就是富邦科技(0052)進場的好時機，並嘗試回測，不論選擇在台積電跌破月線當天進場，或等到隔天再買進，獲得正報酬的機率都有6成以上，若持有1年，報酬更有超過10%的優異表現。除了月線之外，他還提到，「台積電跌破季線」也可能是另一個進場機會。 ▼原PO表示，自己整理資料並回測後發現，只要台積電個股跌破月線，就是0052進場的好時機，若持有時間超過1年，報酬可達逾10%。（東森新聞資料照） 因此他分析，市場回檔不一定代表應該急著出場，反而可以趁機觀察布局時點，並強調面對市場震盪，投資人不必因短期波動而過度恐慌。同時也分享自己的投資經驗，表示曾以3萬8千元買進的群益臺灣加權正2（00685L），目前已有約20%的報酬。他認為，單押0052這種持有多檔權值股如台積電、聯發科（2454）、鴻海（2317）、日月光投控（3711），對於希望長期布局科技產業的投資人而言，或許是相對容易理解的投資選擇。並認為只要維持「台積電跌破月線進場買0052，長期持有」的原則，就有一定勝率，最後還呼籲散戶網友們在市場震盪時，要「團結一心，全力作多！」 ▼原PO看好0052長期持有的獲利機率，認為近期台股震盪反而可能是進場布局的好時機。（示意圖／AI生成） 此話題吸引許多網友留言討論，有些網友認同原PO的論點，認為0052的表現不俗，也適合長期持有：「0052分批買起來！」、「0052長線報酬屌打0050」、「明天開始日日扣0052、0050」、「市值型平常定期定額，大跌手動買一些，然後蓋牌」。 不過也有網友認為，重點其實在於「長期持有」：「長期持有，你怎麼買都贏」、「長期持有可能跌不跌破月線差異不大」。還有一些網友主張直接買台積電個股就好：「為何不直接買台積就好？」、「為啥不跌破月線直接進台積零股」、「其實買台積電就好，長期投資，台積電的產品是寡占市場，所有公司都要跟台積電買」、「我也會直接撿台積電，價值慢慢浮現了」、「搞笑，買台積電就好啦」、「台積本來就是長期持有阿」。

news.Title: 24日台積電運動會取消　基層員工「每人加發3萬元獎金」
news.Content:
即時中心／徐子為報導

薔琵颱風來襲，明（24）日全台有13縣市停班課，台積電表示，為考量人員安全，已決定取消辦理原訂24日舉行的2026台積電運動會。不過，台積電仍會對基層員工發放獎金，每人獎金自去年的2萬5千元，提高至3萬元。

台積電原訂於24日舉行2026台積電運動會，因受薔琵颱風影響，新竹縣、市政府都公告10月23日停止上班，運動會的準備工作也受到影響，為考量人員安全，2026台積電運動會取消辦理。

儘管運動會取消，董事長魏哲家向基層員工發布電子郵件，宣布每人發放3萬元獎金，獎金金額比去年再高5000元。

據了解，魏哲家在信中說，運動會不能如期舉行有點遺憾，但大家在準備過程中的凝聚力跟團體精神就是珍貴的收穫，謝謝員工和家屬的支持。他並提醒大家留意天候狀況。

台積電董事長魏哲家出席去（2025）年台積電運動會。（圖／民視新聞資料照）

原文出處： 快新聞／24日台積電運動會取消　基層員工「每人加發3萬元獎金」

news.Title: Microsoft wants to keep more of its AI billions from Nvidia
news.Content: Microsoft (MSFT) is facing a costly artificial intelligence issue. Two-thirds of the $41 billion in capital expenditures in the latest quarter went to shorter-lived assets such as central processing units and graphics processing units. These are the costly devices that lie behind solutions like Copilot and Azure. Microsoft now wants to retain a larger portion of that expenditure inside the company. With multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, Microsoft will use its Maia chips to run AI inference across its products and services. There is an obvious potential loser if Microsoft succeeds: Nvidia (NVDA). One of the large cloud firms purchasing Nvidia chips to develop AI infrastructure is Microsoft. Microsoft may not need to run all of its workloads on someone else's processors in order to transfer them cheaply onto Maia. There is just one issue. Microsoft's proprietary processors are still "nowhere close" to the more advanced technology of Nvidia or Alphabet (GOOGL), according to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Mandeep Singh . This creates a test worth billions of dollars. Nvidia doesn't have to be replaced everywhere by Microsoft. Maia only has to become proficient at the AI tasks that Microsoft does millions of times every day. Microsoft has a powerful reason to build its own chips Long after a model has been trained, artificial intelligence may be costly. Computers must provide the answer each time someone asks Copilot a query, requests code from GitHub Copilot, or ultimately dispatches an AI agent to do a job. That process is called inference. Because Microsoft runs such services on a massive scale, even modest efficiency improvements may have a significant impact when replicated over millions of users. Microsoft said its current Maia 200 chip is already serving Copilot workloads. Maia 300, expected to enter production deployments in 2027, is designed to become the company's primary inference system. Microsoft also said the Maia 300 can produce seven times the output of the Maia 200 at full rack size and 40% more AI per megawatt than top GPUs. In other words, the company believes it can get more AI work from the infrastructure and power it currently pays for. Because of the massive expenditure, that is important. Microsoft added nearly $116 billion of property and equipment during fiscal 2026, compared with about $65 billion a year earlier. In the June quarter alone, capital expenditures reached $41 billion. It is not necessary for Microsoft to create a semiconductor that is superior than Nvidia for every use if Maia enables the company to offer Copilot and other repetitive AI tasks at a lower cost. Story Continues It could simply lessen the quantity of costly external processors Microsoft need for tasks that its own silicon is capable of handling. Nvidia is not disappearing from Microsoft data centers The catch is that making an AI chip and replacing Nvidia are two completely unique things. Singh contended that when it comes to proprietary AI silicon, Microsoft is still far behind both Nvidia and Google. Google is especially significant, since it demonstrates what Microsoft is attempting to develop. More Microsoft: Microsoft's $665 target hinges on a new AI advantage Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft just sent a strong message to Anthropic Alongside external chips, Alphabet has spent years creating its Tensor Processing Units. This gives Google an additional way to manage the price and efficiency of the AI operating in its cloud. With Maia, Microsoft is attempting to establish a comparable edge. However, Nvidia has spent years creating the software environment that developers use in addition to CPUs. This makes replacing Nvidia an undertaking that involves more than making competitive silicon. Additionally, Microsoft has no justification for giving up on Nvidia entirely. Different hardware is needed for different AI tasks. Serving Copilot replies to clients on a regular basis may need different computer power than training massive frontier models. Therefore, whether Microsoft continues to purchase Nvidia is not the crucial point. It's whether Microsoft can alter the economics by moving enough high-volume work to Maia. Microsoft's AI bill makes Maia worth watching The most recent results from Microsoft demonstrate why investors should be concerned. The tech giant's 2026 annual report showed that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for fiscal 2026 , rising 41%, while Microsoft Cloud revenue reached more than $214 billion. AI is contributing to that company's growth, but Microsoft is investing heavily to provide the processing power that consumers want. The June quarter's $41 billion capital-expenditure bill was larger than Microsoft's $35.8 billion quarterly net income . That doesn't mean the spending is ill-advised. Microsoft is investing because demand is strong. But the larger the infrastructure bill becomes, the more valuable efficiency becomes. That is where Maia could matter. Microsoft may increase the economics of every encounter without waiting for Nvidia to reduce pricing if it can execute more Copilot requests, coding activities, and AI-agent workloads using processors built around its own software. And for this to matter, Microsoft doesn't need to defeat Nvidia. Even a small fraction of an AI infrastructure operation could save tens of billions of dollars. For this reason, what might otherwise seem to be just another piece of arcane semiconductor news should be of interest to a Main Street investor. Microsoft is more than just a chip manufacturer. It is attempting to manage one of the largest costs associated with its AI business. Microsoft may retain a larger portion of Copilot and Azure's earnings if Maia is successful. If it doesn't, Microsoft may continue spending heavily on its silicon while Nvidia keeps collecting on the AI boom anyway. news.Title: 《強勢美股特報》APA,EOG,CBOE,TPL等10檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-23 22:05:54 數位內容中心 發佈

APA（APA.US）： 成交價51.68美元，上漲4.53%，開盤49.94美元，盤中高點51.73美元，盤中低點49.58美元，均價50.81美元，成交量10.49萬股。

APA近期營運主線仍是既有油氣資產對油價變動的高敏感度。輸入資料顯示，公司因營運槓桿較高而被點名，主要資產分布於美國二疊紀盆地、埃及與北海，其中埃及仍被描述為近年重要成長引擎，顯示市場焦點仍在資產組合的原油曝險，而非新交易或新產能。

EOG Resources, Inc.（EOG.US）： 成交價162.6美元，上漲2.94%，開盤159美元，盤中高點162.6美元，盤中低點158.95美元，均價159.99美元，成交量4.8萬股。

EOG近期延續高油價下的穩健增產與資本紀律。輸入資料顯示，公司第2季EPS為5.07美元、營收86.2億美元，管理層將表現歸因於油價走高與營運紀律，並持續強調在避免過度擴張前提下維持強勁現金流，代表公司仍以效率優先，而非激進擴產。

Cboe Global Markets（CBOE.US）： 成交價335.96美元，上漲2.51%，開盤333美元，盤中高點337.36美元，盤中低點332.1美元，均價335.78美元，成交量1.68萬股。

Cboe Global Markets剛把與S&P Dow Jones Indices的獨家授權延長至2051年，持續保有S&P500指數期權的核心特許權。公司也同步提出探索代幣化期權，但明確表示仍屬研究階段，現階段更重要的變化仍是先把既有SPX期權護城河再往後延長數十年。

Texas Pacific Land（TPL.US）： 成交價342.25美元，上漲2.57%，開盤334.96美元，盤中高點342.25美元，盤中低點334.51美元，均價335.41美元，成交量3864股。

Texas Pacific Land近期最值得注意的差異，在於其權利金模式與一般上游油商明顯不同。輸入資料指出，公司主要透過土地與權利金獲利，並非直接開採與銷售原油，因此油價走高時超額利潤更多落在承租方，這也使TPL在能源股強勢期間被點出受惠程度較同業有限；另一項補充訊號是其派息增長評級獲A+。

Twilio（TWLO.US）： 成交價259.31美元，上漲2.24%，開盤256美元，盤中高點260美元，盤中低點253.38美元，均價256.12美元，成交量13.26萬股。

Twilio近期把成長重心押在AI語音與訊息服務。輸入資料顯示，公司2026年第2季營收15億美元，單季自由現金流3.53億美元創高，並預估第3季營收中值15.1億美元，高於市場預期；同時在SIGNAL大會推出Conversation Memory、Conversation Orchestrator與Conversation Intelligence等AI功能，顯示產品正往代理式通訊延伸。

ExxonMobil（XOM.US）： 成交價181.53美元，上漲1.85%，開盤179.37美元，盤中高點182.06美元，盤中低點179.4美元，均價180.56美元，成交量45.76萬股。

ExxonMobil近期一項明確進展，是接手巴布亞液化天然氣項目的運營權。輸入資料顯示，TotalEnergies將縮減持股並把該項目交由ExxonMobil主導，目標是在年底前推進最終投資決策。這代表ExxonMobil在既有PNG LNG基礎上，進一步強化對當地LNG開發節奏與整合協同的掌控力。

EchoStar（ECHO.US）： 成交價87.63美元，上漲2.14%，開盤85.43美元，盤中高點87.74美元，盤中低點85.27美元，均價86.9美元，成交量2.49萬股。

EchoStar近14日未見輸入資料揭露新的財報、資產交易、客戶合約或監管進展。就目前可用資訊來看，市場尚未出現足以重新界定公司近期營運方向的新增公司催化劑，短線仍待後續是否釋出更具體的衛星、無線或資本配置更新。

Skyworks Solutions（SWKS.US）： 成交價83.4美元，上漲1.22%，開盤81.95美元，盤中高點83.67美元，盤中低點81.51美元，均價83.06美元，成交量1.5萬股。

Skyworks Solutions近期最關鍵的變化，是完成對Qorvo的收購。公司預估此案每年可帶來至少5億美元綜效，且在整合完成後24至46個月逐步反映，管理層並稱交易將立即增益調整後每股盈餘。這代表Skyworks正透過整併擴大射頻平台規模，強化手機以外的產品與客戶布局。

EQT（EQT.US）： 成交價55.36美元，上漲1.26%，開盤54.28美元，盤中高點55.57美元，盤中低點54.28美元，均價54.86美元，成交量17.17萬股。

EQT最新可見的變化集中在現金創造與資產負債表修復。輸入資料顯示，公司2026中報每股收益為2.72美元，高於2025中報的1.71美元，經營活動現金流量由298.3億美元增至410.3億美元，同時負債占總資產比率降至30.15%，反映天然氣上游業務的獲利與去槓桿同步改善。

news.Title: 〈美股早盤〉 美油價格突破100美元 重燃市場憂心 主要指數下挫
news.Content: 受科技股大幅拋售及原油價格衝破每桶 100 美元影響，投資人對地緣衝突升溫與通膨復燃深感不安，美股周五(23日)主要指數大多下跌，道瓊指數下跌1.06%，標普 500 指數下跌0.50%，那斯達克指數下跌0.29%，費半下跌0.27%。 投資人在歷經前一日科技股的大幅拋售後仍心存不安。市場對超大規模雲端業者大舉投入全球 AI 建置的龐大資本支出(Capex)能否帶來相應的營收回報產生質疑。此外，龐大的企業借貸與高利率環境引發信貸市場壓力，公司債信用利差已擴大至 2025 年 5 月以來最高水準，大幅提高了額外募資的門檻。 原油價格進一步攀升對股市造成沉重壓力。紐約西德州原油(WTI)期貨上漲 1.4% 至每桶 101 美元，布蘭特原油則觸及 114 美元。油價走高的主因在於市場傳出美國與以色列正擬定計畫，可能對伊朗重啟打擊行動，引發中東衝突再度升溫的擔憂，同時也加劇了通膨前景的不確定性。 儘管如此，目前市場仍預計將在下周的政策會議上維持利率不變。繼9月自2023年以來首次升息後，一些聯準會決策者淡化了近期升息的緊迫性，但同時強調需要將通膨率控制在2%的目標水準。預計聯準會將在12月的年內最後一次會議上升息。 美銀策略師指出，市場尚未完全反映民主黨在國會參眾兩院獲勝的潛在政治風險，若出現此情境，現行的低稅率與法規鬆綁紅利將告終，進而壓抑企業獲利。因此，市場整體的戰術性避險情緒預計可能一路延續至 11 月中旬。 截至台北時間周五21時許： 道瓊指數下跌559.02點或1.06%，暫報52308.96點 標普 500下跌38.58點或0.50%，暫報7624.85點 那斯達克下跌82.98點或0.29%，暫報28875.70點 費半下跌28.91點或0.27%，暫報10703.07點 台積電 ADR上漲0.40% 至每股414.02美元 十年期美債殖利率上漲2個基點，至4.98% 紐約輕原油上漲1.55%，至每桶101.01美元 布蘭特原油上漲1.35%，至每桶114.70美元 黃金上漲0.19%，至每盎司4032.14美元 美元指數上漲0.10%，至101.71 焦點個股： META(META-US)下跌1.84%，報636.92美元 Meta 近期出人意料地宣布發行新一類無投票權股票，此舉讓市場對這家AI巨頭的情緒明顯降溫。 在監管文件中，Meta特別委員會強調，此次決策的動機不僅在於留住執行長祖克柏(Mark Zuckerberg)在加州的控制地位，更在於應對「日益嚴峻的融資環境」。文件特別點名Alphabet、SpaceX、Anthropic及OpenAI等公司近期及預期中的大規模融資行動，指出這些公司正競相「為同一AI增長目標籌集資金」。 文件指出：「特別委員會認為，儘管公司目前擁有足夠的資本資源以應對現有需求，但為了滿足未來的資金需求，公司應在更多企業吸走市場上可用資本之前，審慎地提前完成融資安排。」 SpaceX(SPCX-US)上漲0.77%，報145.87美元 媒體報導，SpaceX正與多家主要蜂窩基礎設施企業洽談，其中最引人注目的是Crown Castle，計畫在全美獲得至少8萬個基站的使用權。分析師指出，這一規模與建設第四個全國性無線網絡的需求相符。 報導於前一晚曝光後，傳統電信運營商AT&T、Verizon及T-Mobile承壓下跌，顯示市場普遍認為SpaceX進軍電信領域的野心正逐步成真。

news.Title: OpenAI aiming for new $30 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation
news.Content:
OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) is looking to raise a fresh $30 billion funding round that would value the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. The company was previously looking to raise capital at a $1.5 trillion valuation, according to Bloomberg.

OpenAI last raised $122 billion in March, which valued the company at $852 billion .

Rival Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), meanwhile, is preparing to file its initial public offering (IPO) ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, with Wall Street anticipating a valuation of as high as $2 trillion.

The company could publicly reveal its S-1 at any time in the coming days.

OpenAI's funding discussions come amid wide-ranging declines in AI stocks on Wall Street over concerns about the data center build-out. Neoclouds, especially CoreWeave ( CRWV ), have been at the center of the latest rout, with investors questioning the companies' enormous debt loads.

Everything from semiconductor to hyperscaler stocks has taken a hit, with Meta ( META ) dropping as much as 7% on Thursday after raising the lower end of its capital expenditure guidance.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is off 7% in the past 5 days.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq slip after sharp tech sell-off
news.Content:
US stocks declined on Friday as worries over the AI trade lingered, following a steep sell-off in Tech ( XLK ) that triggered a flight to bonds.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1%, while those for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) decreased 0.3% after semiconductors and Big Tech sold off on Thursday.

The 10-year Treasury (^ TNX ) yield held below the 5% threshold as investors flocked to bonds.

The AI trade sank on Thursday as concerns over rising financing costs and a potential slowdown in capex weighed on already-battered neocloud stocks like CoreWeave ( CRWV ). AI chip giants Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( SPCX ) also retreated, along with other infrastructure plays.

Shares of this week's earnings headliners, SpaceX ( SPCX ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Meta ( META ), stabilized in premarket trading on Friday after declining in the previous session.

Oil prices remained near a five-month high amid fears of escalating tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude ( BZ=F ) hovering near $110 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) climbing to near $101 per barrel.

LIVE 5 updates

36 mins ago

Stocks open lower as investors search for stability in tech

US stocks opened lower as investors reassessed technology stocks following the Nasdaq Composite's worst day since June.

At Friday's open, major indices are on pace for a clear split in weekly performance after all three traded lower on Thursday.

The Nasdaq is on pace for its second consecutive week of losses, while the Dow is poised for its third straight week of gains. The S&P 500 is hovering near the flatline for the week.

Meanwhile, oil prices rose early Friday as momentum builds around renewed tensions in the Middle East conflict.

Today at 12:46 PM UTC Ines Ferré

SpaceX may not follow Meta's bold plan to raise money for AI

Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports:

Don't expect SpaceX ( SPCX ) to surprise investors like Meta ( META ) did this week by announcing it would issue a new class of nonvoting stock to help fund its AI build-out.

"Importantly, in our discussion w/management, SPCX also said that it is not considering raising equity," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth wrote in a new post-earnings note on Friday. "Capital requirements are front and center across the market, and SPCX indicated it has a number of available pools of capital on the debt side."

SpaceX gave investors a taste of what could be to come on the debt funding front in its earnings report this week.

Today at 11:26 AM UTC Ines Ferré

SpaceX could be on the cusp of buying 80,000 cell towers in a bid to really challenge Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile

Yahoo Finance' Brian Sozzi reports:

Elon Musk's SpaceX ( SPCX ) may be close to sending another message to the telecom giants: we are seriously coming for you.

The company is eyeing the purchase of 80,000 cell sites across the US, Bloomberg reported on Friday. SpaceX is reportedly in talks with two of the companies, Crown Castle and American Tower, among the largest owners of cellular towers.

"Committing ~$30 billion into spectrum is serious enough. Committing to 80K macro sites could be a point of no return," Bernstein analyst Laurent Yoon said. "That is a meaningful number, broadly consistent with the scale required for a nationwide terrestrial wireless network. Whether SpaceX ultimately leases anything close to that figure remains uncertain, but the reported scope suggests a far greater level of commitment than spectrum accumulation alone."

Shares of AT&T ( T ), Verizon ( VZ ), and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) traded sharply lower in pre-market trading.

Today at 10:20 AM UTC Ines Ferré

Investors' flight to bonds sends Fed rate hike bets tumbling

The tech sell-off on Thursday sent investors rushing into bonds, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) to its biggest one-day drop in more than two years and back below 5%.

Behind the move was a shift in rate expectations as longer-term yields fell. With the Federal Reserve set to meet next week, on Oct. 28, investors had been bracing for a rate hike to combat fears of oil-driven inflation.

But those bets faded quickly with the Fed funds futures market putting the odds of an October hike at about 5%, according to Bloomberg data, down from 15% earlier this week, and 37% at the end of September.

Today at 9:31 AM UTC Ines Ferré

This level-headed Tesla bull still expects something huge from the Cybercab

Tesla's ( TSLA ) surprise $5 billion haircut to its capital expenditure plans in its latest earnings call hasn't shaken investor confidence in the long-term potential of a large Cybercab network.

Maybe some near-term confidence was lost in the Optimus humanoid as Tesla deals with design challenges, but not in Cybercabs.

Case in point: Even the reasonable modeling assumptions on the Cybercab from Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco, who has an Equal Weight rating on the stock, still have the fleet size hitting 5 million by the end of 2040. That will be fueled by sharp growth over the next three years, as the chart below indicates.

news.Title: 台股破季線免驚？ 他喊「分批買到半年線」：拉回不買沒道理
news.Content: 台股近期幾番震盪，有網友認為，7月也曾遭遇跌勢，但只花一季就重創新高，因此樂觀看待後續走勢，並稱「若相信AI未來發展，台股拉回就沒有不買的道理」，引發眾人討論。 該名網友在論壇PTT上發文發表對於近幾日台股震盪的看法，並明確表示雖然台股經歷起伏，但自己仍「看多台股」。至於市場上擔憂台股將崩盤的說法，他反而認為台股在7月觸底後，只花一季的時間就重創新高更令人訝異，並表明自己的判斷原則「如果你仍然相信AI未來發展，那台股拉回沒有不買的道理，買低賣高就是這麼簡單」。 ▼原PO表示比起台股近期的跌幅，他認為經歷7月時的跌勢後，台股只花一季的時間就重創新高更令人訝異。（示意圖／AI生成） 至於實際操作策略，他也建議「碰季線沿路買，買到半年線停手」，以分批布局的方式進場，若短期操作，可考慮在月線與指數5萬點附近分兩次停利，長期投資持續持有、不設定停利點；若是藉此區分長短線交易策略。 此論點吸引許多網友留言討論，有些網友認同原PO的看法，認為以目前的情況來看，台股拉回時就是布局的好時機：「拉回不買，難道你想追高套山上」、「台股拉回就是買到底怎麼輸」、「我也等季線在往下買」、「第一次摸季線都會反彈，記得等反彈再砍」、「台股只會小跌然後大漲」。 ▼有些網友認為近期的確是進場布局的好時機，但也有網友認為這波跌勢可能突破季線，甚至有可能跌至年線，對於進場時機眾人看法不一。（示意圖／AI生成） 不過，也有網友認為原PO「看好AI=台股會漲」的論調太簡單，認為兩者間雖然有關，但某個行業的興盛不一定必然會反映在股市上，認為網路泡沫就是前車之鑑：「當年泡沫後難道網路、電商變成夕陽產業嗎？還不是蓬勃發展，然後你能否認當年網路泡沫是假的嗎？根本兩回事」，有人則認為，季線之後可能還會再下跌：「我怎麼覺得有機會破4萬去碰一下年線」、「你慘了這波跌到五年線」、「直接在五年線盤整」，有人因此打算等待更低點再進場：「3萬點再進場」、「2萬點再進場」、「融資沒斷頭前不進場」。從網路上眾多的留言討論來看，可見對於季線能否守住、是否應提前進場，投資人仍有不同看法。 （封面示意圖／東森新聞資料照）

news.Title: BofA names Meta a top AI idea, raises price target on stronger ad growth
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Meta Platforms' expanding artificial intelligence ambitions are creating new avenues for revenue growth beyond advertising, prompting Bank of America to raise its price target on the social media company and reaffirm it as a top AI investment idea.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Bank of America raised its price target on Meta Platforms to $845 from $810, and also maintained its buy rating on the company's stock.

The brokerage's revised outlook follows Meta's third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year over year and above analysts' expectations of $63.3 billion. Advertising revenue reached $63.1 billion, beating estimates of $61.7 billion, while growth excluding foreign-exchange effects remained at 26% despite tougher comparisons with the previous year. Meta also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, above the Wall Street estimate of $73.6 billion.

BofA said Meta's AI investments are strengthening its core advertising business by improving content recommendations, ad targeting and advertiser returns. The brokerage highlighted improvements in user engagement across Instagram, Facebook Reels and Threads, arguing that deeper integration of large language models could support further advertising growth.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The analysts also pointed to emerging opportunities from Meta's Muse AI assistant and enterprise AI services. Meta is developing potential revenue streams through subscriptions, advertising, commerce transactions and enterprise offerings, including API licensing and coding agents. BofA said these businesses could begin contributing incremental revenue in 2027, while management is targeting more than 1 billion Muse users over time. Muse had surpassed 10 million setups in the United States and Canada within roughly six weeks of launch, according to the report.

BofA raised its 2027 revenue estimate by 1.3% to about $319 billion but trimmed its adjusted earnings outlook to $34 per share from $34.24, reflecting higher costs associated with scaling Muse and building its enterprise AI business. The brokerage expects expenses to rise substantially as Meta expands its AI infrastructure, with 2027 capital expenditure forecast at about $210 billion and free cash flow projected to turn negative by roughly $33 billion.

Story Continues

Meta's third-quarter earnings per share came in at $3.83, below the consensus estimate of $5.52, partly reflecting a one-time $9.9 billion legal settlement charge. BofA said profitability was stronger after adjusting for the charge, supported in part by lower-than-expected research and development spending.

The brokerage said growing visibility into AI monetisation could improve investor confidence in Meta's returns, although rising infrastructure costs, potential capital raises, competition from OpenAI and Google, and further legal or regulatory expenses remain risks. It sees Meta's current valuation as attractive relative to its growth prospects and believes the market is not fully accounting for the potential value of its AI models, agents and enterprise services.

news.Title: 台股震盪新手嚇到！ 他抱2檔ETF憂問「會下殺到4萬」內行勸寬心：刪掉APP
news.Content: 這一週台股震盪劇烈，不少投資新手的心情也隨之起伏。有網友坦言自己投入股市約半年，之前看到大盤稍跌時會買進，近日卻聽到「台股會逐步跌到四萬」的預測，感到很不安。 該名網友在論壇Dcard上以「台股會一路殺回四萬嗎？」為題發文，表示自己剛開始投入台股不到半年的新手，目前只買了富邦台灣半導體（00892）、主動統一升級50（00403A）2檔ETF，之前的操作方式都是單股看到大盤稍跌時多少買一些，目前持有2張00892、8張00403A，上週台股下跌時，他也陸續買進，沒想到買完後股價又繼續下跌，讓他的信心開始動搖，尤其看到網路上關於「台股會逐步跌到四萬」的預測，讓他更為不安。 他坦言，雖然自己打算長期持有，也買在台灣最強的半導體上，但看到關於台股走跌的猜測，心中還是有些忐忑，擔心自己現在加碼是否操之過急，不確定是否該持續加碼，或者是否該降低每次加碼的金額「分多批一點慢慢丟」？ ▼原PO表示自己雖然是想長期投資，但看到網上有「台股會逐步跌到四萬」的預測，還是感到擔憂，也不確定是否該繼續加碼買進。（示意圖／AI生成） 此貼文引來不少網友留言討論，有網友認為00892的長期表現值得期待，認為短期震盪終將過去，勸原PO寬心：「買00892等於買台灣科技業的未來，長期有什麼好怕的」、「00892長線絕對沒問題，成分股都是台灣供應鏈牛的上端，震盪都只是過程」，有人認為原PO投入金額不算高，不用太擔心：「才買2張8張是在慌什麼，本金又不大，趁現在回檔多撿便宜」、「才10張就睡不著，那那些手上有幾百張的大戶怎麼辦，放寬心」、「也鼓勵原PO後續可分批陸續投入：「分批丟可以，不要預設立場它會跌到哪 不要被情緒影響」、「季線目前有撐，不要恐慌性賣壓」、「現在逢低佈局00892很好吧，幾年後再來看誰不是笑著數錢」、「如果這樣會怕損失，那我建議定期定額，把app刪掉十年後再看」。 ▼不少人看好00892長期表現，勸原PO不要因短期漲跌就患得患失。（示意圖／AI生成） 還有人針對原PO的擔憂心態提出建議：「沒人能真正預測短期走勢，你只能做好規劃，先想好如果真的發生你該怎麼應對，不要事先假設一定不會發生甚麼，不然真的發生的時候你很容易驚慌失措做出錯誤判斷」、「未來事，誰知道，新聞都是假的，不用看，隔天會漲會跌沒人知道，只要財報優於預期，股市終究會往上漲」，認為原PO若打定注意長期投資，就不必因短期市場震盪過度恐慌。

news.Title: Pre-Markets Remain Spooked by AI Investment Capacity
news.Content:
Friday, October 23rd, 2026

Pre-market futures are down again this morning, after the Dow clawed back into the green by yesterday's close but the tech-heavy (read: AI-invested) Nasdaq fell nearly -700 points (-2.6%). The Dow is now taking the biggest tumble, -377 points, while the Nasdaq is -34 points, the S&P 500 -22 points and the small-cap Russell 2000 -15 points. When Meta Platforms META reported earlier this week, they raised questions about AI infrastructure buildout viability, which spooked markets (here in Halloween season).

The doubt surrounding AI infrastructure investment is palpable, and now affecting the nuts-and-bolts companies listed on the Dow 30 — such as Caterpillar CAT, which is currently -4.9% in today's pre-market. (The heavy equipment manufacturer reports Q3 earnings next Thursday.) Conversely, this has helped ease bond yields, which are down notably from their multi-decade highs a couple weeks ago. The 10-year is below +5% for the first time in a month.

Oil prices remain sticky, with the U.S. and Israel drawing up plans to attack facilities in Iran reportedly aimed at developing nuclear weaponry. We've seen over the past eight months (recall: the war was supposed to last 2-4 weeks) that retaliation from Iran routinely involves shuttering global oil supply. In anticipation of this new round of strikes (and the ongoing bombings at Saudi airport by Iran-backed Houthi rebels), the WTI spot oil price is back up over $100 per barrel (/bbl) while Brent crude is back to early May highs: $115/bbl.

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: AXP, SLB

We see two notable earnings beats on earnings in this morning's Q3 reports. Starting with American Express AXP, earnings of $4.68 per share outpaced the Zacks consensus of $4.47 by +4.7%; it also easily surpasses the year-ago $4.14 per share reported. Revenues of $20.06 billion, on the other hand, missed expectations by -0.74%. Shares are off -12% year to date, and down another -1.9% in today's pre-market. For more on AXP's earnings, click here.

Oilfield management company SLB Corp. SLB, formerly known as Schlumberger, outpaced estimates by 2 cents to $0.64 per share on revenues of $9.45 billion, which beat the Zacks consensus by +1.72%. Shares are up +2% on the news ahead of the bell this morning, adding to the company's +29% gains year to date. For more on SLB's earnings, click here.

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

Normally, in-session Friday trading does not need to deal with many economic metrics, but after the opening bell today we'll see flash U.S. PMI on Manufacturing and Services for October. Estimates for both are expected to tick down month over month to 55.3 and 58, respectively, but still above the 50-level which determines growth from loss.

Also, the final University of Michigan Consumer Survey for October is expected to dip to 46.3 from the previous print of 48.1. Both of these numbers are below the 50-level, demonstrating the negative sentiment regarding the American consumer's outlook from earlier this month.

news.Title: Should KLAC Stock Be in Your Portfolio Pre-Q1 Earnings Results?
news.Content:
KLA KLAC is set to report its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Oct. 28.

For the to-be-reported quarter, KLAC expects revenues of $4 billion, plus/minus $200 million. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $4.05 billion, indicating an increase of 26.09% from the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

For the fiscal first quarter, non-GAAP diluted earnings are projected at $1.16 per share (plus or minus 10 cents). The consensus mark for earnings is pegged at $1.18 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating year-over-year growth of 34.09%.

KLA Corporation Price and EPS Surprise

KLA Corporation price-eps-surprise | KLA Corporation Quote

Consensus Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

KLAC's earnings have surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 2.75%.

Let us see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Key Factors to Note Ahead of KLAC's Q1 Results

KLA's first-quarter fiscal 2027 results are expected to have benefited from accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, particularly advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Increasing demand for AI processors, high-performance computing chips and sophisticated semiconductor designs is driving the adoption of KLA's inspection and metrology solutions. The transition toward 2-nanometer manufacturing and gate-all-around transistor architectures is increasing process control requirements. The company's Semiconductor Process Control business is expected to have benefited from these trends in the to-be-reported quarter.

Increased investments in DRAM manufacturing, particularly high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators and data centers, are expected to have driven top-line growth in the fiscal first quarter. Growing HBM adoption, increasing extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography applications and rising memory-device complexity are creating additional demand for process control equipment. HBM's larger die sizes, stringent performance specifications and complex stacking architectures require more sophisticated inspection and metrology capabilities. These factors bode well for KLAC.

Moreover, fiscal first-quarter results are expected to have benefited from robust demand for advanced packaging solutions, supported by growing adoption of heterogeneous integration, chiplets and high-performance computing architectures. Increasing packaging complexity is encouraging semiconductor manufacturers to deploy more advanced inspection and metrology tools to improve yields and manufacturing efficiency. KLA expects its advanced packaging process control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, indicating growth of more than 70% year over year. The company is also witnessing growing adoption of its front-end inspection technologies in advanced packaging manufacturing.

Meanwhile, fiscal first-quarter results are also expected to reflect improving component availability and expanding manufacturing capacity. KLA expects revenues in the second half of calendar 2026 to increase approximately 20% from the first half, reflecting accelerating customer demand and improving supply chain execution. Strong equipment orders and a backlog of approximately $12.57 billion at fiscal 2026-end are providing substantial revenue visibility.

Nevertheless, KLAC management has highlighted that calcium fluoride optical components can have lead times of 18-24 months or longer, potentially limiting production flexibility. Rising memory prices have also pressured gross margins, with the company indicating a negative impact exceeding 100 basis points in recent quarters.

Story Continues

KLAC Shares Outperform Sector & Peers

KLA shares have returned 21.6% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 18%. However, the company has underperformed peers, including Applied Materials AMAT, Teradyne TER and Axcelis Technologies ACLS, YTD. Shares of Applied Materials, Teradyne and Axcelis have returned 46.1%, 58.2% and 30.3%, respectively, over the same timeframe.

KLAC Stock's Performance

The KLAC stock is not so cheap, as suggested by the Value Score of D. In terms of the forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E), KLAC is trading at 25.44X, higher than the broader sector and peers like Applied Materials and Axcelis but cheaper than Teradyne. The broader sector is trading at 19.79X while Applied Materials, Axcelis and Teradyne trade at 20.69X, 20.67X and 28.37X, respectively.

KLAC Stock's Valuation

KLA's Prospects Ride on Strong Advanced Packaging Growth

KLA's advanced packaging business represents a significant long-term growth opportunity as semiconductor manufacturers increasingly adopt chiplets, heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging architectures. The company expects KLA's share of the advanced packaging market to increase to approximately 7-8% in 2026 from only a few percentage points in 2023. The increasing application of front-end manufacturing processes in advanced packaging is driving demand for more sophisticated inspection and metrology solutions. Growing adoption of hybrid bonding and high-density interconnect technologies should further expand KLA's addressable market.

The company is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending, supported by AI infrastructure investments, semiconductor capacity expansion and technology transitions. The company raised its calendar 2026 WFE market outlook to the low-$150-billion range, representing mid-20% growth from approximately $120 billion in 2025. KLAC management indicated that industry growth in 2027 could match or exceed 2026 levels, with a scenario approaching $190 billion in WFE spending.

KLA's growing installed equipment base is expected to support sustained expansion in its services business. The company has established a long-term annual services revenue growth target of 13-15%, supported by increasing equipment installations, maintenance requirements, upgrades and productivity-enhancing solutions. Approximately 80% of services revenues are contract-based, providing recurring revenue visibility. Strong equipment shipments in calendar 2026 and 2027 should expand the installed base, creating additional opportunities for service contracts and customer support.

Conclusion

KLA's strong positioning in the semiconductor process control market, accelerating AI infrastructure investments and robust demand for advanced packaging solutions bode well for its growth prospects. Increasing process control intensity, rising HBM adoption and expanding WFE spending are expected to sustain revenue momentum. A strong backlog and growing services business further strengthen its long-term outlook.

KLA currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which implies that investors should start accumulating the stock ahead of the fiscal first-quarter earnings results. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: AMAT vs. LRCX: Which Stock Has an Edge in the WFE Space?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT and Lam Research LRCX stand out as key suppliers of wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) like Chemical Vapor Deposition, Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD), Physical Vapor Deposition, Chemical Mechanical Planarization Epitaxy and etching tools to serve various stages of chip manufacturing.

With the AI boom continuing to drive growth for the semiconductor industry, the question remains: Which WFE stock is a better investment pick today? Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which offers a more compelling investment case.

The Case for AMAT Stock

Applied Materials is gaining from rising demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, especially in its Semiconductor Systems business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Systems generated revenues of $7.04 billion, up approximately 27% year over year.

Growing investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging is creating opportunities for the company's wafer fabrication equipment, while rising manufacturing complexity supports demand for differentiated process technologies.

Applied Materials is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Centris Spectral SiN ALD system supports advanced logic manufacturing, while enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD systems target DRAM performance and higher-layer-count high-bandwidth memory.

Beyond revenue growth, Semiconductor Systems is strengthening Applied Materials' profitability. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% in the third quarter from 53.5% a year earlier. The operating margin expanded to 38% from 33.2%, reflecting the value of its technology portfolio and operating leverage.

AMAT's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 guidance anticipates Semiconductor Systems revenues of approximately $7.9 billion, representing 62% year-over-year growth. The outlook indicates that demand across leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging could sustain strong near-term momentum.

Applied Materials expects non-GAAP earnings of $4.02 per share (+/- 20 cents), indicating 85% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The Zacks Consensus Estimate suggests year-over-year growth of 86.6%. The estimates have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Case for LRCX Stock

Lam Research is benefiting from rising demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment as artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure drives investment in memory, leading-edge foundry and advanced packaging. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, systems revenues increased 61.6% year over year to $5.73 billion, reflecting stronger spending across NAND, DRAM and foundry markets.

Story Continues

Growing investments in higher-layer-count NAND, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced chip manufacturing are creating opportunities for Lam Research's etch, deposition and other process technologies. NAND sales increased approximately 40% sequentially, supported by conversions to 256-layer-and-above devices and initial investments in 384-layer technology. Meanwhile, demand for DDR5 and HBM supported DRAM spending, while leading-edge chipmaking and advanced packaging helped drive record foundry revenues.

Lam Research is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Akara etch and Aether dry resist products are gaining traction in foundry and DRAM manufacturing. The company has also raised its cumulative Aether revenue outlook to approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, up roughly $1 billion from its previous estimate. Additionally, its panel plating systems have reached more than 20 customers, highlighting opportunities in advanced packaging.

Beyond systems growth, Lam Research's Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) is strengthening its recurring revenue base. Customer support-related revenues and other increased 40% year over year to $2.49 billion, marking a fourth consecutive quarterly record. High equipment utilization, NAND upgrades and demand for spare parts and services supported performance. The company expects CSBG revenue growth of more than 30% in 2026 and over 15% in 2027.

Lam Research's profitability is also improving. Non-GAAP gross margin reached a record 52.4%, up from 50.6% a year earlier, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 40.2% from 35%. A favorable customer and product mix contributed to the improvement, although higher operating expenses and increased investment in product development remain important considerations.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, LRCX forecasts a non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, plus or minus one percentage point, and an operating margin of 40.5% (+/- 1%). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for LRCX's fiscal second-quarter earnings is pegged at $2.26, suggesting year-over-year growth of 78%. Estimates have been revised upward in the past 30 days.

Stock Price Performance and Valuation of AMAT and LRCX

Year to date, shares of Applied Materials and Lam Research have gained 46.1% and 33.4%, respectively.

YTD Performance Chart

From the valuation perspective, AMAT is trading at a discount. AMAT is trading at a price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of 6.57X, below LRCX's P/S multiple of 7.92X.

Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Conclusion: LRCX vs. AMAT

Lam Research appears better positioned for growth-oriented investors, driven by rising demand for advanced memory manufacturing, AI infrastructure and innovative process technologies. Its strong customer support business and expanding technology portfolio offer attractive long-term opportunities, although its premium valuation makes Applied Materials a compelling alternative for value-conscious investors. LRCX and AMAT carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) each at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .
