news.Title: Analysts Estimate Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR (APELY) to Report a Decline in Earnings: What to Look Out for
news.Content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR (APELY) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.81 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -25.7%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.71 billion, down 5.7% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 39.22% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR?

For Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR, the Most Accurate Estimate is the same as the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that there are no recent analyst views which differ from what have been considered to derive the consensus estimate. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of 0%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #1.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR would post earnings of $0.02 per share when it actually produced a loss of -$0.21, delivering a surprise of -1,150.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Alps Alpine Co Ltd. - Unsponsored ADR doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Another stock from the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry, KLA (KLAC), is soon expected to post earnings of $1.18 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +34.1%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $4.05 billion, up 26.1% from the year-ago quarter.

news.Title: Meta stock pares losses in premarket trading following yesterday's 7% decline
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) stock pared losses in premarket action Friday, following a dismal Thursday trading session. Shares of the social media giant plunged 7%, despite reporting better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue on Wednesday as AI bubble fears reemerged across Wall Street.

Investors have been pullin g back on semiconductor and other AI stocks across the board on questions about whether massive investments in AI data centers will pay off in the long run.

Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimates to between $135 billion and $145 billion from $130 billion and $145 billion. The company also has $825 billion in various spending commitments related to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products.

Despite Wall Street's reaction to Meta's earnings, analysts were largely bullish on the company's outlook, owing to its prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg repeatedly pointed to Muse as a source of growth potential during the company's earnings call, saying that "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years," as long as compute efficiency in AI systems continues to improve.

Meta posted an all-time high revenue of $64 billion in the quarter, well ahead of the $63.3 billion analysts anticipated. GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus expectations of $3.56, but would have been $7.40 without legal charges related to the company's teen mental health settlement.

The company also announced it will issue new nonvoting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders , effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split. The move is meant to ensure Zuckerberg stays in California and retains voting control of the company if the state's Proposition 40 passes on Election Day.

Proposition 40 calls for a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

Ahead of Meta's earnings report, a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in connection with the state's consumer-harms case against the social media giant.

news.Title: Meta’s capital-raising plans expose a major weakness in the AI boom
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Meta's (NASDAQ:META) recent surprise move to issue a new class of non-voting stock has weighed on sentiment toward the AI giant, as Thursday's 7% sell-off shows despite strong earnings. But one of its motives for the move paints a more concerning picture for the AI-dependent stock market.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

In its filing, Meta's special committee highlighted that a motivation for the decision was not only to keep CEO Mark Zuckerberg in California but also "an increasingly challenging environment for raising capital," citing recent large capital raises and anticipated capital raises at Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI "to fund the same AI growth."

"The Special Committee considered that, while the Company presently has sufficient capital resources for its current needs, in order to finance its funding needs going forward it would be prudent for the Company to do so before even more companies have absorbed available capital in the market," the filing said.

Meta expects to use the new Class C shares for equity offerings from time to time, subject to market conditions, and wants them available as early as the end of 2026.

The language is striking because it suggests that even one of the world's most profitable technology companies sees access to capital as something that could become increasingly constrained as the AI arms race intensifies.

Meta is hardly a company in immediate financial distress. But its filing makes clear that the scale of investment required to compete in AI is changing its financing calculus. The new shares would give it another way to raise money, compensate employees and finance acquisitions without diluting the voting power of existing shareholders.

That flexibility could prove valuable as the company commits ever-larger sums to AI infrastructure. More importantly, however, Meta's reasoning raises a broader question for investors: What happens if the companies racing to dominate AI begin competing not just for computing power, but for the capital needed to finance the race itself?

The AI spending race is becoming a race for capital

The companies competing to dominate AI are embarking on an extraordinary investment cycle. Building and operating increasingly powerful models requires vast computing infrastructure, including specialized chips, data centers, networking equipment and electricity. Those investments must be financed well before their eventual returns are fully established.

Story Continues

Meta has raised its projected 2026 capital expenditure to between $135 billion and $145 billion, underscoring the scale of the investment required to sustain its AI ambitions. Its third-quarter results showed revenue growth of 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, but capital expenditures, including finance lease repayments, reached $34.91 billion. Free cash flow turned negative as spending outpaced cash generated after investment.

Those figures do not mean Meta cannot finance its ambitions through its existing business. Its advertising operations remain a significant source of cash. But they illustrate why the company may want additional financing options as its investment requirements expand.

Meta's filing explicitly identifies Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI as companies whose recent or anticipated capital raises could make the funding environment more challenging. The concern is not simply that Meta needs money. It is that many of the companies pursuing the same technological opportunity may need substantial amounts of money at the same time.

This creates a potential paradox for the industry. The greater the perceived opportunity in AI, the more aggressively companies may invest to capture it. But as more businesses seek financing for similar ambitions, competition for investor capital can intensify, potentially increasing the cost of funding and making it harder for some companies to finance their plans on attractive terms.

The risk is not necessarily that the money disappears overnight. Rather, the terms on which it is available could become less favorable just as companies feel compelled to spend more.

Why Meta wants another financing option

Meta's decision also highlights the distinction between having sufficient resources today and being able to fund a long-term investment strategy at an acceptable cost.

The new Class C shares are designed to separate economic ownership from voting power. Under the proposed arrangement, shareholders will receive non-voting shares alongside their existing stock, effectively creating a two-for-one stock distribution. Meta will then have a class of shares it can use for future equity offerings, employee compensation and acquisitions without reducing Zuckerberg's voting control.

That distinction is important because Zuckerberg controls a majority of Meta's voting power despite owning a much smaller share of its economic value. Issuing additional voting shares could weaken his control, while repurchasing shares to offset dilution consumes cash that could otherwise go toward AI investment.

The new structure gives Meta more flexibility to raise equity without forcing that trade-off. It could sell shares to investors, including large institutional or strategic investors, while preserving the governance arrangement that keeps Zuckerberg firmly in control.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Equity financing also has an advantage over borrowing: it does not create interest payments or contractual repayment obligations. But it is not cost-free. Issuing shares dilutes existing investors' economic ownership, and the value of that dilution depends on the price at which the shares are sold and the returns generated by the money raised.

For shareholders, preserving voting control is not the same as preserving economic value. Investors will still need to assess whether the returns generated by AI investments justify the capital committed to them and any dilution that follows.

Meta's move therefore has two implications. It gives the company another tool to finance its AI ambitions, but it also signals that management wants to prepare for a future in which those ambitions may require more outside capital.

A warning sign for the wider AI trade?

The broader concern is what Meta's disclosure might reveal about the financing conditions underpinning the AI boom.

The market has largely focused on the enormous spending commitments being made by major technology companies and the potential revenue that AI could eventually generate. Less attention has been paid to what happens if the companies pursuing those opportunities begin competing more directly for a finite pool of investment capital.

Meta's filing provides an unusually explicit acknowledgment of that possibility from a company at the center of the AI investment cycle. Its special committee is concerned that other companies could absorb available capital before Meta has secured the funding it may need in the years ahead.

That is not proof that capital is running out, or that investors are about to abandon AI. The pool of potential financing is not fixed. Companies can generate cash internally, issue bonds, sell equity, bring in private investors or form partnerships to fund infrastructure. Capital raised by one company does not automatically prevent another from raising money.

Still, those alternatives are not interchangeable. Debt increases financial obligations, equity can dilute shareholders, and private financing or infrastructure partnerships can come with their own costs and constraints. If the industry requires ever-larger sums to sustain its growth, the cost and availability of financing could become as important as the amount being spent.

The implications could extend beyond the companies raising money directly. If investors become less willing to finance ambitious AI projects, private companies could face pressure to delay expansion, while publicly traded companies might have to reassess capital expenditure plans or accept less favorable financing terms. A more selective funding environment could also expose differences between companies with strong cash-generating businesses and those more dependent on external capital.

For investors, the concern is therefore less about an imminent funding crisis than about the possibility that financing becomes more expensive or restrictive just as expectations for AI-driven growth become more demanding.

The real test is whether AI spending generates sufficient returns

Ultimately, the sustainability of the AI boom will depend on whether the revenues and profits generated by the technology can justify the infrastructure being built to support it.

If AI adoption produces durable new revenue streams, boosts productivity and supports attractive returns on invested capital, the industry's enormous funding requirements may prove justified. Companies that secure financing early could be well positioned to capitalize on the opportunity.

If monetization falls short of expectations, however, the same spending commitments could become a burden. Companies might find themselves competing for capital to sustain projects whose returns take longer to materialize than anticipated. That could pressure valuations, constrain investment elsewhere and expose investors to the consequences of an industry-wide rush to build capacity.

There is also a potential feedback loop. As companies spend more to keep pace with competitors, investors may demand stronger evidence that those expenditures will generate sufficient returns. If the evidence fails to materialize quickly enough, the market could become more selective about which companies deserve continued access to capital. That, in turn, could force some businesses to slow their investment just as competitors continue to expand.

Such a scenario would not necessarily mean the AI opportunity itself is overstated. It would mean that the financial returns from the technology may be distributed unevenly, and that some companies could struggle to finance their ambitions even as others succeed.

Meta's new share class does not establish that such a reckoning is approaching. But its filing reveals that the company sees a strategic advantage in securing financing flexibility before its competitors absorb more of the available capital.

For a market that has spent years pricing in the transformative potential of AI, that is an important distinction. The next phase of the boom may depend not only on who builds the most powerful technology, but also on who can finance the race — and generate enough returns to make the spending worthwhile.

news.Title: SpaceX won't follow Meta's playbook to fund its AI build-out, JPMorgan says
news.Content:
Don't expect SpaceX ( SPCX ) to surprise investors like Meta ( META ) did this week by announcing it would issue a new class of nonvoting stock to help fund its AI build-out.

"Importantly, in our discussion w/management, SPCX also said that it is not considering raising equity," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth wrote in a new post-earnings note on Friday. "Capital requirements are front and center across the market, and SPCX indicated it has a number of available pools of capital on the debt side."

SpaceX gave investors a taste of what could be to come on the debt funding front in its earnings report this week.

Execs guided to $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditures for the fourth quarter. This would be a meaningful step-up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, $18.4 billion in the second quarter and $10.1 billion in the first quarter.

SpaceX ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

On the earnings call, the company's veteran CFO, Bret Johnson, didn't seem fazed by recent tremors in the debt markets amid concerns over the financial health of neoclouds such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ).

All systems go on the pursuit of capital, or so it appears.

SpaceX is reportedly eyeing a capital raise of $40 billion with financial powerhouses Goldman Sachs and Apollo. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years (particularly in the AI segment)," Moffettnathanson analyst Julie Zhu said. "SpaceX has moved at a frenetic pace over the last few months, closing the Cursor acquisition; announcing a new Starbase in Louisiana; winning yet another large IaaS contract; launching Starship flight 14; and purchasing Grain's 800 MHz spectrum. Each of these announcements portends an enormous amount of spending, both capex and opex, ahead."

news.Title: Why Tesla's $5 billion capex cut isn't the warning sign AI stock bears think it is
news.Content:
It was the capex cut heard around the world of markets.

Or was it a capex cut to begin with?

Tesla ( TSLA ) said this week it's cutting its 2026 capital expenditures guidance by $5 billion to $20 billion. Just three months ago, the company lifted it by $5 billion to $25 billion. The quick retrench sparked worries in an already nervous market for tech stocks that Tesla's capital expenditures cut signaled a slowdown in AI demand.

The thing is, Tesla isn't a hyperscaler. And the cut ties more closely to the challenges of making Optimus humanoid robots than a less optimistic view on AI from CEO Elon Musk.

"Bears are already calling that the first hyperscaler capex cut, but Tesla has no cloud to sell and no contracted capacity to walk away from," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said in a note. "We expect Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Amazon ( AMZN ) to confirm the massive capex spending path next week rather than cut it, because the demand underneath keeps showing up in the numbers and monetization is now starting to kick into next gear."

Ives makes a great point — one that warrants a deeper think by the bears trying to grab a firmer hold on the broader market by dumping top tech names.

Thursday was an absolute bloodbath for Big Tech , with the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) getting slammed nearly 2.6% in its worst single-day beatdown since June.

Adding to the perception of what Tesla did, Meta ( META ) dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results , posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive spending on AI.

The company said it would issue a new tranche of stock to help fuel its AI build-out.

Throw in crude oil spiking above $112 a barrel on geopolitical tensions with Iran, and you have a mini market meltdown like Thursday.

Just don't blame Tesla for it.

"Tesla delivered the opposite of a capex scare: it cut its full-year capex guide, spent well below expectations, and turned an expected cash outflow into positive free cash flow while FSD attach, subscriptions, backlog, and Megapack orders all moved the right way, so the core business is funding the autonomy and robotics build," Ives said.

news.Title: Down 21.0% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why KLA (KLAC) Looks Ripe for a Turnaround
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) has been beaten down lately with too much selling pressure. While the stock has lost 21% over the past four weeks, there is light at the end of the tunnel as it is now in oversold territory and Wall Street analysts expect the company to report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Here's Why KLAC Could Experience a Turnaround

The RSI reading of 23.92 for KLAC is an indication that the heavy selling could be in the process of exhausting itself, so the stock could bounce back in a quest for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

This technical indicator is not the only factor that calls for a potential rebound for the stock. There is a fundamental indicator as well. A strong agreement among sell-side analysts covering KLAC in raising earnings estimates for the current year has led to an increase in the consensus EPS estimate by 0.4% over the last 30 days. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Moreover, KLAC currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. news.Title: NVDA vs. LRCX: Which AI Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy?
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two leading semiconductor stocks benefiting from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

NVIDIA powers AI workloads through its advanced computing chips and platforms, while Lam Research provides essential manufacturing equipment used to produce advanced chips and memory. Both companies are benefiting from rising AI infrastructure investments, but their growth opportunities, valuations and risks differ.

With NVIDIA trading at a lower price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple and Lam Research delivering stronger year-to-date stock gains, which semiconductor stock offers investors a better buying opportunity today? Let's find out.

NVDA: AI Leadership Supports Strong Growth Prospects

NVIDIA delivered an impressive second-quarter fiscal 2027 performance, with revenues soaring 106% year over year to $96.22 billion. Data Center revenues surged 117% to $89 billion, driven by strong demand for its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased 120% to $2.22, while gross margin reached 75%.

NVIDIA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote

NVIDIA's growth opportunities extend beyond hyperscalers to AI cloud providers, enterprises and sovereign customers. The rollout of its Vera Rubin platform and expanding AI infrastructure investments could support further growth. Its third-quarter revenue guidance of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and management's preliminary expectation of roughly 70% fiscal 2028 growth signal continued momentum.

However, NVIDIA faces significant challenges. Supply constraints are limiting its ability to meet customer demand, while rising memory costs are expected to pressure gross margins. Management anticipates margins could decline to 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in fiscal 2028.

Geopolitical uncertainty also remains a concern, with the company's forward outlook assuming no Data Center compute revenues from China. Despite these risks, NVIDIA's strong profitability, computing ecosystem and expanding customer base support its long-term investment appeal.

LRCX: AI-Driven Equipment Demand Creates Opportunities

Lam Research is benefiting from growing semiconductor manufacturing requirements as AI chips, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging become increasingly complex. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues increased 54.4% year over year to $8.22 billion. Non-GAAP EPS rose 74.6% to $2.20, while non-GAAP gross and operating margins reached records of 52.4% and 40.2%, respectively.

Story Continues

Lam Research Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote

The company's deposition and etch technologies are essential to manufacturing advanced semiconductors. Its customer support business provides another growth driver, generating nearly $2.5 billion in quarterly revenues. Management expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to increase well more than 40% and projects wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027.

Nevertheless, Lam Research remains exposed to semiconductor capital-spending cycles. Clean-room availability and component shortages are restricting industry output, and near-term constraints limited its second-quarter revenue guidance to $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. The revenue guidance reflects a 4.6% sequential increase, significantly lower than the 22.3% increase in the second quarter.

China supplied 35% of first-quarter revenues, but management expects a meaningfully lower share in the second quarter. These factors could affect near-term growth.

NVIDIA vs. Lam Research: Which Has a Better Growth Profile?

Analysts' projections suggest NVDA has a better growth profile than LRCX. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NVIDIA's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year increase of 88.7% and 95%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 67.5% and 69.3%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year jump of 48.5% and 60.9%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 17.2% and 22.2%, respectively.

NVDA vs. LRCX: Valuation and Price Performance

NVIDIA has the valuation advantage, trading at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 15.18 compared with 23.02 for Lam Research. This difference is notable, given NVIDIA's faster recent revenue growth, higher gross margins and strong revenue outlook.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Lam Research has delivered superior stock market momentum, with shares rising 33.4% year to date compared with a 13.8% gain for NVIDIA. However, NVDA's lower valuation and stronger growth profile make it more attractive than LRCX.

Conclusion: NVIDIA Is the Better Investment Bet Today

Lam Research offers compelling exposure to rising semiconductor manufacturing spending, advanced packaging and memory production. Its record profitability and favorable industry outlook make it a strong contender.

However, NVIDIA appears to be the better investment bet today. Its faster growth, 75% gross margin, expanding AI customer base and lower P/E multiple offer a more attractive mix of growth and relative value. Supply constraints, memory costs and geopolitical risks remain important considerations, but NVIDIA's leadership in AI computing gives it the edge.

Currently, NVIDIA sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), making it a must-pick compared with Lam Research, which has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Content:
台積電(2330-TW)原定於10月24日運動會因為颱風薔琵取消，不過，「小禮物」特別獎金據悉仍將照常發出，且加碼達3萬元，高於去年的2.5萬元。

news.Title: US equity funds post inflows for a second straight week
news.Content:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - US equity funds attracted inflows for a second consecutive week in the seven days to October 21, as ‌easing Treasury yields and strong corporate earnings so far bolstered investor ‌appetite, although caution over the artificial intelligence trade capped weekly net purchases.

US equity funds recorded ​net inflows of $5.07 billion, a roughly 62% decline from $13.37 billion the week before, according to LSEG Lipper data.

Easing US Treasury yields partly alleviated concerns over high borrowing costs, with the benchmark 10-year yield down nearly 38 basis ‌points from its early-October peak ⁠of 5.3645%, a 24-1/2-year high.

Investors also drew confidence from the solid start to the US earnings season. Nearly 24% ⁠of S&P 500 companies have reported, with roughly 82% topping analysts' average estimates, according to LSEG data.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite, however, fell 2.6% on Thursday after ​Meta ​reported strong results on Wednesday but announced ​plans to issue non-voting stock, ‌reigniting concerns about rising capital commitments across the technology sector.

Investors bought a net $8.63 billion of US large-cap funds and $1.92 billion of mid-cap funds during the week, while withdrawing a net $4.24 billion from small-cap funds.

Sectoral funds attracted $1.8 billion in weekly inflows after two consecutive weeks of outflows, driven largely by $1.18 ‌billion flowing into metals and mining funds. ​Technology and industrials funds also recorded net ​inflows of $429 million and $269 million, ​respectively.

US bond funds recorded weekly outflows of $969 million, ending ‌a 26-week streak of net purchases.

Investors ​withdrew $3.3 billion from longer-dated ​government and Treasury fixed-income funds after three weeks of inflows, but invested $1.76 billion in short- to intermediate-term government and Treasury funds. They ​also added a notable $1.56 ‌billion to municipal debt funds.

Meanwhile, money market funds attracted $14.82 billion ​in weekly inflows, following roughly $45.93 billion in outflows the previous week.

(Reporting ​by Gaurav DograEditing by Tomasz Janowski)

news.Content:

Shares of this week's earnings headliners, SpaceX ( SPCX ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Meta ( META ), stabilized in premarket trading Friday after declining in the previous session.

news.Title: Should You Buy Amazon Stock Before Oct. 29?
news.Content:
Corporate America just entered earnings season for the quarter ended Sept. 30. It comes at a critical moment, because investors are grappling with elevated inflation, rising interest rates, and turbulence in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry -- all while the S&P 500 index is trading at a historically expensive valuation. So, strong corporate earnings will be necessary to keep this bull market going.

Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) is one of the companies at the center of the AI boom. It operates an industry-leading cloud platform, develops its own large language models (LLMs), and even designs its own data center chips. It's scheduled to release its operating results for the third quarter on Oct. 29, and they will give investors some insight into the current state of the AI industry.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amazon stock looks attractively valued right now, so is it a buy heading into the report?

All eyes on Amazon Web Services

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is Amazon's cloud computing platform, which offers a growing portfolio of tools and services that enterprises need to develop and deploy AI software. It's consistently the company's fastest growing business segment, and it's also the most profitable, so its results will be Wall Street's main focus on Oct. 29.

AWS operates state-of-the-art data centers all over the world which house advanced AI chips from suppliers like Nvidia , and it rents the computing capacity to its enterprise customers. However, Amazon also designs its own chips now, like Trainium2 and Trainium3, which it says offer better price-performance than the competition.

Amazon not only rents these chips, but also sells them to customers, and sales revenue was tracking at an annualized rate of over $25 billion on June 30. This could become a huge business over the long term, so look out for some updated numbers on Oct. 29.

In addition to computing capacity, enterprises also need ready-made LLMs to sit at the foundation of their AI software projects, and the AWS Bedrock platform offers a library of 100 of them. AWS also built an AI-powered coding assistant called Kiro that can help programmers bring software to life more quickly.

AWS generated $42.2 billion in total revenue during the second quarter of 2026, up 37% from the year-ago period. That growth rate accelerated for the fourth-straight period, so the platform was carrying significant momentum into the third quarter.

Story Continues

As of June 30, AWS had a whopping $496 billion order backlog from customers who were waiting for more data center capacity to come online. That number increased by a triple-digit percentage year over year, which is a sign revenue growth could accelerate even further in the coming quarters.

Longer term, Amazon chief executive Andy Jassy thinks AWS can eventually reach $1 trillion in annual revenue, so while the Oct. 29 report will be important, it's just one part of a much bigger growth story.

Amazon stock looks attractively valued heading into Oct. 29

Amazon's earnings have steadily improved over the last few years, not just because of AWS, but also because its flagship e-commerce business is gradually becoming more profitable. The company generated earnings of $12.44 per share over the last four quarters, placing its stock at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 21.2, so it's much cheaper than the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index which has a P/E of 30.2.

But there is one caveat. In the first half of 2026, over $69 billion of Amazon's $120.7 billion in pre-tax profit came from paper gains from its investment in Anthropic, which were completely unrelated to the company's operations. That's why Wall Street's average forecast (provided by Yahoo! Finance) suggests Amazon's earnings will actually decline to $10.55 per share in 2027. But with a forward P/E of 25 based on that estimate, its stock is still very attractively valued.

The signs suggest Amazon's third-quarter report will be another blockbuster, thanks primarily to AWS. Therefore, its stock could be a solid buy ahead of Oct. 29, but it's important for investors to stay focused on the long term, because the best returns won't come over the next few months, but rather over the next 5-to-10 years.

news.Title: ETFs in Focus as META Drops 7% Despite Q3 Earnings Beat, Strong View
news.Content:
Shares of Meta Platforms META dropped nearly 7% on the bourses yesterday, despite reporting better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 21, 2026. The slump experienced by the social media giant's shares was primarily led by negative free cash flow and an upward revision to the lower end of its full-year capital expenditure guidance.

The company's growing long-term debt, which rose 38% year over year to $80.9 billion in the third quarter, coupled with persistent revenue weakness in META's Reality Labs unit, likely further dampened investor sentiment, contributing to the stock's decline yesterday.

Nevertheless, the company's advertising business continued to show strength, with its partnership ads product growing more than 97% year over year and surpassing $15 billion in annual revenue run rate in the third quarter.

Against this backdrop, investors with strong conviction in Meta's long-term trajectory might see the latest share pullback as a golden opportunity to invest in the WhatsApp owner. However, concerns over the company's rapidly escalating AI investments and their impact on its share price performance may prompt some investors to remain on the sidelines.

Amid this backdrop, investors may consider exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with substantial exposure to Meta Platforms as an alternative to investing directly in the stock. Such ETFs offer an opportunity to benefit from a potential rebound in META stock while avoiding the idiosyncratic risk and sharp volatility associated with a single-stock position.

Now, before we explore the best ETF options for gaining exposure to Meta, let us examine the company's third-quarter performance across other key operational metrics and how market, particularly rating agencies, reacted to its results.

A Brief Analysis of META's Q3 Results

META's third-quarter adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 13.5%, while revenues beat the consensus mark by 1.9%. A similar trend was observed on a year-over-year basis, with the bottom line increasing 2.1%, while the top line registered robust growth of 26%.

The total number of ad impressions served across META's Family of Apps increased 10%, driven primarily by growth in engagement and users, as well as ad load optimizations.

On the other hand, the global average price per ad increased 14% year over year, as META benefited from ad performance gains and improved macro conditions.

On the operational front, Meta reported key performance gains driven by updates to its ad infrastructure during the third quarter. Notably, the company expanded its GEM ads ranking model to additional surfaces, driving a 1% to 1.7% increase in conversions for off-site conversion campaigns and a 9.6% increase in app ad conversions.

Story Continues

Meta continued to scale its retrieval systems efficiently. In the reported quarter, improvements to Andromeda, such as scaling model complexity and throughput, increased Facebook conversions by 1.4%.

Meanwhile, its generative AI ad creative tools continued to strengthen in the third quarter. Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of Meta's generative AI ad creative tools during the quarter. Adoption of video generation features rose 25% sequentially, supported by ready-made video tools.

Its Reality Labs segment continued to incur operating losses, which, however, narrowed year over year.

Meta expects to generate fourth-quarter revenues in the range of $73-$76 billion, the midpoint of which is $74.5 billion and comes in higher than the consensus estimate of $73.65 billion.

As for its Reality Labs unit, META anticipates losses to narrow to $18-$19 billion this year and approximately $15 billion next year, reflecting its ongoing efforts to redirect investments toward higher-priority areas, particularly AI.

Market Reaction

Following META's third-quarter results, Rosenblatt raised its price target on Meta Platforms shares to $900 from $886 on Oct. 22, 2026, while maintaining a Buy rating.  JPMorgan also raised its price target for Meta to $940, emphasizing the company's AI momentum and fourth-quarter revenue outlook, which exceeded their expectations (as cited in Investing.com).

news.Title: 南韓KOSPI上演V型反轉收高0.3% 半導體雙雄強彈
news.Content:
受隔夜美股科技股重挫、中東局勢升溫及市場對人工智慧支出放緩疑慮的衝擊，南韓綜合股價指數KOSPI周五(23日)早盤面臨沉重賣壓，盤中一度重跌超過 4%，最低下探至 5305.98 點。不過，午後在半導體權值股買盤回流帶動下，大盤演出戲劇性的「V型反彈」，終場逆勢上漲 16.53 點或 0.30%，收在 5550.30 點。

其中，SK海力士因宣布撤回旗下固態硬碟子公司 Solidigm 的赴美掛牌上市(IPO)計畫，消除了長期困擾股價的潛在利空，自早盤下跌 4.3% 逆轉收漲 4.4%；三星電子尾盤也翻紅收漲約 0.46%。

針對周五的逆轉行情，Fibonacci Asset Management Global 執行長 Jung In Yun 指出：「早盤的拋售迅速反映了諸多利空消息，促使投資人逢低承接遭到超賣的股票。」

他進一步表示，美國公債殖利率大幅回落，有助於舒緩科技股的評價壓力；儘管市場對 AI 支出的疑慮猶存，但在企業獲利前景依然具備韌性的情況下，被壓低的股價已難以忽視。不過，他也強調：「當天的反轉雖展現出買盤承接意願，但若要形成可持續的復甦，仍需即將公布的企業財報給予信心。」

相較之下，三星證券股票銷售交易員 Roy Lim 則認為，這波回升「主要是技術性反彈，是機構投資人在 Solidigm 撤回上市案後買進海力士所推動。」

隨著 10 月以來韓股回檔近兩成，KOSPI 的 12 個月預估本益比已下滑至約 4.2 倍，成為 2006 年有紀錄以來首個跌破 5 倍門檻的兆美元級市場。彭博專欄作家 Garfield Reynolds 指出，南韓在經濟強勁成長期間，其市場折價不僅未縮小反而持續擴大，這意味著一旦市場情緒轉向，南韓股市後續極可能展現超越其他市場的強勁走勢。

然而，籌碼結構仍暗藏隱憂。iM Securities 研究員 Lee Sang-heon 分析，9 月外資大舉賣超時，有八成賣壓是由兩大半導體龍頭的買回庫藏股計畫吸收；他表示：「買回庫藏股僅提供了下檔支撐；當前的重挫並非單純因為庫藏股退場，而是因為市場已步入空頭階段。」

展望後市，韓亞證券研究員 Kim Rok-ho 預期，SK海力士財報將展現至少 30 兆韓元的額外股東回饋空間，且買回並註銷庫藏股的可能性高於發放股利。但未來資產證券研究員 Kim Seok-hwan示警，獲利及長期合約題材已充分反映於股價中，推升股價的動能自 8 月起由獲利成長轉向股東回饋，這項轉變本身可能就是景氣循環接近頂部的信號。

news.Title: Is Meta Platforms Stock a Buy as Revenue Continues to Soar?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) stock looks like a buy after the social media company once again reported strong revenue growth and issued upbeat guidance. While the stock has rallied from its summer low following the introduction of its Muse AI agents, the stock is around breakeven on the year after a post-earnings sell-off.

Let's dive into Meta's results and prospects to see why the stock looks like a buy.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Meta delivers 26% revenue growth in Q3

The biggest reason to own Meta stock is that it has been one of the best companies at using AI to drive growth in its core business. This was evident again in Q3, when revenue grew 26% to $64.6 billion, beating the $63.37 billion consensus, as compiled by LSEG .

Adjusted EPS, excluding a large legal settlement, came in at $7.40. That easily surpassed the $5.75 consensus.

Meta's advertising revenue jumped 26% to $63.1 billion, while other revenue climbed 59% to $1.1 billion. Revenue at Reality Labs, which is home to its reality headsets and smart glasses, fell 6% year over year to $443 million.

Reality Labs continues to produce large losses, with operating income coming in at a loss of $4.1 billion. Excluding charges, Meta's overall operating income would have risen 11%. The company said it is shifting its focus with Reality Labs toward personal superintelligence and incorporating Muse into its smart glasses while deemphasizing virtual reality investments

Meta's advertising growth was led by a 14% rise in average ad price and a 10% increase in ad impressions. The growth continues to be driven by AI, with new predictive models and generative AI tools continuing to improve ad personalization and effectiveness. This is helping improve engagement and conversion rates.

Meanwhile, over 10 million people in just the U.S. and Canada have already been using the company's new Muse AI agents since its launch a month and a half ago. About a quarter of users are interacting with the platform daily. Meta will initially monetize Muse through a combination of transaction fees and subscriptions for high-use plans. It also sees an eventual opportunity around paid usage and business services. It's also building an enterprise product as well, where it said it wants to " serve as much high-margin inference demand as possible."

Story Continues

Meta also continues to grow its user base. Family Daily Active People (DAP), a metric measuring registered users who log in to one of Meta's apps daily, rose 2.8% year over year to 3.64 billion.

One of the biggest topics surrounding Meta and other hyperscalers (owners of large data centers) is the capex spending on AI infrastructure. The company raised the low end of its prior capex budget, taking it to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion from a prior outlook of $130 billion to $145 billion. Despite generating nearly $32.8 billion in operating cash flow in the quarter, Meta had negative free cash flow of $2.1 billion due to its $34.9 billion in capex spending.

Looking ahead, Meta forecasted Q4 revenue of between $73 billion and $76 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 22% to 27%. Analysts were looking for Q4 revenue of $73.7 billion. While the company did not give a full-year 2027 outlook, it did say its losses for Realty Labs would fall to $15 billion.

Now is the time to buy Meta stock

Meta is one of the best AI growth stories out there while trading at an attractive valuation, making the stock an solid buy. It's using AI in its core business to keep users on its site longer while delivering them more relevant ads that lead to higher conversions and ad prices. Meanwhile, its Muse AI agents have taken off and it looks like this could become another big future revenue stream for the company.

Trading at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 19 based on 2027 analyst estimates. Meta's stock is cheap for the type of growth it is delivering. That makes it a top AI stock to own heading into 2027.

news.Title: Apple could be about to dethrone Nvidia as world's most valuable company
news.Content:
Tough reviews of Apple's ( AAPL ) new foldable Duo smartphone don't appear to be shaking the bulls on the stock.

Apple's market cap of $5.08 trillion is less than 1% shy of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) $5.12 trillion, putting it on the cusp of knocking the AI chip darling off the throne as the world's most valuable company.

Nvidia by and large has held the crown for more than two years.

But with investors starting to question the health of the AI trade, Nvidia's Teflon stock has come under pressure. Nvidia shares are down 7.3% over the last month, while Apple is up 2.5%.

Apple is seen as a more defensive play given its hardware focus.

Thursday was an absolute bloodbath for big tech, with the Nasdaq Composite getting slammed down nearly 2.6% in its worst single-day beatdown since June.

AI play Meta ( META ) dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results, posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive spending on AI.

The company said it would issue a new tranche of stock to help fuel its AI buildout.

"With roughly 375 million iPhones that have not upgraded in over 4 years, we believe the pool of buyers waiting for a reason to upgrade is deep enough to keep Duo demand high well into 2027," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said in a note on Apple.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: 黃金也被賣來救急 匯豐解析金價失守4000美元背後壓力
news.Content: 現貨黃金23日一度跌破每盎司4000美元關卡，與美股同步走弱，讓黃金的避險功能受到考驗。匯豐指出，股市下跌引發的追加保證金需求，可能迫使投資人賣金籌措現金，加上債券殖利率上升與美元走強，使黃金短期承壓，但債務與通膨疑慮仍支撐長期配置需求。 金價今年曾突破每盎司5000美元、創下歷史新高，隨後漲勢放緩並回落，市場波動加劇。匯豐資產管理策略師在最新報告中指出，高油價、利率上行與債券殖利率飆升，正對黃金構成壓力。 股市下跌急需現金 黃金也成賣壓來源 黃金近期跟著美股下跌，關鍵在於流動性壓力，而非避險需求完全消失。匯豐警告，槓桿資金集中持有黃金，一旦股市下跌觸發追加保證金要求，投資人可能被迫出售黃金，以補充現金，造成股票與黃金同時承壓。 在這種情況下，流動性較好的資產反而容易成為優先變現的對象。即使投資人仍看好黃金的長期價值，也可能因眼前的資金需求而賣出，使黃金無法抵銷股票部位的跌幅。 匯豐強調，沒有任何一種資產能抵禦所有類型的市場衝擊，投資人不應將黃金視為萬能避險工具。 殖利率走高 持有黃金成本上升 除了籌措現金的需求，美國公債殖利率上升，也是壓抑金價的重要因素。 匯豐全球首席投資長Willem Sels與全球財富洞察主管Lucia Ku在7月的報告中指出，黃金在中東衝突期間未能明顯上漲，走勢與股票大致同步。由於黃金本身不孳息，債券殖利率上升會提高持有黃金的機會成本，對金價形成壓力。 因此，地緣政治風險升高，並不保證黃金一定上漲。當高油價、殖利率上升、美元走強與股市下跌同時出現，黃金仍可能遭到拋售。 匯豐預期，實質殖利率維持高檔與美元走強，可能使金價短期維持區間震盪。黃金雖可對沖部分長期貨幣與信用風險，卻未必能在短期流動性衝擊中保護投資組合。 多頭過度擁擠 獲利了結加劇波動 對於先前金價大幅回檔，匯豐貴金屬首席分析師James Steel在5月指出，金價今年1月底觸及每盎司約5400美元高點後回落，部分原因是多頭部位過於擁擠，獲利了結進一步放大價格波動。 Steel認為，黃金在中東衝突期間表現不佳，並不代表避險功能失效。當油價上漲、債券殖利率與美元走強，加上股市下跌，投資人可能出售黃金籌集現金。 他形容：「黃金是一份保險單，而這份保險單正在被變現。」這也反映黃金在市場壓力下的另一種作用：投資人可能透過出售黃金取得所需資金，而金價因此承受賣壓。 債務與通膨疑慮未解 長期支撐仍在 儘管短期走勢承壓，匯豐資產管理策略師認為，近期回檔並不代表以對抗貨幣貶值為核心的交易邏輯已經失效。

news.Title: Earnings flood, Fed meeting pose pivotal tests for rickety AI market rally
news.Content:
By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting both posing critical tests for a suddenly shaky market rally.

Weakness in technology shares left investors on edge about the state of the AI trade ‌that has driven the US equity bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary.

The AI pullback deepened on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite posting its biggest one-day drop ‌since June. Investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Meta is one of the hyperscalers spending massively to build out data centers, while Lam is a high-flying semiconductor company, one of a group that has ​been among the biggest AI stock winners.

Three other hyperscalers -- Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon -- headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies. The Fed's interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday also could rattle markets.

"There are a lot of balls in the air," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro.

"Next week, you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi said. "The market's just not giving the benefit of the doubt to companies ‌that are spending a ton of money on building this all ⁠out, which to us is actually very healthy, but still does augur for some short-term pain."

Investors also have their focus trained on the US midterm elections on November 3, with growing bets that the Democrats will wrest control of the US Congress away from President Donald Trump's Republican party. ⁠The series of market catalysts could ratchet up volatility over the next couple of weeks and challenge optimism that has helped lift the benchmark S&P 500 index up about 12% in 2026.

HYPERSCALERS ON THE HOT SEAT

Robust US profit growth has underpinned the stock market's gains this year in the face of headwinds including spiking Treasury yields and rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.

With more than 100 ​companies ​having posted results so far, third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to have climbed more than 32% ​from a year ago, according to LSEG IBES data. Next week is ‌the busiest of the reporting season.

"I think earnings will determine whether this ... tech pullback is a buying opportunity, or is there a deeper correction ahead," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management. "What we need is just another round of really strong earnings."

Story Continues

Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon's results are due Thursday. Focus will be on the guidance the companies give on capital spending plans and whether they are seeing returns on the massive outlays.

Capital spending from hyperscalers, expected to be around $800 billion this year, is boosting the bottom lines for a wide swath of companies involved in the AI buildout. But investors are wary of the sustainability of such spending amid mounting financing costs.

"Earnings are critical to the overall confidence level of the AI ‌trade and how much longer the spend will continue," said Kevin Mahn, president and chief investment officer at ​Hennion & Walsh Asset Management.

FED EXPECTED TO PAUSE ON RATES, FOR NOW

Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel and ​Sandisk also could influence the AI trade.

Elsewhere, other high-profile companies set to report next ​week include drugmaker Eli Lilly, oil majors Exxon and Chevron and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar.

The prospect for more interest rate hikes also comes into ‌focus with the Fed meeting. The Fed raised rates in September for the ​first time since 2023, in an effort to ​control above-target inflation, but Fed fund futures late on Thursday suggested only a 5% chance the Fed will hike again when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.

One factor: Investors are dubious that the Fed will want to increase rates just a week before the midterm elections.

However, markets are leaning toward a hike ​at the next meeting in December, with futures suggesting an 80% ‌probability of such a move then.

Walter Todd, chief investment officer at Greenwood Capital, said he will be watching for any hints about the rate path at Fed ​Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference following the decision.

"Does he say something to give an idea about December, because right now the expectation is there is going ​to be a hike?" Todd said.

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, editing by Colin Barr and David Gregorio)

news.Title: 史上最大包！台積電「員工運動會大紅包」每人平均領3萬元
news.Content:
薔琵颱風打亂晶圓代工龍頭台積電（2330）原訂本周六舉行的年度運動會，雖因天候因素與考量員工安全宣布取消，但員工期待的「運動會大紅包」並未被颱風打亂，據了解，台積電內部已發信通知，今年特別獎金將加碼至每人3萬元，創下歷史新高。

台積電董事長魏哲家先前曾指出，受惠公司營收與獲利持續創下新高，「不只今年，未來每一年都要創新高。」依循往年慣例，公司都會為同仁準備「小禮物」。回顧去年，凡符合資格的基層及中階員工（職級 60 至 64、20 至 26、31 至 33，含副理），每人均獲發 2.5 萬元特別獎金。

今年特別獎金再攀新高峰，人均金額直接跳升至3萬元。不過，根據過往，這份大紅包並非人人有獎，發放對象主要針對「基層員工」與「非主管職」。

若將台積電全球廠區（含台灣、美國、日本及中國大陸等海外子公司）的「基層員工（技術員與助理）」與「非主管職工程師及職員」全部加總，估計符合資格者超過8萬人，總計發放金額將超過24億元。

news.Title: Big Tech's capex spending looks different this year as Meta and Tesla save for later
news.Content:
When will investors see returns on all that AI spending? That's the nagging question facing tech companies quarter after quarter. The AI build-out sounds nice, but shareholders are craving returns on those investments.

The easiest way to improve margins, as any corporate consultant knows, is to watch spending. And in high-rate environments, spending less and showing financial discipline is rewarded even more.

Meta ( META ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and SpaceX ( SPCX ) did that for their near-term outlooks, which undershot expectations. That looks different, and welcome.

But it was short-lived: The costs were just moved to a different spot on the timeline.

Longer-term, off-balance-sheet spending plans of $825 billion for Meta and a $100 billion chip plant estimate for Tesla upended all the goodwill on Thursday — sending markets into a tizzy.

A gauge of Meta's credit risk surged to a new record and its bonds sank, Bloomberg reported, after the company said it would spend about $825 billion in the future on computing power, AI infrastructure, and other commitments.

Meanwhile, Elon Musk said the chip plant Tesla is building with SpaceX will need tens of billions of dollars in equipment through early 2028 and likely more than $100 billion over the long term.

Scaling robots and robotaxis, reusable rockets, and putting data centers in space are things that these companies do not currently do. So it should come as no surprise that it's going to be expensive. After all, that brief list probably has some of the most expensive-sounding things a person could conceive.

The bigger truth of these expenses, however, is that they're not yet on balance sheets and represent hopes for massive growth. In other words, hyper-bullish ambition.

Even as these companies showed some pleasingly responsible capex numbers on their latest earnings, Zuckerberg and Musk still need to sell their visions above all else.

All this stands in stark contrast to Apple ( AAPL ) and its tremendous rise this year . The company is sitting on its cash pile and watching its peers pour hundreds of billions of dollars into AI tech, proving the point in reverse. In the absence of meaningful AI profits and plenty of AI volatility, a stable hardware business has become Wall Street's favorite tech hedge.

Wall Street is fickle. And there's a fine line, apparently, between tech companies spending too much or too little on their AI dreams. Sometimes, pulling back on AI investment isn't received as more disciplined corporate finance, but as taking your foot off the gas pedal.

Story Continues

As Dan White, head of global equities at M&G Investments, put it, "When you see the hyperscalers pull back on capex spend, or maybe announce capex that's not as high as the market was anticipating, that's not great for the [AI ecosystem]."

Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban .

news.Title: 台積電一口氣蓋13座廠！日商伊藤忠殺進台灣 奪台工機龍頭51％股權
news.Content:
台積電擴廠帶動台灣半導體建廠商機，日本伊藤忠商事（Itochu Corporation）決定加碼布局台灣工程機械市場，計畫在今年底前收購日立建機旗下台灣銷售子公司永日建設機械51%股權，取得營運主導權，交易金額達數十億日圓，藉此搶占半導體廠房、資料中心帶來的設備需求。

《日經新聞》報導，台積電規劃未來數年間在台灣興建13座先進製程晶片廠與先進封裝廠，帶動營建工程及相關設備需求。隨著人工智慧、資料中心與半導體產業持續擴大投資，台灣工程機械市場的成長潛力也吸引日本商社積極布局。

報導指出，伊藤忠將斥資數十億日圓（約新台幣2.1億至8.5億元，最終以實際收購金額而定），取得永日建設機械51%股權。完成收購後，日立建機將保留其餘49%股權，雙方持續合作拓展工程機械業務。

永日建設機械總部位於桃園，在桃園、台中、高雄及花蓮設有4個營運據點，服務範圍涵蓋全台。伊藤忠透過取得經營主導權，可望進一步擴大在台灣工程設備銷售與相關服務的布局。

除了搶攻新設備需求，伊藤忠商事也計畫整合工程機械銷售、維修保養及設備租賃等服務，提升客戶支援能力，並與日立建機深化合作，擴大工程機械從設備供應到售後服務的價值鏈。

隨著半導體廠房、人工智慧資料中心及公共基礎設施投資持續推進，工程機械業者不僅有望受惠設備需求增加，也可透過維修與租賃服務拓展營收來源。伊藤忠此次收購，正是看準台灣建設投資帶來的長期商機，期望藉由整合資源提升永日建設機械的企業價值與獲利能力。

news.Title: SpaceX may not follow Meta's bold plan to raise money for AI
news.Content:
Don't expect SpaceX ( SPCX ) to surprise investors like Meta ( META ) did this week by saying it would issue new stock to help fund its AI buildout efforts.

"Importantly, in our discussion w/management, SPCX also said that it is not considering raising equity," said JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth in a new post-earnings note on Friday. "Capital requirements are front and center across the market, and SPCX indicated it has a number of available pools of capital on the debt side."

SpaceX gave investors a taste of what could be to come on the debt funding front in its earnings report this week.

Execs guided to $35 billion to $40 billion in capex for the fourth quarter. This would be a meaningful step-up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, $18.4 billion in the second quarter and $10.1 billion in the first quarter.

SpaceX ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

On the earnings call, the company's veteran CFO Bret Johnson didn't seem fazed by the tremors in the debt markets of late on concerns over the financial health of neoclouds such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ).

All systems go on the pursuit of capital, or so it appears.

SpaceX is reportedly eyeing a capital raise of $40 billion with financial powerhouses Goldman Sachs and Apollo.

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years (particularly in the AI segment)," Moffettnathson analyst Julie Zhu said. "SpaceX has moved at a frenetic pace over the last few months, closing the Cursor acquisition; announcing a new Starbase in Louisiana; winning yet another large IaaS contract; launching Starship flight 14; and purchasing Grain's 800 MHz spectrum. Each of these announcements portends an enormous amount of spending, both capex and opex, ahead."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq wobble after sharp tech sell-off

This week's earnings headliners, SpaceX ( SPCX ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Meta ( META ), all declined.

news.Title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 32% of Berkshire Hathaway's $364 Billion Portfolio Invested in 3 Unstoppable AI Stocks
news.Content:
This has been a year of immense change for Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) and its investors. After more than half a century at the helm, the iconic Warren Buffett retired as CEO on Dec. 31, paving the way for Greg Abel to take over.

It took Abel mere months to completely reshape Berkshire's $364 billion portfolio . He dumped 16 stocks in the first quarter and has brought a tech focus to the company's investment portfolio that hadn't existed under the Oracle of Omaha. Today, three unstoppable artificial intelligence (AI) stocks account for roughly 32% ($115.7 billion) of Berkshire's portfolio: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG), and Bending Spoons (NASDAQ:BSP).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Warren Buffett's Dec. 31 retirement turned the proverbial keys over to Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

Apple: $78.28 billion (21.5% of invested assets)

For the better part of the last decade, Apple has been Berkshire's top holding by market value. Warren Buffett piled into Apple because he appreciated the brand's loyal customer base and favored the company's market-leading share buyback program.

But Apple is in the midst of a multi-year transformation that emphasizes higher-margin subscription services and AI. Prior to his own recent retirement as CEO, Tim Cook shifted Apple's focus to services designed to enhance existing customer loyalty and bolster margins. Double-digit sales growth in the company's services segment should lessen the revenue peaks and valleys commonly seen with major iPhone upgrade cycles.

There's also Apple Intelligence, which is the company's generative AI built directly into its operating systems. Embracing these tools should make its physical devices (iPhone, Mac, and iPad) considerably more attractive.

Alphabet: $36 billion (9.9% of invested assets, both share classes combined)

Perhaps the biggest change in the wake of Buffett's retirement has been Abel's aggressive purchases of Google parent Alphabet. Though Buffett initiated this position before his retirement, Abel more than tripled it in the first quarter and purchased around $17 billion in additional stock in the second quarter.

Alphabet possesses the sustainable moat that Berkshire's current and former bosses often seek out. In September, Google accounted for 90% of global internet search traffic. Maintaining a virtual monopoly in internet search affords the company exceptional ad-pricing power.

Story Continues

But it's Alphabet's AI ambitions that are really turning heads. Since Alphabet began integrating generative AI and large language model capabilities into Google Cloud, sales for this significantly higher-margin operating segment have soared. In the June-ended quarter, Google Cloud's year-over-year revenue growth accelerated to 82%!

Image source: Getty Images.

Bending Spoons: $1.44 billion (0.4% of invested assets)

The third unstoppable AI stock that, alongside Apple and Alphabet, collectively makes up 32% of Berkshire Hathaway's $364 billion investment portfolio is the Italian-based tech- and AI-focused acquisition company Bending Spoons.

Last week, Berkshire Hathaway worked out a deal to acquire an additional 10 million shares of Bending Spoons via a private placement at $33 per share. This comes atop Berkshire's initial investment at the company's July initial public offering.

Bending Spoons has acquired several mature tech and digital businesses, including AOL and Vimeo. It develops software and relies on AI, among other factors, to make these businesses more efficient and generate sustainable subscription sales. It's a relatively low-cost/high-margin operating model that's now well-funded, thanks in part to Warren Buffett's successor.

news.Title: 台股下週慘了？ 陳重銘揭「3大利空」：先別想衝5萬點
news.Content:
週四費城半導體暴跌6.7%，台積電ADR重挫4.5%，台指期夜盤更是大跌超過580點，讓下周台股面臨沉重壓力。市場賣壓主要源於三大利空。陳重銘建議投資人應做好資產配置，切勿盲目追高，可適度轉向低本益比的金融股以降低波動。

Meta資本支出吃掉現金流

不敗教主陳重銘在臉書發文表示，第一大利空源自科技巨頭Meta的財務數據。Meta第三季營收雖然達到646億美元、年增26%，但單季自由現金流卻呈現負21.2億美元。這項數據被市場解讀為龐大的AI投資已經開始侵蝕現金流。陳重銘說明，自由現金流量是企業在維持日常營運與必要資本支出後，實際留在手上可自由支配的現金，正數可用於發放股利、償還債務或再投資；當科技巨頭短期砸下巨額資本支出時，自由現金流可能轉負，後續重點在於未來能回收多少回報。

黃仁勳點出新型雲端業者資金缺口

第二大利空來自輝達執行長黃仁勳的發言。黃仁勳指出新型雲端業者的需求呈現「好到爆表」的情形，但同時也發出警告，表示資金不足將會阻礙這些業者的成長。這番言論被市場解讀為整體AI產業鏈面臨「缺錢」問題，致使市場開始重新檢驗AI產業的成長性。

美伊局勢緊張與通膨升息疑慮

第三大利空則是地緣政治風險升溫。根據《紐約時報》報導，美國與以色列計畫在11月3期中選舉後對伊朗發動新一輪打擊。這項消息導致國際油價上漲，引發市場對通膨再度回升的擔憂，進而預期聯準會年底前可能再升息1碼，這對整體經濟與股市發展均屬不利因素。

市場資金轉向與台股投資策略

這波賣壓主要集中在科技類股，道瓊指數則仍維持收小紅，顯示市場資金已明顯從科技股轉向防禦型與傳統產業類股。對於台股投資人而言，後續可持續觀察周五與下周一的美股走勢，若能止跌反彈將是積極訊號。不過陳重銘提醒，最近股市上檔壓力明顯，投資人暫時不要想著衝5萬點，而是要做好投資組合配置，不要將資金全部壓在AI科技股，適度分攤至獲利成長且低本益比的金融股，才能降低資產波動，穩健前行。

news.Title: 台積電打折賣、華經飆漲停！台股31檔撿便宜 連假後別慌
news.Content:
台股意外因颱風假形成四天連假，暫時躲過今（23日）日的恐慌性賣壓，隨著日韓股陸續出現抗跌力道，加上美股期貨止跌，可稍稍化解投資人的擔憂。展望下周行情，分析師林漢偉認為可以鎖定4大資金避風港，塑化、航運、電信及資安族群，並伺機布局「打折」的優質企業。

台股周年慶 優質好股最低打7折？

摩爾投顧分析師林漢偉於直播中指出，Meta未來支出承諾高達8250億美元，且自由現金流轉負，引發人工智慧產業的融資疑慮，使科技股重挫，資金轉進內需消費族群，包括民生消費、醫療保健及公用事業等，重災區落在半導體、光通訊及記憶體。

選股上，林漢偉強調，當市場大跌應先求穩再求好，台積電、台達電、台光電、日月光、欣興及奇鋐等具備技術護城河的指標大廠，從今年高點下殺至10月低點約10%至30%，形成打九折與七折狀況，若信任人工智慧的長線發展，此時是布局時機。

老AI逢低布局 高殖利率就選它們

除此之外，高價股跌深且具技術利多的標的則包括信驊、川湖、穎崴、旺矽、世芯-ky、聯亞、光聖、貿聯-KY及智邦；消費性電子族群則有聯發科、大立光、華通、南亞科、華邦電、上銀、華碩及微星。

若是高殖利率族群，林漢偉點名記憶體模組族群與老AI伺服器，威剛、創見、十銓及宇瞻；技嘉、廣達、鴻海及緯創，皆是投資人可以在大盤回落之際，考慮分批布局的個股。

4大資金避風港 分析師曝操作

資金轉入避險族群，傳產與資安題材將是市場關注焦點，林漢偉指出，塑化股與航運股將是短線的避風港，觀察指標為台塑化、台塑、南亞、台化等；航運族群則有萬海、長榮及陽明等。

資安族群方面，林漢偉認為，PHP資安危機升溫，華經就因此飆上漲停，「觀察指標在華經，10月才開始起漲，籌碼相對乾淨，建議大家盡量選擇交易量大的個股，包括華經、驊宏資及東捷資訊等，下周可以考慮的標的。」

news.Title: Better Memory Stock: Micron vs. Sandisk
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) are members of an elite club. Only four stocks in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) have tripled or more so far in 2026. Micron and Sandisk make up half that group.

Sandisk has been the bigger winner by far this year. But that performance is water under the bridge. Which is the better memory stock to buy now?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Two different kinds of memory stocks

Micron and Sandisk are similar in some respects. However, they're two very different kinds of memory stocks.

The most important difference between the two companies is the types of memory they focus on. Micron makes high-bandwidth memory (HBM), dynamic random access memory (DRAM), and NAND memory. Sandisk specializes in NAND flash memory.

HBM is Micron's crown jewel these days. In the company's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, HBM revenue growth exceeded total revenue growth. Management said that it has completed sales agreements "for the vast majority" of its 2027 calendar-year HBM supply at significantly higher prices than it obtained in 2026.

Sandisk's NAND flash focus has worked to its benefit, though. Surging NAND prices have allowed the company to capture the full upside without any dilution from memory chips that aren't experiencing as strong demand.

But artificial intelligence (AI) serves as a massive tailwind for both companies. Memory is critical to AI applications. In particular, the shift to inference and the rising adoption of agentic AI are driving significant demand for multiple types of memory.

By the numbers: how Micron and Sandisk compare

Micron is much bigger than Sandisk. Its market cap tops $1 trillion, making Micron one of the world's top 10 largest technology companies . Meanwhile, Sandisk's market cap is around $200 billion.

Unsurprisingly, Micron also makes more money than Sandisk. In its latest quarter, Micron reported revenue of $54.2 billion and earnings of $37.7 billion. Sandisk's revenue in its latest quarter was $8.97 billion, with earnings of $6.9 billion.

Both companies boast impressive growth. In its fiscal 2026 Q4, Sandisk's revenue soared 372% year over year and 51% quarter over quarter. Micron's fiscal Q4 revenue jumped 379% year over year and roughly 31% quarter over quarter.

Micron and Sandisk are cyclical stocks, which is reflected in their valuations. Micron's shares trade at only seven times forward earnings, while Sandisk's forward earnings multiple is 8x.

Story Continues

Wall Street likes both memory stocks, although the bullish views seem somewhat stronger for Micron. Of the 29 analysts who rated Micron over the past three months, 27 (93%) recommended buying the stock. The consensus 12-month price target for Micron reflects a potential upside of around 74%. Of the 17 analysts who rated Sandisk over the past three months, 15 (88%) recommended buying the stock. The average price target for Sandisk is roughly 60% above the current share price.

The verdict

Both Micron and Sandisk could (and probably will) continue to deliver exceptional returns over the next few years. But I think that Micron is the better memory stock overall.

While Sandisk's pure-play NAND focus is its greatest strength, it's also the company's most significant risk. If NAND prices fall, Sandisk's revenue and profits will sink. Micron faces risks, too, but its breadth across multiple types of memory should provide some cushion.

I also think that Micron could have a bigger long-term opportunity. In particular, I'm excited about the company's prospects in the humanoid robotics market. Humanoid robots require enormous low-power memory. Micron is investing to meet expected demand and believes it will enjoy "a sustained, substantial multi-decade memory demand cycle" beginning later this decade.

My verdict aligns with Wall Street's take on these two stocks. Micron is the better pick right now.

news.Title: Hedge fund returns worsen this week as tech selloff deepens
news.Content:
By Summer Zhen and Anirban Sen

HONG KONG, New York Oct 23 (Reuters) - Global hedge funds were hit by a fresh tech reckoning this week, with major strategies ‌posting their worst day since the COVID-era market rout.

A renewed selloff in big tech ‌stocks, driven by growing skepticism over the massive AI buildout spending, swept through global markets and dealt a heavy ​blow to global hedge funds.

"If last Thursday felt bad, today has been worse," Goldman Sachs' prime brokerage team said in a note sent to clients.

All three major strategies tracked by Goldman Sachs lost more than 1% on October 22, a first since the COVID pandemic, with losses spanning fundamental equity ‌long-short, systematic and multi-strategy funds.

One ⁠catalyst for the latest selloff was Meta, one of the hyperscalers spending billions to build AI models, after the company said it would issue a ⁠new class of shares to help it raise funds.

Meta Platforms slumped 7% on Thursday, its largest drop since July. Nvidia tumbled 4%, while the broader Nasdaq Composite lost 2.6%, its largest decline since June ​5.

Asian stocks, ​from South Korea to China, were also at ​the center of the selloff, pressured by ‌higher oil prices and fears over hefty AI spending.

The downturn triggered deleveraging among hedge funds, market participants said, as losses in crowded AI-linked trades forced investors to cut exposure and rein in risk.

Global fundamental long-short funds, or stock pickers, have dropped 3.8% so far in October, but are still up 8.8% year-to-date, Goldman Sachs estimates.

Performance was weighed down by losses on China and ‌technology holdings, as well as a squeeze in crowded ​short positions, the bank said.

Tech-focused and Asia-focused hedge funds were ​among the biggest losers this month ​through to October 22, down roughly 10% and 9%, respectively, according to ‌Goldman.

Masaki Gotoh, a partner at Tokyo-based TriVista Capital, ​said the hedge fund ​had trimmed its hardware investments since late June.

"I'm actually a very strong believer in AI... But the concentration level is staggering. If you go back to the IT dotcom ​bubble, that had similar types ‌of concentrations and we saw that happen. The circular financing is also a source ​of some concern," he said.

(Reporting by Summer Zhen and Anirban Sen, additional reporting ​by Rocky Swift in TokyoEditing by Shri Navaratnam)

news.Title: 黃仁勳一句話引爆賣壓？陳重銘揭3大利空：台股要小心
news.Content: 意外多了一天颱風假，接連四天連假，台股下週走勢備受關注！美股科技股遭遇賣壓，費城半導體指數（費半）重挫約6.7%，台積電ADR（TSM）也下跌約4.5%，AI概念股面臨估值修正壓力。 財經專家「不敗教主」陳重銘 分析，這波賣壓主要來自AI投資成本攀升、資金疑慮升溫，以及美伊衝突可能推升油價等 3大利空 。他提醒，台股近期上檔壓力浮現，投資人不宜急著期待5萬點行情，更應檢視持股配置，適度分散至獲利穩健、評價相對合理的金融股。 【AI投資燒錢！Meta營收成長仍引發疑慮】 陳重銘指出，第一個利空來自科技巨頭AI投資成本持續攀升。Meta（META）公布2026年第三季財報，營收達646.01億美元，年增26%，但自由現金流卻轉為負21.2億美元，讓市場重新檢視AI投資的回收速度。根據Meta公布的財報，當季資本支出約349.1億美元，已高於營業活動現金流入的327.9億美元。\ 自由現金流是企業扣除必要資本支出後，能夠靈活運用的現金，可用於還債、發放股利或投入新事業。當企業大舉擴建AI資料中心、購買晶片及相關設備時，即使營收持續成長，自由現金流仍可能短期轉負。 問題在於，鉅額投資未來能否帶來相應的獲利成長。當市場開始懷疑AI投資報酬率，科技股即使基本面不差，也可能因估值過高而遭到修正。 【黃仁勳談資金壓力！AI產業鏈遭重新檢視】 第二個利空是AI產業的資金需求。陳重銘提到，輝達（NVIDIA，NVDA）執行長黃仁勳曾談及新型雲端業者需求強勁，同時也提醒資金不足可能限制業者成長。 這番話凸顯AI產業的另一項挑戰：市場需求雖然旺盛，但建置算力、擴充資料中心及購買高階晶片都需要龐大資金。若業者融資成本上升，或無法持續取得資金，擴張速度與未來獲利就可能受到影響。 近期市場也開始擔心，AI產業的投資規模不斷擴大，相關企業卻未必能在短期內創造足夠的現金流與報酬，進而引發科技股賣壓。 【美伊衝突添變數！油價與升息壓力升溫】 第三個利空來自地緣政治風險。外媒報導，美國與以色列正在研擬美國期中選舉後可能對伊朗採取新一輪軍事行動的方案，讓市場擔憂中東局勢再度升溫，進一步推高國際油價。 油價上漲不只會增加企業生產與運輸成本，也可能讓通膨更難降溫。市場因此重新評估聯準會（Fed）後續利率政策，升息預期升高，對仰賴未來獲利支撐估值的科技股尤其不利。 【別急著喊台股5萬點！不敗教主曝配置策略】 陳重銘認為，這波賣壓主要集中在科技股，反映市場開始重新評估AI投資成本及未來報酬。台股與美國科技股連動程度高，若費半持續走弱，台股短線仍可能承受壓力。

news.Title: 以為相對低點！ 新手小白「買完一路跌」 網見持股傻眼：也太碎
news.Content: 今年上半年台股屢屢上漲，但近期震盪加劇，讓投資新手感到徬徨，有網友表示自己初入股市不久，原以為買在相對低檔，未料買入後一路走跌，讓他猶豫該繼續攤平還是停損出場。 該名網友在論壇Dcard上以「高位前輩會怎麼操作」為圖發文求教，表示自己剛開始投資股票，買了不少個股，原本自認都買在相對低點，但發現買了之後股價卻一路往下，文中也貼出自己的持股明細，包含聯電（2303）、台達電（2308）、國巨*（2327）、台積電（2330）、環科（2413）、京元電子（2449）、銘異（3060）、中美晶（5483）、環球晶（6488）及愛普*（6531）等10檔個股。從截圖可看出持股全數呈現綠字，其中聯電、銘異及環球晶的帳面跌幅超過17%，銘異更下跌24.10%。雖然目前虧損金額不多，但他仍想了解，遇到這種「買了股價就往下走」的情況，比較建議繼續攤平，還是到某個點之後就要認賠出場？ ▼原PO表示自己是股市新手，買了10檔個股，股價卻一路往下，感到懊惱與不解，也不知未來該如何調整投資策略。（示意圖／AI生成） 此案例吸引許多網留言討論，有網友認為原PO的持股過於分散，建議本金有限的投資新手不要同時持有多檔個股，應調整，先從大盤ETF著手較穩妥：「本金少就不要買那麼多檔了」、「幹嘛買那麼雜，買超過10檔的，長期下來都是賠」、「這太碎了，本金少的情況下先集中買單一股，累積多了再去投下一支標的，建議投ETF大盤，0050、00878這種的，月配跟季配」、「全部賣掉改買0050跟009826」、「全賣，趁回檔買0050穩盤，買00913、00935衝積效」。 ▼不少網友認為原PO是本金不多的投資新手，就不要買太多個股，先投ETF跟著大盤走比較穩。（示意圖／AI生成） 也有網友認為，如果看好特定公司的長期發展，還是可以買個股，不過不要太多，可以選1至2檔標的，在股價下跌時分批加碼，並賣出其他不看好的持股：「選1-2檔看好的往下攤，其他全砍」、「除了台積電跟台達電，其他都賣一賣，之後只買0050」、「如是我、只留台積電 集中台積電與1、2檔市值型ET」。 還有另一派網友還是看好台股後續走勢，建議原PO保持耐心：「放著什麼都不會改變，加碼拉低成本，反彈一下就回本了」、「沒有什麼是真正的低點，看的是長期，如果公司好一直賺錢就會一路上漲，短期只是籌碼洗來洗去而已 ，你買的時候想一下你買進的理由是什麼，決定好再進場就比較不會遲疑了」。

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉三大指數開低走高 滬指一度失守3600點 創業板指終止九連黑
news.Content:
中國A股三大股指今(23)日開低走高，上證指數( SSEC ) 結束連2日跌勢，盤中一度失守3600點，創業板指亦終止連跌9日頹勢，本周滬指累跌0.69%，深證成指累跌1.09%，創業板指累跌3.18%

滬指今日收漲0.89%至3690.48點，深證成指( SZI ) 收高2.79%，報11673.83點，創業板指收紅4.16%至2684.1點，滬深兩市成交額人民幣1.96兆元，較前一天放量逾4200億元。

盤面上，人形機器人族群大漲，宇樹科技漲停，本週累漲逾46%，大業股連6天漲停，福萊新材出現5個交易來第3根漲停板，華陽智能、正裕工業、襄陽軸承連2日亮燈，宇樹科技，萬向錢潮、山東威達、派斯林、大豐實業漲停；科創次新股表現亮眼，燧原科技、沐曦股份、摩爾線程等多股漲超10%；晶片股回暖，粵芯半導體、利亞德、奧普特等多股漲停；大金融類股拉升，匯金科技、華林證券、大智慧漲停；影視院線族群走高，中廣天擇、慈文傳媒漲停。

下跌族群方面，電力類股走勢較弱，閩東電力、皖能電力、黔源電力紛紛下挫；銀行族群震盪回落，中國銀行跌超4%，工商銀行、建設銀行跌超3%，農業銀行、江蘇銀行、交通銀行亦跟跌。

消息面上，OpenAI切入人形機器人賽道，執行長奧特曼稱該公司正組建名為「OpenAI Robotics」的新團隊，並公開招募全端硬體、營運、系統及機器學習工程師。本周一(19日)，特斯拉向美國證交會(SEC)提交2026年年度股東大會相關文件，特斯拉在同期提交的年度股東報告中明確表示，第三代Optimus人形機器人已為大規模量產做好準備。

此外，國際顧問機構弗若斯特沙利文近日公布《2026年全球人形機器人市場研究報告》，揭露業界最新產銷數據。今年上半年全球人形機器人銷售達3.6萬台，已超越去年全年3.5萬台的規模，同期市場營收為5.4億美元，產業商業化進程明顯加速。

中信證券表示，當下市場風險偏好、情緒接近冰點，三季報在本月中陸續披露，A股市場可望進行主題投資行情風格切換。此外，機器人流動性、估值、政策、技術、鏈主等催化大都符合過去七輪機器人上漲行情特徵，因此，從策略角度來看，中信證券認為機器人主題行情目前已具備啟動條件。

中歐基金出具研報指出，當前市場處於情緒冰點附近的高波動階段，但需區分兩層邏輯：全球長端利率高位、油價與地緣擾動疊加存量資金調倉，屬於估值與流動性層面的衝擊，往往帶來非線性的殺跌；海外AI資本開支仍在上行，記憶體與算力供給偏緊等線索並修緊，等潛在客戶反映動人的威脅性趨勢。
