news.Title: 台積電護城河有多深？ 英特爾技術長揭「難追關鍵」：不只比技術
news.Content: AI算力需求持續飆升，全球半導體產業卻面臨設備供應跟不上需求的難題。英特爾技術長Pushkar Ranade近日接受Dwarkesh Podcast訪問時直言，即使資金不設上限，全球先進晶圓產能也不可能增加10倍，最多大約只能翻倍。問題不在電晶體設計，而是EUV曝光機、半導體製程設備、無塵室與晶圓廠建置速度都受到限制。 Ranade指出，全球每年交付的EUV設備不到100套，部分設備從下訂到交貨約需18個月，新廠擴建更可能耗時數年。這代表AI業者即使願意投入鉅資，也未必能立即換得更多晶片產能。當AI運算需求與實體製造能力出現落差，半導體競爭的核心，已從單純比拚技術，轉向設備供應、資本投入與量產效率的全面較量。 台積電規模優勢持續擴大 Ranade認為，英特爾與台積電真正難以拉近的差距，在於長期累積的規模經濟。晶圓廠建成後，約80%的成本屬於固定成本，因此產能利用率與良率每提高一些，都可能帶來可觀的經濟效益。台積電憑藉龐大的全球客戶群與先進晶圓產量，能將廠房、設備等成本分攤到更多晶圓上；英特爾過去則主要為自家產品生產晶片，近年才積極拓展外部晶圓代工業務。 依訪談內容，台積電先進晶圓產量超過英特爾3倍，2026年資本支出約500億美元，英特爾則約200億美元。台積電也持續擴大市場領先地位，《TrendForce》統計，台積電2026年第二季晶圓代工營收市占率達72.5%，三星電子以5.9%居次。對英特爾而言，即使製程技術逐步追近，若無法提高產能利用率、擴大客戶基礎並改善良率，龐大的固定成本仍可能成為競爭包袱。 High-NA EUV成關鍵分水嶺！ 先進設備的價值，也取決於各家晶片製造商採用的技術架構。英特爾製程主管Chris Auth指出，High-NA EUV曝光機透過提高數值孔徑，可在單次曝光中印出更精細的圖案，但設備價格極高，必須能減少多重曝光需求，才有機會證明投資效益。訪談估算，High-NA曝光機連同相關支援設備，整套系統約需4億美元。英特爾採用背面供電架構，將電源線移至晶圓背面，釋出正面佈線空間，因此認為High-NA有助降低曝光次數；台積電的製程架構不同，導入效益也不相同。 另一方面，英特爾過去曾因10奈米製程導入過多新技術而延誤進度，如今改採階段關卡審查，要求技術先達到良率、缺陷與效能標準，再進入下一階段。英特爾也計畫讓14A製程從一開始就提供較成熟的製程設計套件（PDK），改善18A初期在客戶設計工具與流程上的不足，爭取外部客戶信任。 技術只差幾個百分點 Ranade反駁英特爾與台積電之間仍存在整整一個世代的技術差距，認為雙方在效能、功耗與晶片密度等指標上，可能只差幾個百分點，但他強調，能否準時交貨、維持高良率並快速擴大產量，比單一技術指標更重要。英特爾規劃從18A邁向14A，部分既有設備可望沿用，有助降低新節點的設備需求與導入成本；不過，外部客戶是否願意採用，仍取決於製程成熟度、設計工具、交付可靠性與量產表現。 先進封裝也成為另一個戰場，英特爾持續發展EMIB與Foveros等技術，台積電則以CoWoS等方案服務AI晶片客戶，並已表態願意協助部分原先選擇英特爾封裝、卻面臨供應限制的客戶。從曝光機短缺到晶圓廠固定成本，再到封裝與客戶生態系，英特爾追趕台積電的挑戰不只是製程技術，而是能否建立可持續擴張的製造體系。

news.Title: Stock Market News for Oct 23, 2026
news.Content:
U.S. stock markets closed predominantly lower on Thursday as artificial intelligence (AI) trade plummeted. Market participants remained deeply concerned about the sustainability of gigantic spending on AI data centers. Higher crude oil prices significantly dented investors' sentiment. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite ended sharply lower while the Dow managed to post a marginal gain.

How Did the Benchmarks Perform?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) gained 11.89 points to close at 52,867.98 after a choppy session. Notably, 20 components of the 30-stock index ended in positive territory, while 10 ended in negative territory. At the intraday low, the blue-chip index was down 347.71 points.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ended at 26,008.86, plunging 2.6% or 694 points on sharp decline in AI bigwigs. The tech-laden index suffered its worst single-day performance since early June. The S&P 500 tumbled 1.2% to finish at 7,663.43.

However, seven out of 11 sectors of the broad-market index ended in positive territory while four finished in negative territory. The Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) rose 1.7%. On the other hand, the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR (XLC) fell 1.1%.

The fear gauge CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) jumped 14.1% to 19.03. A total of 18.79 billion shares were traded on Thursday, higher than the last 20-session average of 17.19 billion. Advancers outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq, a 1.37-to-1 ratio favored declining issues.

AI Trade Plunges

Giant AI hyperscaler and social media behemoth Meta Platforms Inc. META reported strong third-quarter 2026 earnings results. Revenues increased 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $63.4 billion. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $7.40, well above the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $6.52.

Advertisement revenues jumped 28% annually. Advertisement impressions and price per advertisement climbed in double digits year over year as AI continues to optimize its products. However, the most concerning fact is that META reported its first quarterly outflow of free cash flow in its history.

In the reported quarter, Meta platforms lost $2.12 billion of free cash flow compared with a positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion. In the third quarter, the company spent $34.91 billion on AI capex. META hiked the lower end of its 2026 AI capex guidance to $135-145 billion from $130-145 billion reported earlier.

META also plans to issue nonvoting shares to fund AI investments without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Market participants remained highly concerned about the company's solid financial condition. Consequently, stock price of META tumbled 7%.

Story Continues

Other AI infrastructure giants like NVIDIA Corp. NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD and Micron Technology Inc. MU shed 4%, 8% and 6%, respectively. NVIDIA and Micron currently sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Spike in Crude Oil Prices

Crude oil prices reached a five-month high following the news that Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure. As a result, the international benchmark - Brent crude futures - rose 4% to settle at $113.17 per barrel. The U.S. benchmark - West Texas Intermediate crude futures - rose 2.4% to settle at $99.47 per barrel.

Economic Data

The Conference Board reported that the leading indicator was unchanged in September after a 0.1% decline in August. The Zacks Consensus Estimate also remained flat.

The Department of Labor reported that initial claims decreased by 6,000 to 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 17, below the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 197,000. The previous week's data was revised marginally upward to 200,000 from 199,000 reported earlier.

Continuing claims (those who have already received government aid and reported a week behind) increased 25,000 to 1.728 million for the week ended Oct. 10. The previous week's level was revised downward by 7,000 to 1,703,000 from 1,710,000 reported earlier.

news.Title: 台股逃過一劫？ 日股跌幅收斂、韓翻紅 「這巨頭」大漲逾4%
news.Content:
受到AI巨頭Meta資本支出攀升疑慮加劇，以及年期信用違約交換報價創近一年以來最高，美股費半指數重挫，影響日韓股市今（23）日同步下挫，日經225指數一度大跌逾1400點，創近三個月新低；韓股KOSPI指數也一度下跌逾4%，不過隨著低接買盤進駐，日韓股午後跌幅明顯收斂，終場收跌214點，來到62693點；韓股收盤成功翻紅小漲0.3%，SK海力士也由黑翻紅勁揚4.42%。

日股盤中重挫逾1400點

日股今早延續日前頹勢，日經225指數盤中最低落至6萬1000點區間，一度重挫超過1400點，創7月底以來盤中新低；22日甚至下跌逾1700點，若與21日收盤價相比，兩日累計跌幅一度突破3000點；不過，午後隨著買盤進場，跌幅明顯收斂，終場收跌214點，來到62693點，跌幅0.34%。

news.Title: Meta Is Doing Something It’s Never Done Before. Here’s What It Means for Investors.
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is one of the main companies driving the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Though you may know Meta best for its social media apps -- from Instagram to WhatsApp -- the company has expanded its focus in recent years to include AI research and development.

These businesses actually fit well together -- with AI improving and enhancing the apps, users may spend more time on them. As a result, advertisers might buy more ad placement across these platforms. Meanwhile, Meta's AI tools are leading to new revenue streams. But all of this comes with a price. Meta has invested billions of dollars into R&D to achieve its AI goals, and investors haven't always been happy about these levels of spending.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Right now, though, Meta is doing something it's never done before, and this move could help fund its AI projects. Let's find out what all of this means for investors.

Image source: Getty Images.

The Meta story so far

First, a quick note on Meta's business and earnings picture so far. The company generates most of its revenue through advertising across its social media apps, and over time, this has helped earnings to climb. In the recent quarter, revenue advanced in the double digits to $64 billion, and net income came in at $9.8 billion. (This was a triple-digit gain, but it isn't particularly relevant as it was due to a change in a tax rate.)

Importantly, the company said its AI investments are already boosting ad revenue through stronger engagement and improved recommendations.

As mentioned, Meta has made spending on AI a top priority over the past few years. The company has built out its own data centers, developed AI models, and even created a superintelligence lab led by industry experts. All of this has pushed capital expenditures higher quarter after quarter. And this has weighed on free cash flow.

META Capital Expenditures (Quarterly) data by YCharts

In the latest quarter, Meta said that capex primarily went toward servers, data centers, and network infrastructure. The company narrowed its 2026 capex range to $135 billion to $145 billion from the prior outlook of $130 billion to $145 billion and said that into the future it will "continue investing aggressively."

Now, let's consider the fresh move Meta's about to make. For the first time, the company has announced a stock split . The operation is a bit different from a standard split, in which a company issues more of the same class of shares to current shareholders.

Story Continues

Preserving Mark Zuckerberg's power

Instead, Meta is creating a new class of shares, Class C shares that don't have voting rights. The company will offer one of these shares to current shareholders for each share they already own. As a result, this will double the share count, but it won't interfere with chief executive officer Mark Zuckerberg's voting power.

The move is particularly positive for the company and shareholders because it offers more financing flexibility, and at a time when investors are concerned about Meta's investment in the AI build-out. For example, Meta could sell new Class C shares to the public to raise cash, without diluting Zuckerberg's holding. The company also could decide to use Class C shares instead of cash to pay for a potential acquisition or offer employees such shares. So, this decision offers Meta attractive new ways to raise cash and bring in and keep talent. That's positive for the company as it reduces financial risk and maintains Zuckerberg's leadership.

As with a traditional stock split, this operation doesn't change anything fundamental such as market value. It will unfold on Jan. 19, and it will be paid to current shareholders in the form of a dividend. As essentially a 2-for-1 stock split, the value of the stock, based on the Oct. 21 closing price of $697, would be $348 after the operation. Of course, this value could change greatly depending on the stock's performance up until that time.

Though the stock split itself may be a non-event for investors, Meta's post-split financial flexibility is good news, reinforcing the buy case for this top tech player.

news.Title: SK海力士反彈！科技股賣壓降溫 韓股翻紅、亞股跌幅收斂
news.Content:
南韓晶片製造商SK海力士(SK Hynix)周五(23日)股價走勢震盪，該公司表示在評估近期市場情勢後，決定暫緩旗下美國子公司Solidigm赴美首次公開發行(IPO)計畫，股價開低走高、反彈漲逾4%，韓股跟著翻紅，亞股跌幅收斂。

全球科技股賣壓周五在亞洲市場稍稍降溫，MSCI除日本外亞太股市指數周五一度下跌0.8%，之後因逢低買盤進場而收復失土，截稿前大致持平。不過，該指數本周預料連續第四周收黑。

南韓KOSPI指數則在盤中一度下跌4%後，勉力轉為上漲0.3%。日本日經指數下跌0.3%，本周跌幅約4%。

中國A股藍籌股在跌至2025年7月以來低點後獲得買盤支撐，滬深300指數上漲0.8%。香港恆生指數也上漲0.7%，扭轉周四下跌3%的跌勢。

AMP副首席經濟學家Diana Mousina說：「目前還很難對整體股市過度看空，因為企業獲利仍在成長，實體經濟數據也維持穩健。這一切意味著，AI交易熱潮未必已經結束，但正在改變。市場不再是『什麼都買』的局面。」

Solidigm赴美IPO喊卡

SK海力士早盤股價一度下跌3%，但午盤後反彈漲逾4%。SK海力士周五發布聲明表示，評估近期資本市場情勢與股價走勢後，Solidigm將暫停評估上市前募資及IPO等選項。該公司同時正在探索各種融資方式，以因應AI記憶體需求持續成長，並為在美國興建新的半導體晶圓廠籌措資金。

SK海力士表示，Solidigm若能上市，原本有助於為業務擴張提供資金，並提高財務彈性，讓公司能透過發放股利、買回股票及註銷股票等方式回饋股東。

不過，金融市場波動加劇導致半導體類股普遍回檔，這使SK海力士重新評估，IPO是否有利於現有股東。

SK海力士另表示，Solidigm現有生產設施的產能有限，難以滿足AI帶動的記憶體需求成長，凸顯在美國增建產能的必要性。

南韓監管機關聚焦雙重上市規定

據路透報導，南韓金融監管機關周一表示，Solidigm若在美國上市，可能違反南韓限制雙重上市的規定。

南韓金融監督院院長李燦鎮(Lee Chan-jin)表示，監管機關正在檢視這項IPO是否須依照南韓相關規定接受審查，以保障少數股東權益。

對此SK海力士表示，Solidigm的投資需求維持不變，未來將持續尋求其他融資方式，以支持子公司成長並提升股東價值。

news.Title: Take Five: AI trade meets the Fed
news.Content:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - An eye-catching week is in store as rate-setters at the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan announce policy decisions, while investors will gauge whether results from Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft can fuel the next leg of the AI rally.

An election in Brazil, a gathering ‌of China's top leadership and a closely watched British budget add political risk to the agenda.

Here's all you need to know about the coming week in ‌financial markets by Lewis Krauskopf in New York, Kevin Buckland in Tokyo, and Dhara Ranasinghe, Marc Jones and William Schomberg in London.

1/ MOVE OVER

It's a packed week for central banks. The Fed, Bank of Canada and Reserve ​Bank of New Zealand meet on Wednesday, the ECB on Thursday, and the BOJ a day later.

The Fed, ECB and BOJ face no immediate pressure to hike rates after tightening last month.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will be pressed on his view on the rate outlook. The ECB is sure to face questions about surging French borrowing costs that risk becoming a flashpoint, while the BOJ may raise its inflation forecasts in a post-meeting report.

Markets expect Canada and New Zealand to hike rates to contain inflation, with all policymakers grappling with the extent to which high oil ‌will fuel broader price pressures.

2/ HYPERSCALER HOT SEAT

A big week ⁠for US corporate earnings will be headlined by reports from three of the largest companies at the heart of the huge AI capital investment theme that has driven up equities.

Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon — three of the so-called hyperscalers — will post results at a time investors are becoming ⁠wary of the risks of the spending on data centres.

The week will be critical to determining if the third quarter lived up to high expectations for US profit growth, with about one-third of S&P 500 companies reporting.

Other high-profile firms set to report include drugmaker Eli Lilly, oil majors Exxon and Chevron, and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar.

3/ FISCAL TIGHTROPE

British finance minister John Healey will announce his first budget ​on ​Wednesday, when he will try to offer some relief from higher energy prices to households, but without ​unsettling the bond market by ramping up borrowing.

That means Healey may ‌have to accept a narrowing of his room for manoeuvre to meet his fiscal rules. Analysts polled by Reuters think he can allow his headroom to almost halve to around £15 billion ($20 billion) without spooking the market.

Banks might bear the brunt of tax increases, and the share prices of Britain's biggest lenders have fallen in the run-up to Healey's high-profile debut.

Story Continues

Bigger decisions on spending in areas such as defence, public services and welfare are likely to be put off until next year, with Healey hoping the Iran war — and the pressure it is putting on government borrowing costs — may have abated by then.

4/ NETANYAHU'S MOMENT OF TRUTH

Israel's election on Tuesday is poised to be one of the most consequential in the country's history.

Polls ‌have it as a coin toss, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud bloc nor an opposition ​centred around former military chief Gadi Eisenkot expected to win a majority, raising the prospect of lengthy ​coalition negotiations.

Yet for markets, it also comes after an extraordinary rally in Israeli assets. ​Since 2023's October 7 attacks, the Tel Aviv stock market has surged more than 135%, while the shekel is up a world-beating 25%.

Analysts ‌are quick to point out the AI boom has been key, given ​Israel's tech expertise, and will remain so. But ​investors also see the potential for tensions to be gradually dialled down in the longer term if Eisenkot and his allies can win out.

5/ PARTY PRIORITIES

China's top leadership gathers in Beijing for the four-day Fifth Plenum from Monday, with officials deliberating on "Advancing Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance."

That may sound inward-looking, but official Chinese commentary frames ​the initiative as an effort to strengthen Party discipline and ‌execution in response to a more challenging external environment, including an increasingly tense relationship with the United States and curbs on China's access to advanced foreign ​technology.

That's not to say Beijing doesn't face challenges at home too, with domestic demand stuck in a prolonged slump that has proved stubbornly resistant to ​stimulus efforts.

($1 = 0.7470 pounds)

(Graphics by Pasit Kongkunakornkul, compiled by Samuel Indyk. Editing by Mark Potter)

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Meta Platforms and Pepsi
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 23, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Meta Platforms META and Pepsi PEP.

Meta FCF Flips Negative: Why Investors Should Overlook It

Why Did Meta Move Up Its Earnings Date?

Just before the normal market trading hours concluded on Wednesday, investors finally got an answer on why Meta Platforms moved up its earnings date. Meta plans to issue non-voting shares to fund AI investments without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta also narrowed its FY26 CAPEX outlook to $130-$145B.

Meta Misses EPS Expectations Due to One-Time Charges

Meta Platforms reported mixed earnings after Wednesday's market close. Revenue of $64.60B beat Wall Street expectations of $63.33B (26% YoY growth). EPS of $3.83 fell well short of Wall Street expectations of $5.89 (+265% YoY growth). However, the EPS miss was driven by one-time, non-operating expenses, including a $2.4 billion legal settlement, restructuring costs, and aggressive AI infrastructure and CAPEX.

Investors should take the headline EPS number with a grain of salt, as nothing has materially changed in Meta's core business. For instance, Ad revenue, Meta's most important number, jumped 28%. Additionally, Ad impressions and price per Ad each jumped double digits year over year as AI continues to optimize the Meta family of products, while the company's headcount plunged 15%.

Meta Free Cash Flow Flips Negative

The post-EPS headline Wall Street is focused on is that, in Q3, Meta posted its first negative free cash flow quarter since it went public in 2012.

While this stat should normally raise concerns, investors must apply some nuance in their analysis.

Why Investors Should Overlook Meta's Negative Free Cash Flow

On Wall Street, CEOs generally fall into two categories: caretakers and visionaries. For instance, the CEO of a company like Pepsi is going to operate completely differently than the CEO of a cutting-edge tech company like Meta. In Pepsi's case, the CEO's main goal is to ensure nothing "breaks," the company generates cash flow, and it stays stable.

Conversely, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is hyper-focused on spotting the next big tech trends and turning them into growth opportunities. For instance, many Wall Street pundits scoffed when Zuckerberg purchased Instagram for $1 billion in April 2012. Today, Instagram is worth an estimated $70 billion.

Meta Muse Will Spur Future Growth

"Muse," Meta's agentic AI platform, is the answer to the spending question. On the conference call, Mark Zuckerberg said that he expects Muse to beat the Meta family apps average revenue per user over time. In just one month, Muse achieved 10 million setups. The app has also consistently topped the Apple App Store rankings. Most impressively, shopping is the #1 use case, and the average purchase size is over $200. While Muse is still in its early days, continued CAPEX spending is justified by the impressive early traction it's achieved.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

While negative free cash flow often signals trouble, Meta's temporary dip is a deliberate reinvestment into its high-growth future. With a thriving core ad business and early traction from agentic AI platforms like Muse, Mark Zuckerberg's aggressive CAPEX strategy is setting the stage for Meta's next multi-billion-dollar expansion.

news.Title: If the AI Bubble Bursts, These Stocks Will Be Winners
news.Content:
Jitters about the AI trade are spreading across the market again.

CoreWeave has plunged in recent weeks, reaching its lowest level since shortly after its IPO, after its bond yields jumped to as high as 15%. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.6% on Thursday, hitting its lowest level in more than a month. Meta Platforms tumbled 7% in spite of a strong earnings report as investors were spooked by its first quarter of negative free cash flow in its history, reflecting the surge in spending on AI infrastructure capital expenditures.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

While there's no sign of demand issues in AI, investors are clearly skeptical that companies like Meta and CoreWeave will see a return on investment, especially as interest rates have surged.

However, something surprising has happened with interest rates over the past couple of weeks. After investors bid them up on concerns about inflation, the war in Iran, AI spending, and new Fed chief Kevin Warsh's promise to raise the benchmark Fed funds rate, treasury yields have started to come down.

The benchmark 10-year yield fell by 3.8% to 4.95%, its first time below 5% in a month, and it's down by 7% over the last two weeks. That could reflect a rotation out of stocks into bonds to take advantage of high yields, and worries about a sell-off in AI stocks are likely to accelerate that shift.

Image source: Getty Images.

A sign of things to come

While tech stocks were plunging on Thursday, one sector was soaring, and it could be a sign of things to come.

Homebuilder stocks jumped Thursday, due to the decline in interest rates, tech investors looking for opportunities elsewhere, and attractive valuations in many of these stocks, even as the housing sector has struggled.

The State Street SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF (NYSEMKT:XHB) finished the day up 3.8% as stocks like Pool Corporation , RH (Restoration Hardware), and Lennar finished up 14.4%, 9.5%, and 9%, respectively.

Investors clearly see an opportunity in the housing sector if interest rates go down, and if we continue to see the AI trade, bond yields are likely to fall further.

A month ago, investors thought another Fed rate hike in October was more likely than not. After several data points over the last month, including weak jobs growth in September and cooler-than-expected PCE inflation in August, investors now see a 93% chance that the Fed holds rates steady at 375-400 basis points. Over the next year, rates are still expected to go up, but it's much harder to predict what will happen several months from now, and the Fed's own projections are often wrong.

Story Continues

Overall, concerns about interest rates continuing to go up have taken a significant step back over the last month.

Should you buy housing stocks now?

I'm not ready to call an AI bubble , though there's clearly pressure on stocks like CoreWeave. Still, the evidence shows that demand for AI compute remains strong, and there are bottlenecks in the supply chain for memory and beyond, indicating that demand greatly exceeds supply.

However, the reaction in the housing sector shows that if you're an investor with some AI winnings, shifting some of those gains to a homebuilder or a home furnishing stock might make sense. This isn't the first time we've seen beaten-down stocks soar on a similar rotation, as apparel stocks like Nike , Lululemon , and Deckers Outdoor jumped in a single session earlier this month. That's another sign that investors are looking for the next set of winners after AI, and it makes sense to look for stocks that have struggled.

Interest rates will tell the tale for the housing sector. If inflation cools, economic gains remain modest, and worries about AI growth continue to mount, rates are likely to come down, and that will favor the housing sector, as we saw on Thursday.

news.Title: Not IonQ. Not D-Wave. This Quantum Stock Could Be 2027's Surprise Winner.
news.Content:
While quantum computing holds significant promise as a transformative technology that could improve pharmaceutical discovery, materials science, and artificial intelligence (AI), many quantum computing stocks have failed to deliver lately.

Take IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) and D-Wave (NASDAQ: QBTS), for example. Their share prices are down 29% and 54% year to date, respectively, despite the companies being widely considered among the top in quantum computing.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, where can investors find a quantum computing stock winner? Here's the surprising part: You need to look slightly outside conventional quantum computing stocks and choose Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT).

Here's why it's a good quantum computing stock and why it could be a winner next year.

How Microsoft is tackling the quantum computing market

I know Microsoft isn't the first company people think of when talking about quantum computing, but it's making significant moves in this space that are worth considering.

First, Microsoft developed a topological superconductor, which it calls a topconductor, that is capable of producing more stable qubits (the units of computation for quantum computers). Microsoft then pairs that with its own chip architecture, called Majorana, to help scale those qubits, with the goal of eventually reaching 1 million qubits on a single chip.

The company recently made new advancements with Majorana, releasing the second iteration of its chip architecture, which it says yields a 1,000x improvement in qubit stability.

This is important because all quantum computing essentially has the same endgame: to create a fault-tolerant computer that can scale large enough to solve problems traditional computers can't solve.

But Microsoft's work in this area is more than just theoretical. The company already offers some quantum computing processing to customers through its Azure cloud computing services. The Azure Quantum service is already used by researchers now and could expand further in the coming years.

And this is where I think Microsoft has an advantage over pure-play quantum computing companies. Microsoft's Azure Cloud reached $100 billion in annualized revenue in fiscal 2026, as customers relied more on its artificial intelligence cloud services.

AI will drive Azure sales for years as the AI cloud market is estimated to reach $2 trillion by 2030, according to Goldman Sachs . Growth in Microsoft's cloud business and other services allows it to invest in quantum computing technologies without the same risks that IonQ, D-Wave, or other quantum computing companies face.

Story Continues

And because Microsoft is highly profitable -- it had $19.6 billion in free cash flow in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, ended June 30 -- investors don't need to worry if the company will have enough runway to continue operating (which is nearly a concern with some other quantum companies).

Why Microsoft stock could perform well in 2027

Microsoft's Q4 2026 was its best quarter in 28 years, with revenue rising 18% to $90 billion and operating income rising 18% to $40.6 billion.

The growth was fueled by Azure's accelerating AI revenue, and as I mentioned earlier, it's continuing to grow. Microsoft's management says Azure revenue will rise by 45% in fiscal 2027. Investors will get a glimpse of its growth when the company reports its Q1 results on Oct. 28.

Microsoft's ability to tap into the expanding AI cloud space has helped push the company's share price up more than 20% over the past six months, with the initial surge happening right after the company reported its Q4 results.

There's no guarantee Microsoft stock will continue to climb, of course. But Microsoft is a leading cloud computing company with 21% of the global market, surpassed only by Amazon at 28%, according to Synergy Research Group. The combination of the increasing demand for AI cloud computing and Microsoft's strong position in this space suggests that the company's sales and earnings will continue to benefit from this segment.

And with Microsoft continually expanding its quantum computing technologies and already integrating them into its Azure platform, Microsoft is in a unique position to benefit from two of the most significant technologies to emerge in decades.

news.Title: S&P 500 best performers: Zero mag 7 stocks past 13 weeks
news.Content: It's energy, not technology, that's generating the best returns this year, and that's been particularly true recently. Technology's underperformance may surprise you, given how often the media writes about artificial intelligence and how it's on track to disrupt everything from manufacturing floors to store shelves to battle fields. Yet, that's always been a Wall Street truth: Once everyone is talking about it, the easy money has already been made. Consider just how significantly the SPDR Technology ETF (XLK) has lagged other sectors since the summer.  It's been essentially flat since June 30, while the SPDR Energy ETF (XLE) has gained 29%, bringing its year-to-date return to a rather remarkable 55.4%. And look at the magnificent seven. None of them (Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet, Tesla, Meta, and Amazon) is among the top 20 S&P 500 performers over the past 13 weeks. Mag 7 takes a back seat In 2023, when Nvidia (NVDA) surprised everyone with a massive beat-and-raise quarter that kicked off the AI cloud spending boom, nobody was talking about AI, and few had any idea who would likely be the biggest players. Following a bear market drubbing, many were still shunning technology stocks, afraid of aftershocks. It took over a year for most to truly begin to believe AI spending would be durable or ultimately prove profit-friendly, and stock market returns could continue climbing. Read More: Cathie Wood sells $16 million of surging tech stock The result? Nvidia became a $5.1 trillion company that accounts for 7.4% of the S&P 500 on its own, and altogether, the mag 7 represent over one third of the benchmark. This year, the backdrop is different. Just about everyone knows about AI, thanks to using Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude at home or work. And most investors own the biggest AI players, including hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet) and picks-and-shovel providers, including AI chip darlings Nvidia, Micron, AMD, and Broadcom. With so few still left on the sidelines to buy those stocks, it's little wonder the mag 7 has taken a back seat to other stocks recently, including over the past few days. On October 22, the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) fell 3.4% while the less-tech-heavy State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was up 0.4%. "If you own semis or any of the Mags, it's been a really ugly week. But if you own the others, you're probably enjoying this market for the first time in ages," wrote Helene Meisler on TheStreet Pro. Energy sets the pace as geopolitics ignites crude Story Continues Energy has had fits and starts this year, but selling has been short-lived.  Those who have stuck with the basket since the U.S. removed Maduro from Venezuela's government in January have been rewarded much better than the buy-and-hold AI stocks crowd. The main reason for energy's outperformance has been the relentless rise of crude oil amid growing global supply tensions, particularly in the Middle East. Since December, West Texas Crude oil prices have surged to $99 per barrel from about $57 exiting 2025, padding profits at producers less reliant on Middle East oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. Consider ExxonMobil (XOM). The average Wall Street analyst expects it to report third-quarter revenue of $106 billion, up from $85.3 billion in the same period one year ago. Analysts are similarly targeting $4.03 in earnings per share. One year ago, ExxonMobil earned $1.88. More Oil & Gas: Chevron CEO issues stark warning on depleting oil reserves World's biggest oil CEO shares stark oil price warning as pressure builds and supplies run dry Bank of America resets its oil price target with strong warning The situation is similar for Chevron (CVX), which is expected to see revenue surge to $61.7 billion from $49.7 billion last year, and Warren Buffett's favorite oil stock, Occidental Petroleum (OXY), which is expected to see EPS jump to $1.45 from $0.64 last year in the third quarter. It's not just oil exploration and production stocks that are intriguing. Energy service stocks can benefit from uncorking Venezuelan oil fields, and eventually, rebuilding Middle East infrastructure. Long-time value investor Bret Jensen sees Halliburton (HAL) and SLB (SLB) as two oil services stocks likely to win in that scenario. "Both of these energy services names should benefit immensely once hostilities in the Middle East finally end. They should garner plenty of additional work to restore production in the region. As well as to rebuild inventories and strengthen energy security, wrote Jensen on TheStreet Pro. Sector-wide, energy stocks within the S&P 500 will deliver 127.6% more in earnings per share than last year, according to FactSet . That kind of step-up in sales and profits caught most investors off guard. I wrote in January that this would be the year of energy, given the geopolitical tailwind, especially since oil stocks accounted for just 3% of the S&P 500 index, suggesting they were significantly under-owned by Main Street and Wall Street. It's not all bad for tech, but it's software, not hardware , winning Looking at the top 20 S&P 500 stocks over the past 13 weeks, there are plenty of information technology stocks represented, simply not the ones you might think. Instead of mag 7, it's IT information services stocks like Accenture (ACN) and Gartner (IT), and software stocks like Palantir (PLTR), ServiceNow (NOW), Workday (WDAY), and Salesforce.com (CRM) that are setting the pace. In late 2025 and early 2026, software stocks took a drubbing amid fears that AI would enable companies to build their own solutions rather than pay for seat licenses for tools like CRM, HR, and finance. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF (IGV) tumbled 36% from its November high to its April 2026 low, setting the stage nicely for a recovery as 'existential' industry fear dissipated. Since June, it's been a different story. The IGV has risen 20%, with stocks like Palantir, ServiceNow, Workday, and Salesforce up significantly more over the past thirteen weeks. Within technology, the argument is shifting for investors from how much money is being spent building out data centers with next-gen servers powered by super-fast chips to what companies will actually help businesses figure out how best to exploit AI to pay for all those tokens. Outside of technology, it's about what other than the mag 7 makes sense. So far, it's been energy, but investors shouldn't count healthcare out. Of the major sector ETFs, The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) trails only energy since June, returning 13.2%. news.Title: Meta found a new way to pay for its AI boom
news.Content: Meta Platforms (META) is preparing to give shareholders another share of stock. One crucial item that the new stock will deny them is a vote. Starting in January 2027, Meta will issue publicly traded Class C shares without voting rights. The economic effect of a two-for-one stock split will be one Class C share per Class A and Class B share. There is more to the move than just making Meta shares seem less expensive. As the corporation invests enormous sums of money in artificial intelligence, Meta claims that the new shares may be used to raise money, pay staff, and cover acquisitions. Also Read: Cathie Wood sells $16 million of surging tech stock However, Meta is able to raise that capital without diminishing Mark Zuckerberg's power as CEO by issuing non-voting shares. Because of these factors, the new stock provides an exceptionally clear view into Meta's goals. As it purchases processors, constructs data centers, and creates AI products, the corporation anticipates spending between $135 billion and $145 billion on capital expenditures in 2026. In order to continue spending, Meta needs more financial freedom. It does not want Zuckerberg to give up power in order to get it. Meta's new shares are not free money The first thing that regular investors need to realize is that Meta is not going to instantly double everyone's wealth. The intended distribution would ultimately leave an investor with 10 Class A shares and ten Class C shares if they held ten Meta Class A shares. However, Meta anticipates that the market value of its current Class A shares will change to reflect a two-for-one stock split. In other words, investors receive additional shares, but the company's economic value does not immediately double. Voting power makes a difference. Voting rights are attached to Meta's current publicly listed Class A shares. Despite holding less than a majority of the company's economic worth, Zuckerberg has been able to keep control of it because of his Class B shares, which have far more voting power. There are no votes on the new Class C shares. Meta stressed that no shareholder's voting power would be altered by the distribution. That becomes especially important after the initial stock dividend. Thereafter, Meta will have a currency that it may provide to staff members, possible acquisition targets, or new investors without giving them more power over business choices. Reuters reported that Meta designed the structure partly to finance growth while preserving Zuckerberg's control. Story Continues That's the real story for stockholders. Meta is doing more than just dividing its shares. To fund the next phase of its AI evolution, it is altering its toolbox. Meta's AI bill explains why it wants more flexibility Meta has a lot of money. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $82.45 billion at the end of September. However, its expenditures are increasing at an incredibly rapid rate. Purchases of property and equipment increased from $18.83 billion to $34.91 billion in the third quarter alone. After a year of positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion, free cash flow fell to negative $2.12 billion. Meta projects $135 billion to $145 billion in capital expenditures for the whole year. More Tech: Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft cutting off popular software with no extension Oct. 13 Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge Artificial intelligence is becoming more and more connected to expenditure. While attempting to transform its new Muse AI agent into yet another massive consumer platform, Meta is constructing data centers, purchasing cutting-edge CPUs, and creating its own models. In its first six weeks, over 10 million users in the US and Canada registered for Muse accounts, according to Zuckerberg. He thinks Muse will someday have billions of users. However, providing for such a large number of users is costly. Reuters reported that Zuckerberg acknowledged Muse costs more to operate than many products Meta has launched in the past, prompting the company to think about monetizing it sooner. This increases the value of having access to more capital. Zuckerberg keeps control while Meta keeps spending The Class C shares become very intriguing at this point. By issuing a lot of voting stock, a traditional corporation may progressively reduce the power of current shareholders. That may ultimately jeopardize the founder's authority over a firm they own. Meta's suggested structure mostly avoids that issue. The company's board said one reason for creating Class C shares was to ensure Zuckerberg continues leading Meta into its next era. Meta has also entered into what it calls a Founder Alignment Agreement with Zuckerberg covering his Class C shares and potential future stock distributions. This implies that Meta might use shares with economic value to pay staff or fund acquisitions more often without generating fresh votes that would compete with Zuckerberg's. For regular investors, there is a trade-off. The arrangement provides Meta with more freedom to pursue AI opportunities without necessarily relying solely on money or debt. However, investors purchasing the new Class C shares will control a portion of Meta without having any influence over the company's governance. When one CEO already has significant control over the course of the business, that difference is important. Meta is preparing for an expensive AI future A large portion of Meta's goal can be financed by its current operations. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, while advertising impressions increased 10% and average advertising prices climbed 14%. The funding for Meta's AI revolution is still coming from that advertising machine. However, it has become more difficult to overlook the price of competing. During the quarter, Meta invested about $35 billion in capital projects, and it anticipates further aggressive spending in 2027. It now has an additional means of funding that growth, thanks to the new Class C shares. This makes it more than just an odd stock split. Meta is preparing its financing structure for a future where artificial intelligence will require years of massive investment before products like Muse can become significant stand-alone companies. It has built that framework around a single, crucial need. Meta can issue more shares. It can use them to buy companies. It can use them to attract employees. It can potentially use them to raise enormous amounts of capital. But those shares do not have to make Mark Zuckerberg any less powerful. Related: Meta Platforms, Inc. news.Title: Amazon caught hackers probing a PHP flaw 4 days before the fix
news.Content: Most security breaches start with a lock nobody knew was broken. For years, that was the comfortable assumption behind the software that runs the internet. Bugs existed, but finding the dangerous ones took rare skill and a lot of time. That buffer has quietly disappeared. Artificial intelligence is now finding old flaws faster than humans can patch them, and attackers are using the same tools to turn fixes into weapons. If you have a website for your business, your side hustle or your church, this one lands on you too. The fix is free and already out. The hard part is getting it onto millions of servers before attackers get there first, and that race started earlier than most people realize. It also explains why Wikipedia, the Port of Rotterdam, and France's Interior Ministry all pulled sites offline on Oct. 21. I spent the morning going through the disclosures, and one detail stands out more than any outage list. Amazon (AMZN) says its security team caught someone trying to exploit the newly discovered flaws in PHP, the programming language behind most of the web, on Oct. 17. That was four days before the developers released a fix, according to a post on Amazon's security blog . Amazon's honeypot saw the attack before the public did Amazon runs decoy servers, known as honeypots, to watch what attackers do. One of them recorded an exploit attempt from an anonymized internet address while the flaws were still under embargo, wrote CJ Moses, chief information security officer of Amazon Integrated Security. It is still unclear how the attacker learned about the bugs early. Moses said proof-of-concept exploits were circulating as early as 2 a.m. UTC on Oct. 21, about 12 hours before the official release. "PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild," Moses wrote. More Technology : Anthropic announces big plan to help workers disrupted by AI Chip toolmakers can't catch a break, even as TSMC spends more Apple's new CEO just teamed up with Tim Cook's old rival The flaws, tracked as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entries CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, let an attacker run code on a vulnerable server without logging in. Cybersecurity firm Wiz, which Alphabet (GOOGL) owns, said it found them with help from its own AI tool plus Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, according to its research post . Wiz said the bugs reach back to PHP 5.4 and had been hiding in the code for more than a decade. "Applying the PHP security update remains the only complete remediation," the firm wrote. Story Continues Moses explained why the window keeps shrinking. "AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a patch diff or advisory into a working exploit," he wrote. Governments pulled sites offline as PHP shipped fixes The scale is what spooked officials. "All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable," Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association, told Reuters . PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web tracker W3Techs, as cited by Reuters. It sits under WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Here's how the response played out across the first 48 hours: The Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre took its own site offline, and the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl and several hospitals followed, according to Reuters . European cyber agencies, including the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), told organizations to "consider isolating exposed applications" if they cannot patch right away, according to a joint statement . Attackers began altering their payloads to slip past filters, Cloudflare (NET) said, as reported by The Hacker News . PHP released fixed versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 at 14:00 UTC on Oct. 21, according to The Repository , a WordPress industry newsletter. Costin Raiu, co-founder of security firm TLP:Black, warned that the next phase could be "mass compromise of every vulnerable web server on the internet," Reuters reported. Censys count shows 1.5 million servers need upgrades In my analysis, the outage headlines understate the real exposure. Internet scanning firm Censys counted about 1.5 million of 2.6 million hosts running a PHP version with no fix available, according to Reuters . That is roughly 58%. Those servers cannot simply be patched; they need a full upgrade to a newer PHP release, which takes longer and can break older websites. That gap will not close in a week. It means the risk window stays open well after the headlines fade. Hosting companies are moving at different speeds Most people with a website never touch PHP directly. Your hosting company does, and the responses so far vary. Automattic said customers of WordPress.com and its other managed platforms were protected before the release. "On WordPress.com, security is our job to solve, not yours," said Ian Stewart, the company's artistic director and product lead, according to The Repository . GoDaddy (GDDY) said its Managed WordPress hosting was fully patched, while its standard Web and Windows Hosting still relied on interim protections as of Oct. 22, the newsletter reported. Bluehost warned that customers may see limits on upload file sizes while it finishes patching. Risk is highest for small sites run by people with limited technical help, often on shared hosting where customers do not manage the servers, Reuters noted. 3 checks for your own website this week You do not need to be a programmer to protect yourself. Start with three steps: Check your PHP version. In WordPress, it appears under Tools, then Site Health, then Info. Ask your host directly whether your server runs 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 or later. Get the answer in writing. If you sell anything online, review recent orders and admin accounts for anything you do not recognize, and save your logs from Oct. 17 onward, as Amazon advised. If you are still on PHP 8.2 or older, plan an upgrade now. PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on Dec. 31, according to The Repository . Investors get a stress test for Cloudflare and GoDaddy For investors, the story cuts both ways. Amazon and Alphabet just showed their security teams can spot threats early, while Cloudflare's filtering business gets a real-world stress test. GoDaddy carries more operational risk, because its customers skew toward small businesses on shared plans. I will be watching whether any host reports a breach tied to these flaws in the coming weeks. The bigger shift is the speed. "The scale is huge, and with AI, exploitation may happen instantly," Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London, told Reuters . Your website is part of your income now. Treat your host's patch status the way you treat a bank alert: check it today, not next month. news.Title: Google’s AI chip could become a $75 billion business
news.Content: Alphabet (GOOGL) built its artificial intelligence chips so Google would not have to depend entirely on Nvidia (NVDA) . These chips have the potential to grow into a massive enterprise. Evercore ISI predicts $75 billion in 2027 and $113 billion in 2028 sales of Google's TPUs to outside customers. As a result, technology that was initially intended to reduce Google's own computing expenses would become one of Alphabet's main new sources of income. Evercore analyst Georgia Anderson estimates TPU sales could represent roughly 35% of Google Cloud revenue in 2027 , according to Investor's Business Daily . She maintained an Outperform rating on Alphabet with a $450 price target. The significance is clear to investors. Google doesn't need to outperform Nvidia in every area of AI computing. Alphabet can profit from the AI infrastructure boom that has made Nvidia one of the world's most valuable companies by renting or selling Google's chips. Additionally, Google controls the cloud where many of those processors will operate, in contrast to Nvidia. Google turned an internal cost saver into a product Google started creating TPUs more than 10 years ago because traditional processors became too costly for some of its biggest machine-learning tasks. At first, the chips were mostly developed for Google's internal services. This tactic is evolving. Earlier in 2026, Alphabet announced that Google Cloud will begin providing TPU hardware to specific clients for use inside their own data centers. The company expected a small amount of revenue from those agreements in 2026, with the vast majority arriving in 2027 . The opportunity is much increased by such action. In the past, customers who wanted Google chips had to use Google Cloud to consume them. Now, customers may purchase systems for their own facilities, rent TPUs via Google Cloud, or use them through infrastructure agreements, all of which allow Alphabet to generate revenue. For instance, Blackstone invested an initial $5 billion in a joint venture with Google that aims to launch 500 megawatts of TPU cloud capacity by 2027. Google will provide the chips, software and services. As a result, Google begins to resemble a true provider of AI infrastructure rather than just a cloud provider that also designs chips. Nvidia finally has a different kind of competitor Google is not attempting to quickly replicate Nvidia's operations. With a software environment that developers have spent years understanding, Nvidia continues to be the leading supplier of general-purpose AI accelerators. Story Continues Google has a distinct edge. More Tech: Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft cutting off popular software with no extension Oct. 13 Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge The company controls the entire stack around its TPUs. Google creates the processors, runs massive data centers, controls Google Cloud, and creates Gemini models that use the infrastructure. Customers willing to optimize their software around Google's framework may find TPUs more appealing. Evercore's industry checks suggest TPUs can offer 20% to 40% lower costs for customers with experienced engineering teams, although software limitations and a shortage of specialized talent remain barriers to wider adoption. One client has already demonstrated the size that Google is pursuing. This year, Anthropic decided to increase the amount of Google TPUs it uses by several gigawatts. The extra capacity is anticipated to be online in 2027. The Claude developer will use both Google Cloud services and Google-built TPUs provided by Broadcom. It's easy to overlook the importance. Any big AI firm needs a significant amount of processing power. Until recently, much of the investor discourse expected Nvidia to account for the majority of that expenditure. Google is showing that hyperscalers are becoming increasingly interested in the opportunity. Wall Street is starting to put a value on Google's chips Evercore is not the only company seeing the emergence of a sizable enterprise. Piper Sandler estimates external TPU hardware sales could climb from roughly $8 billion in 2026 to $51 billion in 2027 and $104 billion in 2028. While BMO recently lifted its 2027 Google Cloud revenue prediction to $189 billion, citing improved cloud trends and the expanding semiconductor business, Wells Fargo has also increased its Alphabet forecasts due to external TPU sales. These estimations differ significantly, and investors should remember that none of these figures are certain. Google still has to produce the chips, get sufficient power for data centers, and persuade consumers that implementing its technology is worthwhile. Additionally, Nvidia has a significant installed edge. However, TPUs are important, even if Alphabet does not overtake Nvidia. Even with Evercore's $75 billion projection, external chip sales would be a significant business inside one of the biggest corporations in the world. The economics go beyond chip sales, which is more significant. In addition to purchasing storage, networking, databases, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence services from Google Cloud, a client drawn to Google's TPUs may also purchase these services. This implies that a single chip transaction has the potential to increase expenditure inside Alphabet's ecosystem. For many years, investors mainly saw Google as an advertising firm with a potential cloud business. But a third option is being made possible by artificial intelligence. Wall Street is beginning to place a lot of weight on Google, which may have developed one of the only reliable substitutes for the chips driving the AI growth. Alphabet's next big venture may already be in its data centers if Evercore is even close. It was initially designed without external clients in mind. news.Title: Volkswagen workers may get Microsoft AI instead of a raise
news.Content:
Every company eventually has to decide what it will pay for when it can't pay for everything.

For most of the last century, major industrial employers answered that question the same way. You hired people, trained them, and paid them more as they got better at the job.

That bargain has been fraying for years at Volkswagen, the German group behind VW, Audi, Porsche, Skoda, and Cupra. Its chief executive has spent much of 2026 talking about job cuts, idle factory capacity, and a cost gap with rivals that he puts at roughly 20 percent.

If you've ever sat through a budget meeting, you know how this goes. Spending that looks like a cost gets cut. Spending that looks like an investment gets defended, even when money is tight.

So when the company finds money for something new, it's worth asking where that money is going and who pays for it.

This week, I got an answer.

Volkswagen Group (VLKAF) has equipped more than 330,000 employees with Microsoft (MSFT) Copilot, the artificial intelligence assistant built into Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, Microsoft said on Oct. 21.

The timing is hard to miss. Two days earlier, Volkswagen's own labor representatives said the company wants to hold salaries at 2026 levels for the rest of the decade.

Volkswagen puts Copilot on 330,000 desks

The rollout did not happen overnight. Volkswagen first gave staff broad access to Copilot Chat, the free chat version that comes with eligible Microsoft 365 plans, and saw more than 300,000 monthly active users on it, according to Microsoft's announcement .

Employees are now using a more advanced version tied to what Microsoft calls Work IQ. The company says it reaches into engineering, production, procurement, and sales.

"The real value of AI comes from making it available at scale in everyday work," said Sophie Vassarotti, head of group data and AI at Volkswagen Group, in the same release.

Related: Franklin Templeton CEO says AI is hiding a bigger tech story

Microsoft framed the deal as a template for other industrial companies.

"Volkswagen shows how companies can evolve AI from a personal productivity tool into a foundation for future AI innovation," said Agnes Heftberger, chair of the management board of Microsoft Germany.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella cheered the news himself. "Super to see Volkswagen Group putting Copilot to work across the company!" he wrote in an X post on Oct. 22.

Here's what the deal looks like by the numbers:

More than 330,000 employees are equipped with Copilot, and more than 26,000 AI agents are active across the group over the past month, according to Microsoft

About 660,000 people are on Volkswagen's payroll worldwide, including 275,000 in Germany, according to Daily Sabah , which carried the wire report

$30 per user per month, paid yearly, for Microsoft 365 Copilot for enterprise, according to Microsoft's pricing page

More than 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats across all customers as of July, according to Nadella on Microsoft's fiscal fourth-quarter call, as reported by UC Today

Story Continues

Pay freeze talks hit Europe's biggest carmaker

Volkswagen's Global Works Council said the executive board told human resources managers worldwide to suspend pay increases, a directive in effect since early October, according to Daily Sabah .

Germany's Süddeutsche Zeitung estimated affected staff could lose about 10 percent of their income to inflation over that stretch.

More Jobs:

Jeff Bezos explains why Amazon is still cutting jobs

Bill Gates says some jobs should be reserved for humans

Elon Musk delivers 6-word warning on future of employment

A Volkswagen spokesperson declined to comment on what the company called "speculation" and said labor cost proposals belong in talks with unions, according to the same report.

The union is not backing down. "At Volkswagen, pay development is decided at the negotiating table, not by decree from the executive boardroom," an IG Metall spokesperson said. The union is seeking a 5 percent raise over 12 months.

The pay fight sits on top of a much bigger restructuring. Volkswagen said in March that it would cut about 50,000 jobs in Germany by 2030 after profit slid to its lowest level since 2016, according to AFP .

In July, CEO Oliver Blume told staff another 50,000 jobs could go, citing that 20 percent cost disadvantage. "We are currently assessing across all brands, companies and regions how many adjustments are actually necessary and feasible," Blume wrote in an internal memo, according to Just Auto , which cited Reuters.

The company is chasing 6 billion euros in annual net savings by 2030 and had locked in about 1 billion euros so far, according to Quartz , citing Blume's June 18 shareholder remarks.

Workplace columnist Suzanne Lucas read the pay plan bluntly. In her view, the message to staff is: "We don't think you'll find another job, and we don't care about you when you do stay here," she wrote in an Oct. 21 opinion piece on Inc.

What a Copilot AI assistant seat costs at list price

Neither company disclosed what Volkswagen pays, or how many of the 330,000 seats are paid for Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses versus the free chat tier. Large customers also negotiate below the list price.

Still, the list price gives you a ceiling. In my analysis, 330,000 seats at $30 a month works out to $118.8 million a year.

That is a small slice of a 6 billion euro savings target. Per worker, it comes to $360 a year.

Now set that against the pay side. If Süddeutsche Zeitung's estimate holds, a frozen salary could cost those same workers around 10 percent of their purchasing power by 2030.

That contrast is the real story here. A few hundred dollars per head for software clears the budget, and the raise does not.

Whether the tool pays for itself is still an open question. "Most organisations remain uncertain if Copilot's promised productivity gains justify the added cost," wrote Daryl Ullman, a partner at Microsoft licensing consultancy SAMexpert , in an Oct. 20, 2025, analysis.

Ullman's firm sells Microsoft contract negotiation services, so weigh that view with the same skepticism you'd give Microsoft's own productivity claims. Microsoft has also faced user pushback on AI features in Windows , a reminder that rollout numbers and daily use are different things.

Microsoft earnings Oct. 28 put enterprise demand in the spotlight

You won't wait long for the next data point. Microsoft reports fiscal first-quarter 2027 results after the market closes on Oct. 28, with a call at 2:30 p.m. PST, the company said in an Oct. 7 release .

Paid Copilot seats climbed from 15 million in January to more than 20 million in April, according to CNBC , before topping 30 million in July.

If every Volkswagen seat turned out to be paid, the deal alone would equal about 1% of that July base. I'll be listening for whether management singles out industrial customers like Volkswagen when it updates the count.

Volkswagen reports its own third-quarter results on Oct. 29, according to MarketScreener . Investors will want to hear how much of the savings plan is coming from labor and how much from tools like this one.

How this hits your paycheck and your portfolio

If you own an S&P 500 index fund or a target-date fund in your 401(k), you already own a meaningful piece of Microsoft. Deals like this one are how the company is trying to turn its massive AI spending into recurring subscription revenue.

If you work for a large employer, the Volkswagen playbook may look familiar soon. Budgets for software are getting approved while budgets for raises are getting squeezed.

That makes it worth being deliberate. Track what you actually do with the time an AI assistant saves you, and bring that record to your next review.

The companies that win this shift will be the ones that share some of the gains. Your job is to make sure your share shows up in your paycheck, not just in someone else's savings target.

Related: Volkswagen may cut 100,000 jobs in brutal reset

news.Title: U.S. stock futures little changed after Nasdaq posts worst day since June
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures were largely steady in Asian trading Friday after Wall Street ended sharply lower, with the Nasdaq Composite posting its steepest daily decline since June amid concerns over the cost and financing of artificial intelligence investments.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

S&P 500 Futures traded largely flat at 7,705.0 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures gained 0.2% to 29,200.75 points by 02:52 ET (06:52 GMT). Dow Jones Futures edged down 0.2% to 58,939.0 points.

In the regular session, the NASDAQ Composite fell 2.6% to 26,008.86, while the S&P 500 lost 1.2% to 7,663.43. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended flat at 52,867.98, as investors shifted away from growth-oriented technology stocks toward more defensive sectors.

The selloff reflected growing scrutiny of the massive capital spending required to develop AI infrastructure, even as companies report strong demand for computing capacity and AI-related services.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) shares tumbled nearly 7% after the Facebook parent reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade, driven by AI-related expenditure, and announced plans to issue non-voting shares to help finance its growth.

Although quarterly revenue beat analysts' expectations, the company's spending plans heightened concerns about the returns on its investments.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares fell about 3.1% after the electric-vehicle maker cut its 2026 capital expenditure forecast, adding to uncertainty over the pace of its AI and robotics expansion.

Semiconductor stocks were hit particularly hard, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping 6.7%, its biggest daily decline since June 23.

The selloff also hit AI-related infrastructure companies, including CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ:CRWV), highlighting concerns over financing costs and the time required to generate returns from heavy investment.

Oil prices added to the uncertain outlook. Brent crude extended gains on Friday, rising to a fresh five-month high above $114 per barrel. Fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fuelled concerns about disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies, raising the prospect of renewed inflationary pressure.

Investors sought safety in government bonds, sending the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield down nearly 20 basis points to around 4.95%, its biggest daily decline since March 2023. The move reflected a shift toward safer assets amid concerns about technology valuations and geopolitical risks.

Story Continues

Despite the technology rout, corporate earnings offered some support. Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) rose after reporting better-than-expected quarterly results, while Spotify (NYSE:SPOT) gained on a stronger operating income outlook.

Investors will now look for further earnings updates and fresh economic data to gauge whether the technology selloff signals a broader reassessment of growth prospects or a temporary correction in AI-related shares.

The Federal Reserve's policy decision next week will also be in focus, particularly as higher energy prices threaten to complicate the inflation outlook.

news.Title: Stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq tanks as tech stocks sink amid AI trade worries, Meta shares plummet
news.Content: US stocks fell on Thursday as the Tech ( XLK ) sector plummeted, with worries over the AI trade resurfacing following earnings from EV maker Tesla ( TSLA ) and social media giant Meta ( META ). Investors flocked to bonds, sending Treasury yields lower as oil prices surged to a five-month high . The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) was little changed, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 2.6% as semicondcutor stocks fell, reversing gains from Wednesday's session. Neocloud provider CoreWeave ( CRWV ) sank 10% as worries over the cost of capital and its impact on debt-heavy balance sheets resurfaced. Meanwhile, Meta shares tanked nearly 7% as investors weighed the company's quarterly results and 2-for-1 stock split announcement. Tesla shares were volatile after an earnings beat , as investors weighed lower 2026 capex against higher spending in 2027 and 2028 on Optimus, Cybercab, and Terafab. SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock fell, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain. Meanwhile, Blackstone's ( BX ) stock climbed 8% following the firm's upbeat outlook for upcoming investment sales after posting weaker third quarter earnings amid elevated borrowing costs. A report that the US and Israel are preparing for renewed attacks on Iran after the US mid-term elections sent Brent crude ( BZ=F ) to $113 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) climbed to $100. A deadly attack at a Saudi Arabian airport and oil field also put upward pressure on energy prices. In other news, jobless claims fell to 194,000 last week , the fewest in three months, underscoring how layoffs remain low. The 5-year breakeven — the inflation rate implied by the gap between regular Treasurys and inflation-protected TIPS — is a bit lower now than it was before the war. news.Title: Stocks drop as Meta fans AI worries, Treasuries gain
news.Content:
By Caroline Valetkevitch and Amanda Cooper

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Stock indexes fell on Thursday, after Meta's earnings report reignited worries about the AI boom's heavy capital spending, sending investors to the safety of US Treasuries.

Brent crude hit a five-month high following Houthi attacks ‌in Saudi Arabia, which stoked concerns of further disruption to global energy supplies.

The Nasdaq, weighed down by chip stocks, fell 2.6% in its ‌biggest daily percentage drop since early June, while MSCI's All-World index was off 1.3%.

Tech shares in Seoul, Tokyo, Amsterdam and Paris fell earlier.

Shares of Meta Platforms dropped 7% after reported quarterly results on Wednesday. ​Meta's third-quarter revenue beat expectations, but the company said it would issue non-voting stock, a plan that revived concern over its mounting capital commitments and the heavy spend of AI hyperscalers more generally.

An index of semiconductors, among the biggest beneficiaries of AI spending, fell 6.7% in its biggest daily percentage decline since June 23.

Shares of Tesla, which also reported earnings and cut its spending forecast, dropped 3.1%. Reuters reported that some Tesla insiders are concerned that CEO Elon Musk's public comments on ‌a potential merger with SpaceX could invite shareholder scrutiny ⁠and complicate deal talks. Shares of SpaceX ended down 9%.

Investors' shifting views over AI spending have added volatility to the market. The Nasdaq's Thursday selloff followed a 1% rally on Wednesday.

"To the extent investors believe that those (AI) earnings are real... they ⁠are buyers of these stocks," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey.

"But periodically, when they look at current earnings and the amount they're going to have to spend, they become concerned that these stocks are all overpriced."

TREASURIES GAIN IN SAFETY PLAY

US Treasuries rose, pushing yields lower, as ​the ​stock market's fall boosted the safe-haven appeal of government debt.

The yield on the benchmark US ​10-year Treasury note was down 19.3 basis points at 4.953%, ‌its biggest daily drop since March 10, 2023. It has dropped since rising to 5.3645% on October 7, highest since April 2002. Yields and prices move in opposite directions.

"They are rotating out of techs, out of the AIs, and into the more safety trades, whether it's bonds or some of those big Dow Jones stocks," said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading.

Story Continues

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 11.89 points to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 fell 93.74 points, or 1.2%, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 694 points, or 2.6%, to 26,008.86.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 14.95 points ‌to 1,122.93, its biggest one-day fall since June.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 1.05%.

BRENT ​JUMPS ON ATTACKS

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from ​the Middle East, pushing Brent oil up about 4%.

Brent futures rose $4.35, or ​4%, to settle at $113.17 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose $2.32, or 2.4%, to settle at $99.47.

Fragile equity markets also ‌boosted the yen, while the dollar rose against the euro.

The ​Japanese yen strengthened 0.75% to 156.96 per ​dollar. The euro was down 0.09% at $1.1222.

CONCERNS CONTINUE FOR FRANCE

French markets were again hit on concerns over the country's strained public finances and ongoing street protests.

France's 10-year government bond yields surpassed equivalent US Treasuries for the first time since 2013, reflecting growing over France's deteriorating fiscal position ​and rising debt burden.

The benchmark 10-year yield was last ‌up 6.5 basis points at 5.06%.

The premium investors demand to hold French government debt over safe-haven German Bunds widened to its highest ​in 15 years.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Amanda Cooper in London; Additional reporting by Alun John and Jiaxing Li; ​Editing by Kate Mayberry, Shri Navaratnam, Susan Fenton, Elaine Hardcastle and Aurora Ellis)

news.Title: 5 Undervalued AI Stocks According to the Media
news.Content:
The AI trade is getting bumpy as investors question whether the massive spending on data centers and chips will generate sufficient returns. There is only so much capital companies can raise, and cracks are beginning to appear. Yet some prominent investors believe the market is underestimating how much further the AI boom can run.

Speaking to CNBC earlier this week, Altimeter Capital founder and Chief Executive Brad Gerstner said investors have spent the past two years worrying about an eventual glut of AI computing capacity, only to miss substantial gains in semiconductor stocks. He believes the boom still has room to run because physical constraints, including chip production capacity and electricity supply, are limiting how quickly companies can expand AI infrastructure.

Gerstner is one of the loudest AI bulls on Wall Street, and his fund keeps buying AI stocks. Check his top 10 stock picks here . His latest filings show new additions too. Read his two new AI picks here .

"I actually think you have a natural constraint here," Gerstner said on CNBC. "There's only so fast in terms of production of wafers in this country. It's only so fast that we can bring power on."

HSBC's Willem Sels also believes investors are underestimating the AI opportunity. In a September interview with Bloomberg Television, the bank's global chief investment officer said US stock valuations did not fully reflect the potential for AI-driven productivity gains and earnings growth. He particularly highlighted semiconductor companies, whose valuations he believes reflect skepticism about future earnings forecasts despite the possibility of continued strong demand.

"The US is not expensive. The markets are questioning the sustainability of earnings growth, but that's in the price because that gap has closed," Sels told Bloomberg.

So, what are the most undervalued stocks according to the media? We listed the 10 most undervalued AI stock here . You can find the top 5 below.

Photo by AlphaTradeZone

How Did We Select These Stocks?

We based our research on the most undervalued AI stocks on at least 13 major finance sites to see what AI stocks they consider undervalued and analyzed the reasons they gave for their claims.

The ranking itself uses one measure: how many times a stock was called undervalued in the pieces we reviewed. The more often a stock came up, the higher it ranks. We counted each article once.

#5 Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL)

Oracle Corporation sells database software and cloud infrastructure, and bulls say the market prices it like a slow software company while its cloud business grows like a young growth stock. Revenue is expected to rise about 34% in fiscal 2027 and about 46% in fiscal 2028, and earnings per share are expected to rise about 7% in fiscal 2027 and about 35% in fiscal 2028.

Story Continues

The stock trades at 15.9 times forward non-GAAP earnings, which is 28% below its own five-year average. Its forward PEG ratio is 0.52, against 1.17 for the sector. Bulls say Oracle's large backlog of cloud contracts will turn into revenue over the next few years, and that the stock has not priced that in. The risks are heavy data center spending, negative free cash flow and rising debt. Oracle is down about 3% today and about 33% this year. Two billionaires were buying the stock while it slid. Read what they saw here .

#4 Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (NYSE:TSM)

A notable research site calls Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited the world's largest dedicated chip foundry and lists it among its best AI stocks in both April and October. Another finance site wrote on Oct. 12 that TSMC trades at 21 times forward earnings against 33 times trailing. It added that a PEG ratio of 0.89 suggests the stock could be undervalued.

That piece also said TSMC has lagged the chip rally because of margin worries, and that 20 of 21 analysts rate it a Buy. Other coverage pointed to a forward P/E of 25.3, below the 29.4 median for semiconductors, with 30% revenue growth expected in 2026. A popular investing site included TSMC in a January piece on undervalued AI stocks, and a second article called it still undervalued at 25 times forward earnings. Some writers warn that a pullback in AI demand would hurt the stock. Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office owns TSMC. Check the full breakdown here .

#3 Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

Many consider Microsoft Corporation undervalued because they say the market is not paying enough for its long-term cash flow growth. Analysts expect earnings per share to rise about 14% in fiscal 2027 and about 20% in fiscal 2028, so growth is speeding up. Revenue is also expected to grow about 18% in fiscal 2027. The stock trades at 27 times forward earnings, which is 11% below its own five-year average. It has also gone almost nowhere over the past year, and bulls say that gap between the stock and its earnings will close as its AI spending turns into sales.

The risks are slower cloud growth if enterprise spending weakens and tougher competition from Amazon. The stock also still trades above the sector median on forward earnings, and its forward PEG ratio of 1.71 is above the sector's 1.17. Investors keep asking whether its AI spending is paying off. Read the full answer here .

#2 Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

Many consider Micron Technology, Inc. undervalued because they say the market is pricing the stock for a fade that the numbers do not show. Micron makes the memory chips used in AI servers, and AI data centers now buy so much memory that profits have jumped. Analysts expect earnings per share to rise about 134% in fiscal 2027, and 28 of them raised their fiscal 2027 estimates in the past 30 days while 2 cut theirs.

The stock trades at 5.2 times forward earnings, which is 93% below its own five-year average. Its forward PEG ratio is 0.07, against 1.17 for the sector. Bulls say that a market-average multiple would deliver a big gain. The main risk is the memory cycle, since memory prices have swung hard in past booms. Memory stocks also slid again this month on worries about China's ChangXin Memory Technologies. Micron was down about 6% Thursday in the AI selloff. See what Wall Street may be missing here .

#1 NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)

Our research shows the media believes NVIDIA Corporation is undervalued because its earnings are growing much faster than its share price. Analysts expect earnings per share to rise about 95% in fiscal 2027 and about 71% in fiscal 2028, and they keep raising those estimates. The stock trades at 23.8 times forward earnings, which is 43% below its own five-year average. Many websites also point to a PEG ratio of 0.48, against 1.17 for the sector. Nvidia's lead in GPUs, its CUDA software platform and its networking business give it a moat that rivals will need years to cut into. NVDA was down recently, and two billionaires still like it. See who they are here .

While we acknowledge the potential of NVDA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
