news.Title: Up 3,700%, Should You Buy Sandisk Right Now?
news.Content:
The appreciation of Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) stock has been nothing short of phenomenal. Since its formal separation from Western Digital in February 2025, the stock has risen 3,700%, a feat unmatched by any large-cap stock over the same period.

Admittedly, no matter what its future holds, it is unlikely to repeat that growth within such a short time frame. However, history suggests that the chip stock is more likely to pull back than rise over time.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The rise (and possible future decline) of Sandisk

Indeed, when Sandisk spun off, it did not appear to be on the verge of massive growth. The company specializes in NAND memory and solid-state storage products. In general, memory and storage are commoditized products, and thus, the companies in that business tend to not attract as much investor interest.

Nonetheless, the boom in AI centers led to unprecedented demand for flash storage solutions. The stock price surged as AI stock investors and institutional investors took notice. Soon after, Sandisk joined the Nasdaq-100 and the S&P 500 , leading to additional buying.

The company's financials also played a major role in its gains. Its net income was over $11 billion in fiscal 2026, far better than the $1.6 billion loss in the previous fiscal year.

That profit left it with an attractive valuation despite its massive stock gains. Currently, its P/E ratio is 19, and the immediate future appears bright as its forward P/E stands at just 6.3.

Ironically, seasoned investors' long-term memory may explain the low valuations. These shareholders know that memory companies tend to experience more volatile industry cycles than tech stocks in general. This is because memory and storage command tremendous pricing power in boom times. However, when the down cycle begins, lower demand and price cuts can reduce or even wipe out company profits.

Sandisk has signed customers into long-term contracts, which could mitigate a down cycle. Still, slumps can be exceptionally painful for memory stocks. In the nearly nine years Western Digital owned Sandisk, its stock gained over 75%. Still, since it earned all of those gains in the first year of ownership, it is easy to see why Western Digital later doubted the wisdom of the merger and decided to spin off Sandisk.

Story Continues

The performance of both Sandisk and Western Digital stocks since the separation indicates the AI boom would have ended the slump with or without the separation. Still, performance in previous years suggests storage stocks have not performed well historically, possibly pointing to pain for Sandisk in the foreseeable future.

Should you buy Sandisk stock right now?

The history of Sandisk and its industry in general suggests one should approach its stock with caution.

With Sandisk dominating the S&P 500 in 2026, it implies that it is the stock to own. Still, the stocks in that industry have faced huge sell-offs once the boom ends. That history may also explain why investors have not bid the stock higher despite its 19 P/E ratio.

Indeed, if revenue forecasts prove accurate, Sandisk stock could continue rising. Nonetheless, given Sandisk's history and the history of the memory and storage industries in general, investors should probably assume they missed out on this boom.

news.Title: Citadel's Ken Griffin Says AI is in a Bubble Right Now. Billionaire Data Center Backer Jon Gray of Blackstone Disagrees.
news.Content:
Ken Griffin, founder and CEO of Citadel, declared at his firm's Future of Global Markets Conference on October 20 that investors are "almost certainly" in an AI bubble, drawing a direct parallel to the dot-com era and the telecom fiber-optic overbuild of 2000. It's quite a hot take after Citadel's own amended second-quarter SEC filing revealed approximately $8.6 billion invested across five major AI companies, with Amazon (AMZN) and Nvidia (NVDA) ranking as the firm's second and third largest individual stock holdings respectively.

Just two days after Griffin's warning, Blackstone (BX) President and COO Jon Gray countered during a CNBC interview that investors should not fear the AI boom turning into a bubble, expressing confidence in the underlying strength of demand for computing power.

More News from Barchart

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Jensen Huang Says the Next Wave of AI Is Physical. Forget Nvidia and Tesla, I'd Bet on These 2 Mid-Cap Stocks Instead.

Dear Future Anthropic IPO Investors, Mark Your Calendars for October 23

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

As with Griffin, Gray has a tremendous stake in the AI buildout, to the tune of about $200 billion in data centers alone.

Griffin's Three Vulnerabilities, and a $193 Billion Bond Binge

Griffin's concerns center on three specific vulnerabilities: GPU supply outstripping demand; the questionable useful economic life of AI chips that still command extraordinary rental rates five or six years on; and corporate America's highly uneven track record of extracting genuine productivity gains from AI spending.

The scale of capital pouring into AI infrastructure underscores the worry, as Amazon, CoreWeave, Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft, and Oracle (ORCL) had issued approximately $193 billion in bonds by early August to finance AI-related infrastructure — a staggering leap from $16.7 billion in all of 2024.

UBS projects hyperscalers will spend $4.1 trillion on AI infrastructure between 2026 and 2028, nearly triple the preceding six years, while Anthropic's planned spending alone reportedly approaches $750 billion in additional computing capacity.

Gray's Counterweight: Pricing Power and Constrained Supply

Gray's counterargument rests on the observation that demand for computing power remains robust across Blackstone's private portfolio, while supply delivery stays constrained.

Story Continues

He noted that for neocloud companies like CoreWeave (CRWV), compute pricing has risen 50%, legacy chips are worth more than anticipated, and data center leases sit below market rates — a notable but underappreciated signal that the supply-demand imbalance still favors builders.

Gray acknowledged financing challenges facing CoreWeave, which carries roughly $51.6 billion in total debt, but expressed confidence that well-managed firms will navigate the pressure.

Again, it's worth pointing out that the Blackstone exec is largely talking his book when he shares his bullish view on AI.

"On a call with analysts Thursday, the firm said that AI-related holdings represent about 7% of its roughly $1.4 trillion of assets under management," reported Bloomberg of the asset manager's quarterly results.

Citadel's Portfolio Tells a Different Story

Griffin's own behavior complicates his bubble warning in a striking way.

Citadel increased its Amazon stake by 34% and its Microsoft (MSFT) position by 43% during the second quarter, even while reducing Nvidia shares by 37% — a pattern suggesting the firm sees selective opportunity rather than indiscriminate froth.

Furthermore, Citadel profited handsomely when AI hedge fund Situational Awareness was forced to liquidate roughly $35 billion in positions at a steep discount in July, with Citadel subsequently shedding more than 80% of the acquired risk.

The Semiconductor Selloff Adds Urgency

The market digested these competing narratives in real time on October 22, as the Nasdaq Composite ($NASX) fell more than 2% after Meta's earnings report triggered concerns about massive capital spending plans and new non-voting share issuance.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ($SOX) dropped 6.7% to its lowest level since late July, shedding more than $616 billion in market value, while Blackstone (BX) itself rallied 8% after its own earnings beat.

The Next Catalyst to Watch

The tension between Griffin's historically informed caution and Gray's conviction in constrained supply will face its most important near-term test when Nvidia reports earnings on November 17, with guided revenue of $108 billion representing the single clearest verdict on whether AI spending is producing returns commensurate with the unprecedented capital deployed.

news.Title: Meta Approves New Non-Voting Stock Class Worth Billions to Zuckerberg — But the Real Price Was an 8-Year Residency Cage
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (META) disclosed on October 21, 2026, that its board approved a new class of non-voting Class C common stock structured in significant part to address CEO Mark Zuckerberg's personal exposure to California's proposed Proposition 40 — a one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires that could saddle him with a liability exceeding $12 billion on an estimated net worth of $240 billion to $247 billion.

The buried detail that may matter more than the tax math: Zuckerberg committed to remaining a California resident — or wherever Meta maintains its corporate headquarters — for eight years, a binding concession the board's special committee of independent directors deemed essential during what it called an era of intensifying AI competition.

More News from Barchart

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Jensen Huang Says the Next Wave of AI Is Physical. Forget Nvidia and Tesla, I'd Bet on These 2 Mid-Cap Stocks Instead.

Dear Future Anthropic IPO Investors, Mark Your Calendars for October 23

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

A Two-for-One Split With a Bespoke Twist

The arrangement functions as a two-for-one stock split, granting every holder of existing Class A and Class B shares one new Class C share per share held, with the new class carrying no voting rights and taking effect on January 19, 2027.

Critically for Zuckerberg, 20% of his Class C allocation can be sold immediately, representing approximately 10% of his overall economic stake. That provides liquidity to cover a potential wealth tax bill without surrendering any of the voting power that currently gives him roughly 60.6% control of the $1.8 trillion company.

The remaining 80% of his Class C shares are "stapled" to his voting stock, with restrictions gradually lapsing over eight years contingent on continued leadership.

Why the Board Said Yes

Meta's special committee framed the residency commitment as operationally vital, citing the company's need for Zuckerberg's physical proximity to its Menlo Park headquarters and Meta Superintelligence Labs. The filing explicitly referenced operational difficulties Meta experienced during the COVID-19 pandemic when Zuckerberg was physically separated from his management team.

According to the disclosure, Zuckerberg warned Meta's board over several months that he was actively evaluating, and at one point intended, to relocate his primary residence out of California and list his roughly $110 million Palo Alto compound for sale.

Story Continues

The Governance Gap Widens

However, the structure undeniably widens the already substantial gap between Zuckerberg's economic interest of roughly 13.4% and his 60.6% voting control — a governance concern that caused Meta to abandon a similar plan in 2017 after shareholder litigation. Negotiations were reportedly contentious, with committee members at one point discussing resignation if concessions could not be reached.

The new share class also serves broader corporate purposes: Meta's internal forecasts indicate it may need to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years to fund AI infrastructure, and the Class C stock provides a vehicle for capital raises, employee compensation, and acquisitions without diluting Zuckerberg's control.

Prop 40 Looms, and So Does a Legitimacy Question

The broader political backdrop adds a layer of uncertainty, with recent polling showing Proposition 40 narrowly short of majority support at 46% in favor versus 43% opposed ahead of the November 3 voter decision.

Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page have already left California, with Brin contributing approximately $100 million — 30% of the $333 million raised by the anti-Prop 40 committee.

Conversely, Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang has publicly stated he would not object to paying an estimated $8 billion bill.

What Happens if the Tax Never Arrives?

If Proposition 40 fails and Meta nonetheless proceeds with the Class C issuance in January 2027 on these terms, shareholders will reasonably question whether the board restructured the company's capital around one individual's personal tax concerns without ultimate justification.

The deal reveals the extraordinary leverage a founder-CEO with dual-class voting control can exert — effectively compelling a $1.8 trillion public company to engineer a bespoke financial solution for his personal circumstances while framing it as aligned with shareholder interests.

news.Title: Fortinet (FTNT) vs. CSCO and PANW: Can Its Hardware-Software Advantage Support Long-Term Growth?
news.Content:
Is FTNT a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Fortinet, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on FTNT. Fortinet, Inc.'s share was trading at $170.93as of October 20th 2026. FTNT's trailing and forward P/E were 61.58 and 45.05 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a cybersecurity company pitched as a great investment. FTNT shares gained 101.90% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like CrowdStrike and Cisco Systems gained 81.86% and 51.02%, respectively, during the same period. Protecting businesses from cyber threats can create lasting demand, but a stock that has more than doubled also raises expectations. Does FTNT still offer an attractive buying opportunity, or has too much optimism already been priced in?

GlebStock/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 12 Best Growth Stocks Trading in Oversold Territory and FTNT ranked #12 in that article. FTNT returned 14.34% since then. So, hedge funds were right about FTNT. This article explains why Jim Cramer favors Fortinet alongside CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) provides cybersecurity solutions that combine hardware, software, and security services. Its fastest-growing opportunity right now is enterprise cybersecurity demand, and that is central to understanding the stock. As companies expand into the cloud, adopt AI, and face more sophisticated cyberattacks, they need stronger network security — an area where Fortinet specializes.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

Revenue over the past year came in at $7.5 billion, up nearly 19%, with gross margin at 80.2% and operating margin at 32.4%. Despite this strength, the stock isn't cheap: it trades at about 54 times trailing earnings and 45 times forward earnings, well above the peer median of roughly 33 times, suggesting investors are betting on several more years of growth rather than paying only for today's numbers.

The bullish case is that Fortinet can keep growing alongside the expanding cybersecurity market while converting that growth into strong cash flow. Unlike many competitors, it builds its own hardware and software together — including its FortiASIC security chips — which helps it stand out in firewall and network security markets. Results back this up: the company generated $2.2 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year, holds a net cash position of $3.6 billion, and posted a very high return on equity of about 150%.

Story Continues

Management keeps expanding the platform, including its August 2026 purchase of Virtue AI, a company focused on AI-related cybersecurity, aimed at strengthening its position in that growing niche. If businesses keep raising security spending, bulls see years of growth ahead rather than a short-lived cycle. Still, the company needs to prove it can sustain its growth rate and protect its high margins without losing ground to competitors.

Recent results support the bullish story. Second-quarter revenue grew 26% year over year to $2.05 billion, and product revenue jumped 52% to $773 million — both signs that demand is accelerating. Billings, a signal of future revenue, rose 33% to $2.37 billion, while free cash flow reached $966 million for the quarter. Following these results, management raised full-year guidance, now expecting revenue between $8.02 billion and $8.18 billion and adjusted earnings per share between $3.41 and $3.47. The stronger outlook backs the case that growth is broad-based, though investors will want to see whether this pace holds up.

Investors are also watching how durable this growth is, not just how large it is. Fortinet's high margins reflect real pricing power and scale, but holding them steady could get harder as competition rises and enterprise customers grow more selective about spending.

Valuation remains the central debate around Fortinet's stock. Bulls argue that if growth and margins keep improving, the stock could reach $220, while a base case of around $165 assumes steady execution and a stable valuation. The bear case, on the other hand, sees the stock falling toward $102 if growth slows, margins shrink, or investors decide the current multiple is too rich. That range reflects real disagreement about how much more Fortinet can grow into its premium price tag. With the stock trading at about 54 times trailing earnings and 45 times forward earnings, continued strong execution is essential to justify that premium.

AI security is a promising growth avenue, but cybersecurity spending still tends to concentrate among a relatively small group of large enterprise customers, adding some unpredictability. The Virtue AI acquisition gives Fortinet a foothold in AI security, but it still needs to show these new products can translate into meaningful revenue. Investors should also watch ongoing shareholder lawsuits and the company's reliance on specialized chip suppliers, both of which could pressure sentiment if conditions worsen.

Another risk for the stock is the potential loss of customer trust if Fortinet's security products fail to protect against cyberattacks. Customers rely on its firewalls and software to protect critical systems, so an exploited vulnerability could damage trust in the wider platform. Fortinet warns that product defects and unsuccessful security updates could expose customers to attacks or disrupt operations. Its integrated approach makes reliability across those products especially important. A serious incident could slow new sales and weaken subscription renewals. Remediation and customer support costs could also weigh on margins. In our opinion, this could pressure Fortinet's price multiples if customers question its ability to provide the protection underpinning its growth story.

Hedge fund positioning shows a strong signal for Fortinet (see why Emerald Wealth Partners is bullish on FTNT ). As per our database, 62 hedge funds held the stock at the end of the second quarter, up from 52 in the previous quarter. This notable jump suggests institutional investors are growing more confident in the company's growth prospects, profitability, and balance sheet strength, even with its rich valuation. By comparison, Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) was held by 89 hedge funds, up from 87, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) was held by 101 hedge funds, up from 97, and CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) was held by 89 hedge funds, up from 79. The increase in hedge fund ownership across Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Cisco Systems, and CrowdStrike points to continued institutional interest in cybersecurity. CrowdStrike saw the strongest increase in conviction, while Fortinet's larger jump compared with Palo Alto Networks and Cisco Systems highlights improving sentiment despite the company's premium valuation.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for the group. Just 2.06% of Fortinet, Inc.'s float is sold short, compared with 2.66% for Palo Alto Networks, Inc., 2.60% for CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc., and 1.30% for Cisco Systems, Inc. Bearish bets remain low across all four stocks, suggesting limited outright bearish conviction. Fortinet, Inc.'s short interest sits above Cisco Systems, Inc.'s but below Palo Alto Networks, Inc.'s and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.'s, indicating somewhat more skepticism than Cisco Systems, Inc. faces, but less than its other two peers.

Valuation Analysis

FTNT's forward P/E is 45.05x. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc., Cisco Systems, Inc., and Palo Alto Networks, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 208.33x, 19.80x, and 94.34x, respectively. FTNT's own forward P/E was 27.17x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 66% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects significant investor confidence in accelerating cybersecurity demand, Fortinet's integrated platform, and its strong profitability. However, its discount to CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks does not establish a bargain, since differences in growth prospects and earnings adjustments limit direct comparisons. Fortinet, Inc.'s second-quarter adjusted earnings per share increased from $0.64 to $0.90, representing approximately 41% growth, alongside revenue growth of approximately 26%. We believe this performance supports a premium, but investors should not assume that one quarter's earnings growth will continue long enough to justify 45.05 times forward earnings, particularly after the substantial increase in its multiple. If Fortinet sustains strong earnings growth and protects its margins, profits could support further upside, but we would prefer a lower entry valuation to reduce the risk that a falling P/E offsets those gains.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Fortinet, Inc. (FTNT) by Dan in January 2025, which highlighted Fortinet's AI-powered cybersecurity expansion, acquisitions, product innovation, and Secure Networking growth. FTNT's stock price has appreciated by approximately 79.94% since our coverage. We believe FTNT could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its premium valuation could limit returns even if earnings continue growing strongly.

Fortinet, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While FTNT could benefit from growing cybersecurity demand and expansion into AI security, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential at more attractive valuations, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than FTNT and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: Stocks Fall Sharply on Risk-Off as Meta Slides -7%
news.Content:
The S&P 500 Index ($SPX) (SPY) fell -1.21%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DOWI) (DIA) rose +0.02%, and the Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) (QQQ) fell -2.90%. December E-mini S&P futures (ESZ26) fell -1.18%, and December E-mini Nasdaq futures (NQZ26) fell -2.79%.

A heavy bout of risk-off selling pushed both tech stocks and the broad market lower. Investors resumed dumping chip and AI-related stocks, and the broad market fell as investors reduced stock exposure and covered losses. Gold and crypto are also fell as investors licked their wounds and raised cash. Bond prices benefited, with the 10-year T-note yield plunging -16 bp.

More News from Barchart

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Jensen Huang Says the Next Wave of AI Is Physical. Forget Nvidia and Tesla, I'd Bet on These 2 Mid-Cap Stocks Instead.

AST SpaceMobile Stock Gets a New Catalyst. Wall Street Sees 93% Upside.

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

Tech stocks led the charge lower on fresh unwinding of chip and AI-related stocks. Meta (META) fell -7% even after CEO Zuckerberg said the company's AI investment is starting to pay off. Tesla (TSLA) fell -3.1% after trimming its capex plans. Lam Research fell more than -11 after the chip company delivered disappointing guidance.

Stocks were also undercut by a +2.2% rally in WTI oil prices on Middle East tensions after there were several attacks in the past two days by the Houthi militia on targets in Saudi Arabia, including an oil field, a port, and an airport in Dammam. The US State Department also said Wednesday afternoon that it was evacuating non-essential personnel and families from Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi evacuation sparked some market speculation that the US might be planning a new wave of attacks on Iran and/or the Houthis after the November 3 election. Indeed, the New York Times reported Thursday that the US and Israeli militaries have developed specific plans for renewed military strikes against Iran after the US and Israeli elections, although the report said President Trump has not yet approved those plans. The goal of a new military attack would be to deliver a knockout punch to Iran that would topple the government or at least force Iranian leaders to capitulate to US demands, although that has so far only been a fever dream of US planners.

Story Continues

Stocks are supported by the prospect of solid quarterly earnings. According to data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence, Q3 S&P 500 earnings are expected to climb by +25% from a year earlier, up from a July estimate of 22%. As of Thursday, 113 of the S&P 500 companies have reported results, with 80% beating estimates.

Markets are discounting a 7% chance of a +25 bp Fed rate hike at next week's FOMC meeting on October 27-28.

Overseas stock markets closed lower on Thursday. The Euro Stoxx 50 fell -1.94%. China's Shanghai Composite closed down -1.48%. Japan's Nikkei-225 Stock Average closed sharply lower by -2.65%.

Interest Rates

December 10-year T-notes (ZNZ6) rose by +1-07/32 points. The 10-year T-note yield fell sharply by -15.6 bp to 4.963%. T-note prices saw safe-haven demand tied to the sharp sell-off in stocks and increased tensions in Saudi Arabia as the US State Department evacuates non-essential personnel. Also on the bullish side, the 10-year breakeven inflation expectations rate fell -3.2 bp to 2.336%. The odds of a Fed rate hike at its meeting next week fell to 7% from 15% on Wednesday.

European government bond yields fell. The 10-year German bund yield fell -7.9 bp to 3.342%. The 10-year UK gilt yield fell -4.6 bp to 5.332%.

Markets are discounting a 2% chance of a +25 bp ECB rate hike at the ECB's next meeting on October 29.

US Stock Movers

The Magnificent Seven all fell on Thursday, except for Apple (AAPL), which closed up +1.3%. Aside from the sharp sell-off in Meta, Amazon (AMZN) and Nvidia (NVDA) fell more than -4%. Tesla (TSLA) fell -3.2%, Alphabet (GOOGL) fell -2.9%, and Microsoft (MSFT) fell -2.1%.

Meta (META) fell -7% after the company, in its earnings report Wednesday afternoon, raised its target to $825 billion from $700 billion of future spending commitments, mostly related to computing power and AI-related infrastructure. The higher spending plans were positive for companies that deliver those services but raised questions about whether Meta will achieve a sufficient return for investors on that massive investment level. The company also announced a new class of nonvoting stock that could be used to raise more capital, although that could dilute earnings per share for current investors. Revenue and earnings were better-than-expected, with Q3 revenue rising +26% to $64.6 billion and earnings of $3.83 a share beating the $3.57 consensus.

Tesla (TSLA) fell -3.2% after Wednesday afternoon's mixed earnings report and concerns about the company's lagging capex investment. Q3 revenue of $28.05 billion was down -0.2% y/y and was slightly below the consensus of $28.13 billion. Q3 adjusted EPS of 48 cents/share was better than the consensus of 44 cents. Tesla's self-driving subscriptions rose +67% y/y to 1.74 million, above expectations of 157 million. Tesla's main bullish driver this week was Elon Musk's attempt to force a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, folding Tesla's mixed prospects into the bigger SpaceX rocket-and-AI theme.

LAM Research (LRCX) fell more than -11% after its guidance for adjusted fiscal Q2 earnings was slightly weaker than expected. The negative Lam news helped lead to a broad sell-off in chip stocks, with KLA (KLAC) and GlobalFoundries (GFS) down more than -9%. Marvell Technology (MRVL), Intel (INTC), and AMD (AMD) fell more than -8%.

Crypto stocks fell, with Bitcoin's sell-off of -3.9%. Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell -9.5%, Iren Limited (IREN) fell -8.6%, and Riot Platforms (RIOT) fell -8.0%.

IBM (IBM) spent most of the day on the downside but closed slightly higher. Its earnings report raised doubts about its growth sustainability, even though the company's IT services results improved.

Procter & Gamble (PG) rallied more than +5% on above-consensus sales and earnings and relief that the company's limited price hikes didn't put a bigger dent in earnings.

Spotify Technology (SPOT) rallied more than +11% after earnings and guidance suggested improving profit margin trends.

Las Vegas Sands (LVS) fell more than -2% on disappointing earnings.

news.Title: Alphabet (GOOGL) vs. MSFT and AMZN: Can AI Investments and Google Cloud Growth Unlock a 26% Upside?
news.Content:
Is GOOGL a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Alphabet Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on GOOGL. Alphabet Inc.'s share was trading at $334.76 as of October 21st 2026. GOOGL's trailing and forward P/E were 17.62 and 22.83 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a technology company pitched as a great investment. GOOGL shares gained 35.20% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Amazon gained 20.50% during the same period. Strong gains can attract investors, but GOOGL's recent pullback raises a different question: has the weakness created a buying opportunity, or is there more reason for caution?

Photo by Firmbee.com on Unsplash

In July, we published an article about the 10 Best Quantum Computing Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever and GOOGL ranked #3 in that article. While GOOGL has edged slightly lower since then, the #1 stock in that list returned 41.18% over the same period. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick while GOOGL's performance has been more subdued. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on GOOGL. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) provides internet services and technology platforms through Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets. Its core business still centers on Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Maps, and advertising, but the real question for investors is whether artificial intelligence and cloud computing can become its next big growth drivers. Over the past year, revenue reached $445.9 billion, up 20.1%, and profitability improved as well, with margins climbing to healthy levels. The stock trades below the industry average on a headline basis, which on the surface makes it look cheaper than peers — though once one-time gains are stripped out, the valuation looks closer to the sector average. In short, the market isn't just paying for what Alphabet Inc. earns today; it's betting on years of AI and cloud-driven growth ahead.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The bullish case is that Alphabet Inc. can use its massive existing user base to turn AI into real revenue across multiple businesses. Google Search keeps driving advertising income, while Google Cloud is emerging as a fast-growing enterprise business as companies adopt AI tools and Gemini-based products. Recent results back this up: quarterly revenue grew 24% year over year to $119.8 billion, and Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion as businesses ramped up spending on AI infrastructure. If that trend continues, bulls believe Alphabet Inc. can grow both from higher cloud demand and new ways to monetize AI across its platforms.

Story Continues

The company is backing this optimism with money: it raised its capital spending plans to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion to build out data centers and AI capacity. It can afford to, given a net cash position of $144.3 billion and $164.7 billion in operating cash flow last fiscal year. That financial cushion means Alphabet Inc. can keep funding its AI buildout without straining its balance sheet, which supports the bull case that this could be a multi-year growth story rather than a single strong quarter. You can check out whether Amazon or Alphabet makes the stronger AI cloud investment case after the spending bill here .

Wall Street largely shares that optimism. The average analyst price target of $422 implies roughly 26% upside from current levels, with estimates ranging widely depending on how much credit analysts give to AI and cloud growth. For that upside to materialize, though, Alphabet Inc. will need to keep converting its AI investments into actual earnings growth — if that monetization slows, these expectations could prove too optimistic.

The biggest risk is that all this spending doesn't pay off fast enough. If AI is truly opening a new growth cycle, investors will expect the money being poured into infrastructure to eventually show up as stronger profits. Rising capital spending adds execution risk, and regulatory scrutiny over search and advertising practices could threaten some of Alphabet Inc.'s most profitable businesses. On top of that, newer AI-powered search tools are creating fresh uncertainty about the long-term strength of its core advertising model.

Another risk for the stock is businesses cutting advertising budgets when economic conditions weaken. Google can retain its users and search traffic while advertisers spend less to reach them. Alphabet generated more than 70% of its revenue from online advertising in 2025, leaving it heavily exposed to those spending decisions. Weaker consumer demand could prompt advertisers to reduce campaigns or lower their bids. That would pressure advertising revenue even without Google losing market share to AI competitors. Cloud growth may not fully offset a slowdown across its much larger advertising business. In our opinion, this dependence could pressure Alphabet's price multiples if advertising weakens before newer businesses contribute enough profit.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 275 hedge funds held Alphabet Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 265 the quarter before — a modest increase suggesting institutional investors remain generally confident in its AI and cloud story despite valuation and regulatory concerns. By comparison, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) was held by 273 hedge funds, down from 282, Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) was held by 369 hedge funds, up from 353, and Meta Platforms Inc. was held by 254 hedge funds, down from 262. Amazon.com Inc. clearly saw the strongest jump in institutional interest, while Alphabet Inc. gained ground compared with Microsoft Corporation and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), pointing to continued confidence in large-cap tech names tied to AI.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture. About 1.37% of Alphabet Inc.'s float is sold short, versus 0.82% for Microsoft Corporation, 0.88% for Amazon.com, Inc., and 1.52% for Meta Platforms, Inc. That's higher than Microsoft Corporation and Amazon.com, Inc. but slightly below Meta Platforms, Inc., suggesting some investors are watching Alphabet Inc.'s spending, valuation, and regulatory risks more closely than those of Microsoft Corporation and Amazon.com, Inc. Even so, short interest remains low across all four companies, suggesting limited outright bearish conviction across the group.

Valuation Analysis

GOOGL's forward P/E is 22.83x. Microsoft Corporation, Amazon.com, Inc., and Meta Platforms, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 25.13x, 23.64x, and 22.08x, respectively. GOOGL's own forward P/E was 28.01x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 18% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects significant investor concerns about rising AI spending, competition in search, and regulatory pressure. However, its modest discounts to Microsoft and Amazon and slight premium to Meta suggest the stock is reasonably priced rather than deeply undervalued. Alphabet Inc.'s trailing revenue increased 20.1% to $445.9 billion, while second-quarter revenue grew approximately 24%, although large investment gains inflated reported profits and should not be treated as recurring earnings growth. We believe Alphabet can justify 22.83 times forward earnings if its advertising and cloud businesses sustain double-digit earnings growth after rising infrastructure costs, allowing shareholder returns without requiring a higher P/E. If Alphabet turns AI demand into lasting profits and maintains sufficient cash flow after capital spending, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite its execution and regulatory risks.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) by FluentInQuality in May 2025, which highlighted its digital ecosystem, AI foundation, Google Cloud growth, and undervaluation. GOOGL's stock price has appreciated by approximately 111.2% since our coverage. We believe GOOGL could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if advertising and cloud growth sustain double-digit earnings growth after rising AI costs.

Alphabet Inc. is on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While GOOGL could offer long-term upside if AI and cloud growth translate into lasting profits, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than GOOGL and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: Buy, Hold, or Sell Meta Stock After Q3 Earnings & Stock Split Announcement?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms META) stock sold off on Thursday despite the social media giant delivering better-than-expected third-quarter results and announcing plans for a 2-for-1 stock split in early 2027.

While Meta's advertising business continues to grow impressively, concerns about surging artificial intelligence (AI) spending, deteriorating free cash flow, and mounting legal expenses have overshadowed its strong quarterly performance.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meta's Strong Q3 Results Overshadowed by Rising Costs

Meta reported Q3 revenue of $64.6 billion, climbing 26% year over year and topping Wall Street expectations of roughly $63.4 billion.

Reported earnings reached $3.83 per share, reflecting a $9.89 billion legal settlement charge. Excluding this charge, Q3 EPS was $7.40, exceeding expectations of $6.52 per share by 13%.

However, investors are increasingly concerned about Meta's aggressive AI investments, with quarterly capital expenditures reaching $34.91 billion. More concerning, free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion compared to positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion in the prior-year quarter.

Meta also narrowed its full-year capital expenditure outlook to $135-$145 billion, raising the lower end from $130 billion. Furthermore, the company faces additional legal uncertainty following a $25 billion judgment in a New Mexico privacy case, which Meta plans to appeal.

Despite these concerns, Meta expects Q4 revenue of $73-$76 billion, which came in range of analyst consensus forecast of $73.65 billion or nearly 23% YoY growth (Current Qtr below).

Meta Announces Effective 2-for-1 Stock Split

Adding to the intrigue surrounding its Q3 report, Meta announced plans to introduce a new class of non-voting Class C shares in January 2027.

Under the plan, shareholders will receive one new non-voting Class C share for every existing Class A or Class B share they own, effectively doubling their total shares. As a result, Meta's publicly traded Class A stock is expected to trade at roughly half its pre-split price, with the new Class C shares accounting for the other half of shareholders' investment value.

Although the split won't change Meta's overall market valuation or the total value of an investor's holdings, the lower share prices could make Meta more accessible to retail investors and potentially attract renewed buying interest following the recent selloff.

Meta's Earnings Estimates Were Trending Lower

Story Continues

Notably, Meta's earnings estimate revisions were trending lower heading into its Q3 report.

Over the last 60 days, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate for fiscal year 2026 (F1) has declined 7% from $32.20 to $29.94 per share, as shown below. Estimates for FY27 (F2) have slipped 1.69% from $34.41 to $33.83 per share.

These downward revisions reflect growing concerns about Meta's profitability as rising AI infrastructure investments weigh on operating margins and cash flow.

Bottom Line

Meta Platforms stock currently lands a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) , reflecting the unfavorable trend in earnings estimate revisions as investors weigh its aggressive capital spending against its impressive revenue growth.

Nevertheless, Meta's better-than-expected Q3 performance, resilient advertising business, and upcoming stock split could start creating a more attractive long-term buying opportunity amid the recent selloff.

For now, investors may want to wait for earnings estimates to stabilize and for greater clarity on AI spending before aggressively buying the dip.

news.Title: X-Energy Stock Surges on Potential Nuclear Energy Deal
news.Content:
Valued at a market capitalization of $4.4 billion, X-Energy (XE) designs and develops nuclear-reactor technology and manufactures nuclear fuels. It provides the Xe-100 small modular reactor (SMR) — which is designed to generate 80 megawatts of electric power or 200 MW of thermal output — as well as TRISO-X, a fuel for reactors.

X-Energy recently announced a partnership with American Electric Power (AEP) and Amazon (AMZN) to bring a SMR project to Indiana. Let's take a closer look at whether the partnership marks a buying opportunity for potential XE stock investors.

More News from Barchart

Crude Oil Prices Fall As Oil Continues to Flow Through Strait of Hormuz

Crude Oil Prices Rally After Close on US State Department Warning

Crude Oil Prices Rise on Saudi Tensions

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

X-Energy and AEP Eye 960 MW Nuclear Plant in Indiana

According to a statement, X-Energy and American Electric Power have signed a joint development agreement which covers feasibility work for a 960 MW SMR project in Sullivan County, Indiana. The plan calls for 12 Xe-100 units which will produce 80 MW of electricity each. The site sits near the retired Breed Generating Station, which AEP owns.

Amazon will provide project development funding as part of the agreement. This is the second deal under a larger plan between X-Energy and Amazon to add more than 5 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2039.

American Electric Power CEO Bill Fehrman said that the agreements with Amazon and X-Energy provide "all necessary capital protections and financial safeguards" the utility considers essential. Fehrman also said AEP wants to protect affordability for existing customers. "Together, we're looking to develop nearly a gigawatt of carbon-free power for the regional grid and pay our full costs without passing them to others," said Amazon Vice President of Data Center Infrastructure Capacity Delivery Josh Weissman.

AEP owns the land for the project and has decades of nuclear operating experience. Moreover, Amazon is paying for early development, while X-Energy brings the reactor technology itself to the table.

Indiana Governor Mike Braun and state lawmakers have reportedly passed investment and manufacturing tax credits since 2025. The state of Indiana has also launched an Advanced Nuclear Community program. The latest project with Amazon and AEP is X-Energy's third announced U.S. commercial Xe-100 plant and its fourth worldwide, sitting inside a roughly 11.5 GW pipeline.

Story Continues

On the company's Aug. 13 earnings call, X-Energy CEO Clay Sell said the firm was in the "final throes" of an agreement with a major investor-owned utility for its next 1 GW project. The new Indiana plan fits that description.

How X-Energy's Q2 Shows the Stakes

X-Energy went public in April 2026, and the second quarter was its first as a public company. X-Energy reported revenue and grant income of $54.6 million in Q2, up 154% year-over-year (YOY). Most of the top-line originated from reactor design work funded through the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP).

The ARDP program is the company's largest revenue source. The agency said it will add up to $1 billion to the award, lifting its total share to $2.1 billion. The government has already reimbursed $547 million through June 30, 2026.

Operating expenses totaled $164.6 million in Q2, while cash used in operations surged to $97.3 million, up from $20 million last year. X-Energy ended Q2 with liquidity of $1.9 billion and a debt-free balance sheet. Net proceeds from the initial public offering (IPO) totaled $1.1 billion.

Management noted on the Q2 earnings call that X-Energy has secured fuel supply deals with Centrus Energy (LEU) and General Matter. The company also holds about 7.6 metric tons of fuel material from the U.S. Department of Energy for its first Dow project.

Fuel Plant and U.K. Deal Add Momentum

In September, the company's TRISO-X fuel unit said it completed the main structure of its fuel plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The 214,000-square-foot site is expected to manufacture about 700,000 fuel pebbles per year, enough for up to 11 Xe-100 reactors. The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) granted the company's fuel unit a 40-year license earlier this year, and the plant is expected to be the "first new commercial-scale advanced U.S. nuclear fuel fabrication facility built in more than 50 years."

On Sept. 15, the company and Centrica (CPYYY) also said U.K. regulators accepted the Xe-100 into the Generic Design Assessment process. The review should take about three years. Centrica is the company's U.K. partner, and Centrica CEO Chris O'Shea noted the two companies want to build up to 6 GW of new nuclear capacity across the U.K. with Hartlepool being the first site.

What Should XE Stock Investors Watch for Next?

X-Energy will have to focus on execution over the next decade. The company is spending heavily on capital expenditures, and its biggest revenue source is federal money tied to cost sharing. The NRC is weighing the Dow plant in Texas, and X-Energy expects a decision by the first quarter of 2027.

XE stock could generate sizable returns over the next decade if it continues to beat revenue estimates and turns cash flow positive in 2030.

Overall, X-Energy has a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating on Wall Street. Out of 11 analysts covering XE stock, six recommend a "Strong Buy" rating, one recommends a "Moderate Buy" rating, three recommend a "Hold," and one analyst has a "Strong Sell" rating. The average price target of $32.89 represents potential upside of 210% from current levels.

news.Title: Google Is Paying SpaceX $11 Billion a Year for Compute. Here's the Concentration Risk Nobody Is Pricing In.
news.Content:
Alphabet 's (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) Google is one of the world's largest cloud infrastructure companies, yet it just started paying SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) $920 million per month -- or $11 billion per year -- to lease xAI's cloud infrastructure through 2029. Let's see why Google is renting that cloud compute from SpaceX rather than building more data centers -- and how that unusual deal could expose it to some unpredictable concentration risks in the future.

Why does Google need SpaceX's data centers?

Google controlled 15% of the global cloud infrastructure market in the second quarter of 2026, according to Synergy Research Group, putting it in third place after Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) Web Services (AWS) (28%) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) Azure (20%).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

From 2021 to 2025, Google Cloud's annual revenue more than tripled from $19.2 billion to $58.7 billion as the cloud and AI markets expanded, and Google seems like a great vertically integrated play on those secular trends. The tech titan builds its own data centers, produces its own custom AI chips, and hosts a broad range of market-leading cloud-based services and apps. It also ties all of those pieces together with Gemini and its other AI models.

But over the past few years, Google couldn't expand that infrastructure fast enough to keep pace with the AI market's explosive growth. It produced enough of its custom tensor processing units (TPUs) for its own first-party cloud services, but most of its customers needed access to Nvidia 's (NASDAQ: NVDA) graphics processing units (GPUs), which are better suited for training other AI models. Most of the top AI companies -- including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta Platforms -- use Nvidia's data center GPUs to process their AI tasks.

Nvidia controls over 80% of the data center AI chip market, and it locks in those customers with its proprietary software and services. A large portion of Google's servers already run on Nvidia's GPUs, but it doesn't have nearly enough chips to satisfy the market's demand for Nvidia-powered cloud computing services. To fill that gap, Google is willing to pay SpaceX $11 billion per year for continuous access to a cluster of roughly 110,000 GPUs.

Is that a smart long-term decision?

Google's deal with SpaceX instantly resolves a major bottleneck for its cloud infrastructure business. But if it had simply bought those 110,000 chips from Nvidia at $30,000-$40,000 apiece, it would have spent only $3.3 billion to $4.4 billion.

Story Continues

However, it would also have had to secure enough power to run those GPUs -- and it can take three to five years to set up new grid connections for data centers. Google would also need to pay massive energy and labor expenses to continuously operate those centers, and the value of its existing GPUs would depreciate as soon as Nvidia launches newer chips.

Moreover, it could take a long time for Nvidia -- which is still selling chips faster than it can produce them -- to actually fulfill that massive order. Instead of dealing with all of that, it makes more sense for Google to just pay $11 billion (less than 2% of its projected 2027 revenue) to instantly increase its cloud computing power and keep pace with Amazon and Microsoft. Paying SpaceX, in which Alphabet owns a 4%-5% stake, also makes more sense than paying a direct competitor in which the company doesn't own any equity.

But over the long term, this deal could expose Google to some major concentration risks. By paying SpaceX billions of dollars per year, it's essentially funding xAI's transformation into a future cloud infrastructure competitor in the generative AI market.

Google's deal with SpaceX further reinforces Nvidia's dominance of the data center market, rather than challenging it with its own TPUs. Moreover, that massive cluster is located at xAI's centralized facilities -- including its Colossus mega-clusters in Tennessee -- so any power failures or disruptions could impact a large portion of its cloud-based tenants.

For now, investors shouldn't fret too much over Google's deal with SpaceX, since it's a win-win situation for both companies. But it also exposes the limitations of Google's cloud infrastructure, as well as some future catalysts for xAI's growing cloud computing business.

news.Title: SpaceX stock slides as tech trade tumbles
news.Content:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock slid on Thursday, giving back Wednesday's post-earnings gain.

Shares jumped 7.8% on Wednesday following SpaceX's upbeat third quarter results and AI commentary.

The stock is under pressure — down 9% — along with the broader tech trade, following Meta ( META ) earnings and more headlines suggesting new strikes in the US/Israeli war with Iran.

As for SpaceX, it guided fourth quarter capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion, up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, as more compute capacity comes online. The company ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years," MoffettNathanson analyst Julie Zhu wrote in a note to clients.

"We are investment grade, have a very strong balance sheet, and there are a number of available pools of debt capital," SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said on the earnings call.

Then there's the merger talk. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla ( TSLA ) have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a tie-up, and that he is recused as a conflicted party. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said .

That endorsement created a "mess" for the process, a person with direct knowledge of the talks told Reuters . Insiders worry the resulting shareholder scrutiny could delay talks by several weeks.

Bloomberg separately reported that the companies are aiming to announce a deal in the first half of 2027.

On the flip side, Wall Street is now more bullish on SpaceX's prospects. JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target to $500 from $240, citing AI infrastructure growth. BofA raised its target to $275 from $235.

Barclays analyst Dan Levy flagged Tesla's annual meeting, which must be held by Dec. 6, as the likely venue for a shareholder vote. He added that a deal announced in late October or early November could push approval out six to 12 months.

news.Title: Meta stock falls 7% as AI spending fears return
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) stock closed out the trading day Thursday down 7% on, despite reporting better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue results Wednesday, as AI bubble fears remerged across Wall Street.

Investors pulled back on semiconductor and other AI stocks across the board on questions about whether massive investments in AI data centers will pay off in the long run.

Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimates to between $135 billion and $145 billion from $130 billion and $145 billion. The company also has $825 billion in various spending commitments related to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products.

Despite Wall Street's reaction to Meta's earnings, analysts were largely bullish on the company's outlook, owing to its prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg repeatedly pointed to Muse as a source of growth potential during the company's earnings call, saying "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years," as long as compute efficiency in AI systems continues to improve.

Meta posted an all-time high revenue of $64 billion in the quarter, well ahead of the $63.3 billion analysts anticipated. GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus expectations of $3.56, but would have been $7.40 without legal charges related to the company's teen mental health settlement.

The company also announced it will issue new non-voting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders , effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split. The move is meant to ensure Zuckerberg stays in California and retains voting control of the company if the state's Proposition 40 passes on Election Day.

Prop. 40 calls for a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

Ahead of Meta's earnings report, a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in connection with the state's consumer-harms case against the social media giant.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq tumble as tech stocks sink, oil prices surge
news.Content: US stocks fell on Thursday, led by the Tech ( XLK ) sector as the AI trade unwound and Wall Street assessed earnings from EV maker Tesla ( TSLA ) and social media giant ( META ). Investors flocked to bonds, sending Treasury yields lower as oil prices surged to a five-month high . The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) declined 0.3%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 1.5%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 2.7% as semicondcutor stocks fell, reversing gains from Wednesday's session. Meta shares tanked as investors weighed the company's quarterly results and 2-for-1 stock split announcement. Tesla shares were volatile after an earnings beat , as investors weighed lower 2026 capex against higher spending in 2027 and 2028 on Optimus, Cybercab, and Terafab. SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock fell, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain. Meanwhile, Blackstone's ( BX ) stock climbed 6% following the firm's upbeat outlook for upcoming investment sales after posting weaker third quarter earnings amid elevated borrowing costs. A report that the US and Israel are preparing for renewed attacks on Iran after the US mid-term elections sent Brent crude ( BZ=F ) to $113 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) climbed to $100. A deadly attack at a Saudi Arabian airport and oil field also put upward pressure on energy prices. In other news, jobless claims fell to 194,000 last week , the fewest in three months, underscoring how layoffs remain low. LIVE 11 updates 11 mins ago Ines Ferré Big companies are rethinking 'out of control' AI spending — and turning to cheaper models IBM ( IBM ) is calling attention to a growing trend among companies and their AI spending: They're keeping a closer eye on it. "I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what the true ROI of all of their AI spend is," IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said during the tech company's earnings call on Wednesday. "They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending is completely out of control with no real return," he added. Today at 6:00 PM UTC Meta stock drops more than 6% despite strong Q3 results, stock split Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports: Bitcoin ( BTC ) fell below $82,000 early Thursday as crypto joined a broader sell-off in riskier assets amid rising geopolitical tensions. The world's largest cryptocurrency traded around $81,600 Thursday morning, down more than 3% for the last 24 hours. Other major coins also declined. Crypto's total market value fell 1.4% over the previous 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap. Traders saw roughly $400 million in liquidations over the same period, according to data aggregator CoinGlass. Today at 4:55 PM UTC Jared Blikre The bond market is calling oil's inflation bluff If oil is about to spark an inflation wave, the bond market hasn't heard about it. The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX) is on track for its biggest one-day drop in more than two years on Thursday, slipping back below 5% as stocks slide. The 5-year yield (^FVX) is falling even faster. Meanwhile, Brent crude (BZ=F) is hovering around $112, up more than 50% since the Iran war began in late February. The surprise is how little the oil spike has moved the bond market's inflation forecasts. The 5-year breakeven — the inflation rate implied by the gap between regular Treasurys and inflation-protected TIPS — is a bit lower now than it was before the war. The 5y5y inflation swap is the market's forecast for average inflation over the five years starting five years from now, and the Fed watches it closely for signs that expectations are slipping. It has barely moved. So the jump in yields since February has been almost all about real rates — not inflation. Traders are betting the Fed keeps policy tight enough that $110-plus oil doesn't turn into lasting inflation. Not everyone buys it. Bloomberg strategist Simon White argues breakevens are "mispricing" the oil shock. Elsewhere in bondland, France's 10-year yield is above the US 10-year for the first time since 2013. Next up is the 5-year TIPS auction at 1 p.m. ET. Bloomberg's Alyce Andres calls it a referendum on the Fed's inflation bet under Chair Kevin Warsh. Weak demand would signal investors are starting to doubt it. Concerns over a slowdown in AI infrastructure build-outs overshadowed inflation fears stemming from higher oil prices. Today at 2:18 PM UTC Blackstone stock climbs 4% as executives give upbeat Q4 exit outlook Blackstone (BX) stock rose 4% Thursday morning, reversing earlier losses as executives at the alternative asset giant offered an upbeat outlook for investment exits and fee growth in the coming quarters. Blackstone CFO Michael Chae told analysts that performance-fee realizations from investments already under contract and expected to close in the fourth quarter would surpass the firm's total net realizations in the third quarter. He also reiterated expectations for "double-digit" growth in base management fees in 2027. The outlook offered investors some encouragement after Blackstone reported a 34% drop in net realizations during the third quarter compared with a year earlier while distributable earnings fell 9% in the same period. CEO Stephen Schwarzman described the quarterly results as "strong" amid a "volatile external environment" in a statement accompanying the earnings release. Today at 1:36 PM UTC Stocks retreat as investors digest tech earnings US stocks fell as investors digested earnings from Meta and Tesla while oil prices and government bond yields remained elevated. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) declined 0.3%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 0.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 1.4%. Shares of Meta ( META ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) each fell more than 3% at Thursday's open while Oil prices also rose while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) hovered around 5%. Today at 1:25 PM UTC Jared Blikre Chip stocks break below their bear-trap low Chip bulls sprang a bear trap on Tuesday. Two sessions later, they're the ones getting caught. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) is down about 4% premarket, below Tuesday's intraday low of $489.70. That was the floor of the bear trap — a breakdown that quickly reverses, catching traders betting on further losses. SOXX is on track for its lowest close since July 29. Lam Research ( LRCX ) is leading the slide, down about 9% after its results Wednesday night. Applied Materials ( AMAT ) and KLA ( KLAC ) are off about 6%, and AMD ( AMD ), Intel ( INTC ), and Sandisk ( SNDK ) are down 4% to 5%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is off a milder 2%. Semiconductor ETFs saw record flows over the past week, Bloomberg senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas posted Thursday. "Buying the dip here has [a] pretty good record of working," he wrote. There's little room to hide. Watch whether buyers come in yet again this session. A close above $490, roughly Tuesday's trap low, keeps the bulls' hopes alive — barely. news.Title: Better Buffett Stock: Alphabet vs. Apple
news.Content:
Former Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB) CEO Warren Buffett made several incredible investments. However, he was also noteworthy for letting some obvious ones get away.

One of those was Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), which he regretted not buying sooner. However, he remedied that mistake by purchasing shares not long before leaving his role. Current CEO Greg Abel has kept purchasing Alphabet shares, showing that he's also bullish on the stock.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Another stock that Buffett identified as a major value opportunity right away was Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) in the mid-2010s. This turned out to be one of Buffett's best investments ever, and while Berkshire has sold off the number of Apple shares it owns compared to its peak holdings, it's still the largest position in its portfolio.

The question is, between the two, which one is the better buy now? I think it's Alphabet, but the answer to that question may depend on whether you're bullish on AI or not.

Alphabet is going all-in on AI

Alphabet and Apple are taking two distinct approaches to the emerging AI landscape. Alphabet is going all-in on AI, and plans to spend about $200 billion on data center capital expenditures this year. The uses for these data centers range from being rented out via its cloud computing unit (a very profitable endeavor) to being used for compute capacity for its Gemini platform (not profitable right now). Regardless, Alphabet has positioned itself as an AI-first investment, but there are those who may be a bit wary regarding Alphabet's all-in position on an emerging technology.

Apple is taking the complete opposite approach. Instead of rapidly increasing its AI computing power, it's choosing to deploy Google's Gemini model on its devices, cutting development costs substantially. While it will have to pay to utilize Gemini, the cost to develop a new model may have been far higher in infrastructure and research and development (R&D) expenses. Furthermore, the AI features that Apple has rolled out are lackluster to some, although the revamped Siri AI is receiving positive reviews. Apple still has a long way to go before AI is a top product, and it could lose market share in the smartphone market to some Android phones that are pioneering this technology.

Story Continues

We'll see what happens, but whether you're bullish on AI or not may decide which stock you prefer. Regardless, here are other concrete factors we can look at to determine which stock makes more sense from a valuation standpoint.

Apple's stock has gotten expensive

It's no secret that Apple has long been one of the most expensive big tech stocks out there. It just entered its new fiscal year and trades at an impressive 36 times fiscal 2027 earnings (ending about Sept. 30).

AAPL PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

This is by far its most expensive valuation over the past few years, and could be an issue for future returns. If we assess Alphabet's stock from fiscal 2027's earnings projections, it is far cheaper.

GOOG PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

Alphabet trades for a mere 22 times next year's earnings, making it far cheaper. While Alphabet is one quarter behind Apple's results, which skews this figure in Alphabet's favor a little bit, it's still noteworthy enough that Alphabet is about two-thirds the price of Apple when that offset is accounted for.

Apple may be the more cash-conservative business, which Buffett would have loved; Alphabet is the cheaper stock. At the end of the day, I think Alphabet's lower stock price, combined with the major upside AI presents, makes it the better buy. Apple stock is expensive, and I might miss out on one of the most impressive technological shifts experienced in several decades. It just isn't as attractive to me, and I think there's a reason why Berkshire has been buying Alphabet stock recently and not Apple.

news.Title: Tesla, Meta, IBM: 3 earnings call shout-outs that left us thinking
news.Content:
Earnings season is in full swing, and Big Tech calls are about more than the heavy use of "superintelligence," which some read as a bid to please the White House after it reportedly disliked the term "artificial intelligence."

Here are three moments from the earnings calls of Tesla ( TSLA ), Meta ( META ), and IBM ( IBM ) on late Wednesday that stuck with us.

Tesla

Much of the focus today is on Tesla cutting its capital spending plans for this year to $20 billion from the $25 billion it guided to three months ago. A key factor appears to be that its Optimus robots need more training before they're released into the real world.

Elon Musk said investors should think of Optimus as a baby:

"A big difference with Optimus versus the cars is we don't have this vast fleet of cars from which we can gather training data. With Optimus, we have to bootstrap it by making the robots and having them do self-play, which is really how a human learns to navigate the world. You can see this when you have a toddler, and they grow up, and initially, they're sort of wobbly, and they don't know how to do things. Eventually they learn to wipe their own ass, which is a big milestone. As anyone who's had kids knows. Then they learn to read and do all sorts of things and be able to do these things. They learn this by playing. We actually need Optimus to play at scale in order to have it be really good at tasks in the real world."

Meta

Are early users of Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent overspending? Mark Zuckerberg's comments on credit limits during the earnings call suggest they might be.

That raises a bigger question: Could AI agent shopping end badly for retailers and banks, in the form of unpaid debts and write-offs?

"The most common use case for Muse is shopping, with more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size of over $200," Zuckerberg said on the call. "Plaid told us that they hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before. In the first week, we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected."

IBM ( IBM ) CEO Arvind Krishna seemed to be in a better place this earnings call compared to three months ago , which came on the heels of a shock earnings warning that sent the stock reeling.

It was interesting to hear Krishna call out some C-suite concerns about the current spending on AI tools:

"I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what is the true ROI of all of their AI spend. They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending completely out of control with no real return. But the way I have always characterized it is, there is no question to us, and this is the advice I give every C-suite member that I meet, that what we are trying to give people on AI, the productivity, the advantages of AI, the way it is going to change work, is very real. Let me not make any confusion around that."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: Meta has big plans for its Muse AI agent
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results after the bell Wednesday, with revenue hitting an all-time high. The company also announced a 2-for-1 stock split, with current stockholders getting one new Class C share for each share they own.

But the most interesting news out of Meta's report was about the future of the company's Muse AI agent and models .

During Meta's earnings call, Zuckerberg said that some 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up the Muse agent app since it launched. What's more, the most common use case so far is shopping, with the average purchase size over $200.

At Meta Connect last month, Zuckerberg said that the company would generate revenue via Muse by taking a small cut on sales made using the agent . And Wednesday, the chief executive said Muse's American average revenue per user (ARPU) could eventually eclipse American ARPU on the company's social media apps, which is already several hundred dollars.

Muse, like other AI agents and apps, devours computing resources. But Zuckerberg says that Meta anticipates the service's compute cost efficiency will improve 10x in the next year.

"If compute efficiency continues to improve quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years," he said during the call Wednesday.

Analysts on Wall Street reacted positively to the news.

"If you assumed Meta Connect was all hype, think again," Forrester principal analyst Kate Winick wrote in a note following Meta's earnings call.

"More than 10 million new users have tried Muse since launch, and Meta is feeling good about a few key signals: retention is strong and gets stronger with time for the most active users; spending is higher than expected – the average size of a purchase made via Muse is over $200; the most common connectors are email and productivity apps, which signals that at least some users are trusting Muse with a significant amount of personal data."

BofA Global Research analyst Justin Post predicted that Wall Street would come away from Meta's earnings with a more positive outlook on the company's AI investments thanks to the Muse news.

TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge, meanwhile, wrote in a note to investors that he estimates Muse will reach more than 1 billion daily active users over the next five years, but that Meta's leadership says the app could hit that mark even sooner.

news.Title: Why Meta Platforms Stock Took a Hit Today
news.Content:
Shares of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stumbled out of the gate on Thursday, falling as much as 7.6%. As of 1:10 p.m. ET, the stock was still down 7.2%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalysts that sent the social media and artificial intelligence (AI) company lower were its financial results and a change to its stock structure.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The good news

For the third quarter, Meta generated revenue that grew 26% to $64.6 billion, driven by robust advertising. This drove diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.83, up 265%. However, the company took a $9.9 billion charge related to its recent legal settlement regarding teen social media addiction. Excluding this charge, EPS would have been $7.40.

For context, analysts' consensus estimates called for revenue of $63.4 billion and EPS of $5.46, so if not for the charge, Meta would have easily surpassed expectations.

Other metrics were equally robust. The company's daily active users rose 3% year over year to 3.64 billion, while ad impressions and average price per ad increased 10% and 14%, respectively.

The not-so-good news

However, a change to Meta's stock structure was the headline. The company announced that its board of directors had established a new class of common stock -- non-voting Class C shares -- which will be effective Jan. 19, 2027. The company created this new class of shares to raise capital for its rising AI expenses, employee compensation, and potential acquisitions.

Meta will also use this new class of shares to effect a 2-for-1 stock split early next year, though the timing is still up in the air. The use of non-voting stock allows CEO Mark Zuckerberg to retain control of the company with a more than 60% voting interest thanks to his ownership of Class B shares, which carry 10 votes each, while regular Class A shares carry one vote each.

In other bad news, New Mexico hit Meta with a record $25 billion judgment for failing to protect user privacy in connection with the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal. Meta has said it will appeal.

At 22 times earnings, Meta is well below its 3-year average multiple of 27. While the stock is certainly cheap, investors should consider the risk associated with its legal exposure.

news.Title: Google’s Former CEO Eric Schmidt Owns About 1% of Anthropic — a Stake That Could Be Worth $20 Billion at IPO
news.Content:
Eric Schmidt wrote a check in 2021 when most of the investing world hadn't yet figured out what Anthropic could become. That check may now be one of the best bets of his career.

Former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about 1% of the company behind Claude. If Anthropic goes public at a $2 trillion valuation, that slice would be worth around $20 billion.
