Bloomberg reported Oct. 19 that Schmidt put tens of millions of dollars into Anthropic's Series A round in 2021, citing people familiar with the matter. PitchBook data valued the company at just $461 million at the time. Schmidt and Anthropic declined to comment, and it's unclear whether he has sold any shares since.

The Math Gets Wild Fast

At $2 trillion, a 1% stake comes out to about $20 billion before dilution and taxes. That would add roughly a third to Schmidt's estimated $57.5 billion fortune and push him close to $80 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Even at Anthropic's latest private valuation of $965 billion, the stake would be worth nearly $10 billion on paper.

Sponsored Content: A $9 Trillion Flying Car Market Is Taking Shape. This Company Is Open to Investors.

A $2 trillion valuation would be more than 4,300 times the company's Series A valuation, according to Bloomberg's reporting and PitchBook data. For comparison, Schmidt's venture firm Innovation Endeavors turned an early Uber Technologies (UBER) investment into a roughly 1,400-fold gain before the ride-hailing giant went public in 2019. Anthropic would leave that one in the dust.

Thanksgiving Could Bring a Debut

Anthropic is eyeing a stock market debut before the end of the year. Bloomberg reported that formal marketing could kick off as early as the week of Nov. 9, with trading possibly beginning before Thanksgiving. The company hasn't confirmed a date or a valuation.

The number may land lower than the $2 trillion figure. Reuters reported that some investors discussed a $1.5 trillion figure at an October meeting. At that price, a 1% stake would still be worth $15 billion before adjustments.

Story Continues

Revenue is a big part of the pitch. Anthropic told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter, according to Reuters . The company also reported adjusted profitability for the quarter.

A Long Game Built on Early Bets

Anthropic has landed major backing from Amazon (AMZN) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), along with other large investors. Schmidt has kept investing in tech since stepping down as Google's chief executive in 2011, through Tomorrow Ventures, Innovation Endeavors, and his family office, Hillspire. Artificial intelligence companies have taken up a growing share of that portfolio, and Anthropic is one of them.

Whether the windfall is $10 billion, $15 billion or $20 billion will depend on where Anthropic prices, how much of the stake Schmidt still holds and when he decides to sell. Either way, a check he wrote when Anthropic was valued at $461 million could end up as one of the biggest paydays of his career.

news.Title: Investors are punishing Big Tech's biggest spenders. Meta is the latest casualty.
news.Content: Apple ( AAPL ), Eli Lilly ( LLY ), and Walmart ( WMT ) have added more than $400 billion since chip stocks peaked in early October. Meta ( META ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and SpaceX ( SPCX ) have lost nearly twice that. Meta is the latest casualty. The stock is down more than 7% on Thursday, erasing about $125 billion in market value and slipping below its 2025 closing price. That wipes out its gain for the year. The social media giant is also on track for its third straight drop of 5% or more the day after earnings, a first since its 2012 IPO. Meta is stuck in a 2-year box Thursday's drop looks dramatic, but on a weekly chart, it barely registers. Since mid-2024, Meta has bounced between roughly $500 and $800, from its April 2025 low near $485 to its August 2025 record close of $790. Slipping below the 2025 close turns Meta red for the year. It doesn't change the trend. Only a break out of the box would. The broader damage is hitting the AI spenders. Since Oct. 6, Apple, Eli Lilly, and Walmart have climbed while Meta, Alphabet, and SpaceX have bled, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia ( NVDA ) alone has shed more than $600 billion as chip stocks broke a bear trap . The bill for AI is coming due Meta beat on revenue on Wednesday , with sales up 26% to $64.6 billion. But the company raised its full-year expense outlook and narrowed its capital spending plan to $135 billion to $145 billion. It also unveiled a new class of nonvoting shares it can sell to raise money. "He's not going to have the cash flow to support it. So he's going to have to raise capital, both debt and equity," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said to Yahoo Finance in reference to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Bond traders were already nervous. Earlier this week, the cost of insuring debt from Meta, Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet, and Microsoft ( MSFT ) climbed to its highest in months. Truist analysts wrote that Meta's AI investments "will take longer to generate returns." The core business is holding up, though. Luria said Meta is "gaining share from Google," with ad sales growing in the 20s. And Mark Zuckerberg told analysts that if compute efficiency keeps improving quickly, "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years." Watch for a weekly close outside the box. A move above $800 would be a breakout to new highs, while a close below $500 would open the door to a much deeper slide. Until then, the moves are just noise inside the range. news.Title: Ulta Beauty's website traffic just surged a whopping 48%
news.Content:
If you shop for beauty products, you have more choices than ever. Sephora sits inside Kohl's, Amazon sells prestige brands, and Target went all-in on its own beauty push after its split with Ulta , as TheStreet reported.

That crowded field has made investors nervous about Ulta for most of 2026. The worry is simple: if shoppers can find the same lipstick anywhere, why make the trip?

Ulta is still growing anyway. Net sales rose 8.9% to $3.04 billion in the second quarter, and comparable sales climbed 3.8%, according to the company's earnings release dated Aug. 27.

"Our team delivered another impressive quarter of strong sales, profit, and earnings growth," CEO Kecia Steelman said in the release.

However, Wall Street wanted proof that growth would hold up in the back half of the year, when the comparisons get harder.

According to a Bank of America research report reviewed by TheStreet, that proof may already be showing up on Ulta's website. Visits to Ulta.com jumped 48% from a year earlier in September, the bank said, citing Similarweb data.

What Bank of America found in Ulta's web traffic

The September jump wasn't a one-off. Site visits rose 38% through the first nine months of the year, with growth above 30% every month since April, wrote BofA analyst Lorraine Hutchinson in the Oct. 20 note, titled "Higher web traffic creates opportunity for 2H comp upside." That is a long streak for a retailer whose stock was punished over growth fears just two months ago.

"Consumers are engaged, and we are optimistic about ULTA's ability to convert this higher traffic into sales," Hutchinson wrote.

Digital sales have grown at a rate between the low double digits and the mid-teens in recent quarters, the bank said, yet they make up only about 20% of revenue. Steelman said on the August call that e-commerce posted its "sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sales growth," according to the Motley Fool transcript .

Related: Ulta Beauty's move to win back shoppers takes a new turn

That's where the bank sees upside. Ulta's guidance implies second-half comparable sales growth of 2% to 3%, and Chief Financial Officer Chris DelOrefice confirmed that range on the call.

The stock has already moved. Shares fell about 3% to $524 in after-hours trading on Aug. 27 as investors fretted about slowing growth, Investing.com reported. By Oct. 20, they stood at $591.62, according to the BofA note, a gain of roughly 13% by my math.

Beauty spending keeps beating the rest of retail

The broader category is giving Ulta room to run. Prestige beauty sales rose 7% to $17.1 billion in the first half of 2026, and mass beauty climbed 7% to $39.2 billion, according to Circana on Aug. 11.

Story Continues

More Retail :

Walmart gets unexpected boost from stubborn inflation

Bank of America sees a costly catch in America's strong economy

Bath & Body Works faces surprising problem as Americans return to malls

Skincare led prestige with 9% growth, while mass fragrance jumped 15%, Circana said. "Fragrance remains a key avenue for affordable luxury and self-expression," said Larissa Jensen, Circana's global beauty industry advisor.

Bank of America's own card data tell a similar story. Beauty spending rose 6.5% in the third quarter versus 4.8% for total retail excluding autos, the bank said, and the gap widened in September to 8.6% versus 6.3%.

Here is what Ulta and the bank point to as the drivers:

Bolder makeup: Steelman flagged "this fuller face look, more expressive eye" as a trend heading into the back half, according to the Motley Fool transcript .

Wellness: Steelman said wellness "could be one of our next big pillar categories," and BofA noted most loyalty members already buy wellness products elsewhere.

Social reach: Ulta's TikTok followers are up 27% this year and Instagram engagement is up 83%, Bank of America said in the note.

Competition: "We expect the battle for share to remain intense," Steelman said on the call.

Given that backdrop, it's easy to understand why Hutchinson thinks Ulta's heavy spending on loyalty, systems and supply chain is starting to pay off.

Why a $700 price target hinges on turning clicks into sales

The bank now values Ulta at 22 times its fiscal 2027 earnings estimate of $31.86 a share, up from 20 times. That multiple sits at the top of the 19-to-22 range for high-quality peers and below the 25 to 27 times that steady compounders fetch, Hutchinson wrote.

For the current year, BofA expects $28.74 a share, inside the company's raised guidance of $28.70 to $29.00. It sees earnings growing about 12% this year and 11% the next.

There's one catch in the data that I think investors should keep in mind. The Similarweb figures track Ulta.com only, the note says, and they exclude the app, which Steelman said accounts for "more than 60% of online sales."

That cuts both ways. The website surge could be shoppers browsing more before buying in stores, which the bank says still counts for an omnichannel retailer. It could also mean the app-heavy core of Ulta's digital business is growing more slowly than the headline number suggests.

Much will likely depend, however, on whether Ulta can turn visits into orders during a promotional holiday season. Management already acknowledged a more promotional environment in August, the Investing.com report found.

Target's exit adds another wrinkle. The traffic acceleration since April overlaps with the wind-down of Ulta's shop-in-shops inside Target stores, and in my analysis some of those shoppers may simply be finding Ulta online instead. The note doesn't make that link, so treat it as a theory worth watching in the third-quarter report.

For your wallet, a busier Ulta.com usually means more personalized offers aimed at keeping you loyal. Check your rewards account before you buy elsewhere this holiday season. I'd also compare prices across Ulta, Sephora and Amazon before checkout, since the same products often sit at all three.

Bank of America's view is that the investment cycle is turning into a harvest. "The trends support our view that ULTA can now harvest gains from prior investments and reinforce the value of ULTA's omnichannel model," Hutchinson wrote.

news.Title: Amazon Leads a Broader Wave of AI-Linked Job Cuts
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

E-commerce and cloud behemoth Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN , Financials ) is among a rising number of corporations shedding positions as expenditure moves toward artificial intelligence and automation.In January, Amazon said it was cutting 16,000 corporate jobs in a revamp targeting artificial intelligence and efficiency. The tendency is far larger than technology.HSBC is considering almost 20,000 cutbacks, Standard Chartered intends more than 7,000 reductions over four years, and Barclays is aiming for around 5,000 posts.Microsoft claimed it slashed 4,800 workers in July and Block indicated it will remove more than 4,000 people as it restructures to focus on AI.Meta, Cisco, Intuit, Cloudflare and others have similarly cut personnel while shifting resources to AI.The trend matters to investors because corporations are increasingly looking to artificial intelligence as a growth investment and a means to minimize costs.That can be supportive for margins over time, but also raises problems about execution, disturbance to the workforce and whether productivity improvements will come fast enough to warrant massive AI spending.Another area to watch: if more major corporations roll out restructuring plans once 2027 budgets are completed.

news.Title: Why Meta Stock Plunged Today
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) exceeded third-quarter forecasts, but shares fell more than 5% in Thursday morning trading as investors weighed AI costs and a change to its share structure.

Revenue for the quarter reached $64.60 billion, a 26% year-over-year increase and above the $63.33 billion consensus. Earnings came to $3.83 per share, topping expectations of $3.57, although results included a $9.89 billion charge tied to a settlement with 52 U.S. state attorneys general over teen mental-health litigation.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Advertising remained a key growth driver, with sales rising 26% to $63.06 billion. Meta projected fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion and raised the lower end of its 2026 capital spending forecast to $135 billion from $130 billion, while keeping the upper end at $145 billion.

Meta's board also approved a new non-voting Class C share. The company plans to distribute one new share for each existing Class A and Class B share in January 2027, a move expected to have the market-price effect of a two-for-one split without changing shareholder voting power.

news.Title: How much MSFT stock does Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella actually own?
news.Content:
Not many people remember this, but when Satya Nadella took the reins as CEO of Microsoft in February 2014, the company was struggling to find its place amidst a tech landscape dominated by Apple's smartphones, Google's Android operating system, and Amazon's cloud computing services.

Under the leadership of Steve Ballmer, Microsoft had undertaken a contentious $7.2 billion acquisition of Nokia's mobile phone business in 2013. That deal ultimately failed, resulting in billions in write-downs and thousands of layoffs .

But Nadella did not turn the company around overnight. Over the next few years, he shifted Microsoft's business model even further into cloud computing by expanding Azure and its subscription-based services . He also made strategic acquisitions , including LinkedIn, GitHub, and Minecraft, while investing billions into artificial intelligence before it became a household name.

In fact, you could say that Nadella was instrumental in Microsoft's partnership with OpenAI, as he even personally stepped in to serve as mediator when OpenAI's board briefly fired its CEO and co-founder , Sam Altman, in the fall of 2023.

Although Microsoft and OpenAI renegotiated their once-exclusive partnership, Microsoft hasn't lost momentum. Their newest agreement , announced in April 2026, gave each greater independence and allowed Microsoft to continue to expand its own AI capabilities through Azure's cloud services.

MSFT crossed the trillion-dollar valuation threshold on April 25, 2019, and it hasn't looked back since. In its most recent earnings, the company reported that Azure revenue grew by 43% year-over-year . These results show that Microsoft isn't just one of the founders of the digital era — it's very much a power player, and as the driver behind its innovation, Nadella himself has been rewarded handsomely through salary increases, bonuses, and enormous stock awards.

How much of MSFT does Satya Nadella own? Is he the biggest inividual shareholder?

As of Microsoft's latest Proxy statement for fiscal 2025, filed in September 2025, Satya Nadella owned 900,572 shares of Microsoft, equating to about 0.01% of the company's total outstanding shares.

Given MSFT's October 19 closing share price of $533.52, those shares would be worth a whopping $480.4 million.

But Nadella isn't Microsoft's biggest individual shareholder — not by a long shot.

That distinction actually belongs to Steve Ballmer, who is estimated to still own approximately 319 million shares, or roughly 4% of Microsoft. Despite Ballmer stepping down amid Microsoft's struggles, he still owns more than 350 times as much as Nadella's stake.

Story Continues

And in case you're wondering, even Microsoft's founder Bill Gates still owns about 103 million shares , valued at approximately $43 billion . That's substantially more than Nadella — even though Gates has spent decades giving away his fortune.

Related: How much MSFT stock does Microsoft founder Bill Gates actually own?

How much stock does Satya Nadella get as part of his compensation package?

To say that Microsoft's board of directors has been happy with Nadella's efforts is an understatement. In the company's latest Proxy statement , published in October 2025, the board stated that "Our exceptional fiscal year 2025 results demonstrate that Satya Nadella and his leadership team have positioned Microsoft as a clear artificial intelligence leader for this generational technology shift, enabling Microsoft to drive long-term growth through innovation, security, and quality."

Crediting Nadella for the company's 15% annual revenue growth and 17% increase in operating income, the esteemed CEO received a 117.00% payout in annual cash incentives and a 103.69% payout in performance stock awards.

Translated into dollars and cents, Nadella compensation can be broken down as follows:

Satya Nadella's fiscal 2025 total compensation

Category

Amount

Base salary

$2,500,000

Stock awards

$84,245,496

Annual cash incentives

$9,555,000

$196,294

Total fiscal 2025 compensation

$96,496,790

In total, approximately 87% of Nadella's compensation was in stock awards.

The $96.5 million compensation Nadella received in fiscal 2025 was an increase of about 22% from fiscal 2024, when he made $79.1 million.

Microsoft's largest institutional shareholders

Microsoft's largest institutional shareholder is The Vanguard Group. It holds 664,882,153 shares, or 8.95% of Microsoft, worth approximately $354.7 billion.

BlackRock Inc. is the next largest. It holds 540,020,228 shares, or approximately 7.30% of the company's total outstanding shares. Its stake is worth $288.1 billion as of MSFT's October 19 close.

news.Title: Microsoft, Google parent and McDonald’s protest new trading plan
news.Content:
Top publicly listed companies such as Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT), Google parent Alphabet (Nasdaq: GOOGL), Coreweave (Nasdaq: CRWV), Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS), and McDonald's (NYSE: MCD) have joined hands to protest the inclusion of the tokenized version of their stocks on the OKXICE TSV.

As per the public notice issued Oct. 19, the number of companies objecting to the plan is 16, demonstrating growing opposition to the tokenization trend.

What Microsoft, Alphabet, and McDonald's are opposing

The companies' protest centres on OKXICE issuing the tokenized version of their stocks.

In simple words, tokenization is the process of using blockchain technology to turn real‑world assets like stocks, real estate, U.S. Treasury bills, etc. into digital tokens which can be traded fractionally, 24/7.

Crypto companies such as Coinbase Global (Nasdaq: COIN), Robinhood Markets (Nasdaq: HOOD), and OKXICE are at the forefront of the tokenization trend.

The tokenized stocks are advantageous to traders who want to buy and sell shares 24/7. They also offer exposure to those from outside the U.S. who don't have access to avenues like the Nasdaq and the NYSE.

But they don't offer shareholder rights such as ownership and voting like original stocks do.

Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

JPMorgan's answer to the stablecoin threat is here

Major gold holder backs NVIDIA challenger

BlackRock's iconic fund posts strongest day in over 12 months

OKXICE TSV is a proposed tokenized stock trading platform created by OKXICE, a 50-50 joint venture between the NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX.

The avenue will operate under the innovation exemption published last month by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The exemption lets such platforms offer tokenized versions of the U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges.

The latest notice doesn't explain the companies' reasons or if their objection stops TSV from issuing the tokens. However, it says these tokens could be issued by an outside party or the issuer itself, which could give companies a more direct role in the process.

news.Title: Meta: 5 Reasons to Buy the Dip
news.Content:
Early Meta Muse Data is Extremely Bullish

"Muse," Meta Platform's ( META ) agentic AI offering, debuted in early September. In just over a month, Muse shot to the top of the Apple App Store rankings and became the fastest-growing consumer app in history outside OpenAI's ChatGPT. Beyond the rapid user growth, the latest data from Meta's earnings call revealed that each customer is more valuable than a typical AI customer. CEO Mark Zuckerberg explained:

"The most common use case for Muse is shopping. With more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size of over $200, Plaid told us that they hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before. And in the first week, we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected. Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar."

In other words, Muse users are premium, making it easier for Meta to monetize in the future.

Meta Retreats to the 10-week Moving Average

Most amateur investors focus too much on short term time frames and suffer from recency bias from the latest price movements. Conversely, seasoned investors understand the value of analyzing higher time-frame charts (like weekly charts) to filter out the noise and size up the overall trend.

Although Meta dropped ~5% Thursday after its earnings, the overall price trend remains firmly higher. From late July to late September, Meta shares ripped from ~$524 to $780 in a straight line. Before earnings, shares digested the move and traded sideways. However, after earnings, Meta shares tagged the 10-week moving average for the first time since the breakout. Historically, such pullbacks are high-probability buy-the-dip opportunities for investors.

Image Source: TradingView

Meta is Extremely Cheap

With a P/E ratio of just 23x, Meta is the cheapest "Mag 7" name.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meta's Top-Line Growth is Robust

Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest that Meta's revenues will grow at 20% or more through next year. Considering the robust double-digit growth and reasonable valuation, Meta is sure to attract growth-at-a-reasonable price (GARP) investors.

AI Impact on Ad Revenues

While Muse garners the most attention for Meta's AI efforts, its in-house AI optimization efforts are bearing fruit. In Q2, Family of Apps revenue rose 28% year over year to $60.4 billion as ad impressions increased 14% and average price per ad increased 12%.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Early data confirms rapid adoption and strong monetization potential for its Muse AI platform. Meta Platforms continues to prove its leadership in agentic AI. Combined with robust top-line growth, double-digit gains in digital advertising revenue, and a highly attractive GARP valuation of just 23x earnings, the recent post-earnings dip to the 10-week moving average presents a compelling, high-probability entry point for long-term investors.

news.Title: Wall Street sinks as Nasdaq falls over 2% on AI cost worries
news.Content:
By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

Oct 22 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq slid more than 2% on Thursday as growth stocks weakened after earnings from mega-caps Tesla and Meta did little to address AI-related concerns, with a recovery in ‌oil prices further adding to market unease.

Meta slipped 5.2% after the social media giant unveiled a new class of non-voting ‌shares to help fund its costly AI expansion. The decline came despite stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue and an upbeat fourth-quarter sales forecast.

The market weakness marked a sharp reversal from ​Wednesday, when robust results from SpaceX and Super Micro sparked an AI-fueled rally. The optimism faded as investors shifted their focus from earnings strength to the enormous capital required to build AI infrastructure and their uncertain return timeline.

The selloff put the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index on track to shed more than $616 billion in market value, while the Nasdaq-100 was set to erase nearly $1 trillion. The semiconductor index fell 5.6% to its ‌lowest since July 29.

"Semiconductors and the Nasdaq have ⁠been elevated to a huge degree by investors' rush to participate in the AI build-out. Investors are now reassessing the pace of AI spending and the returns that spending can generate," said Steve Sosnick, chief market ⁠analyst at Interactive Brokers.

Tesla fell 0.7% after the electric-vehicle maker cut annual capital expenditure forecast, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics ambitions.

Other constituents of the 'Magnificent 7' group also declined, with Amazon.com and Nvidia down more than 3% each.

At 11:58 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ​fell 29.18 ​points, or 0.06%, to 52,826.91. The S&P 500 lost 85.27 points, or 1.10%, ​to 7,671.90, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 551.50 points, ‌or 2.06%, to 26,152.90.

Six of the 11 S&P 500 sectors posted losses, led by technology, down more than 2.7%.

Consumer staples were leading the gains with a 2.5% rise. Procter & Gamble jumped 6.1% to a near eight-month high after the consumer goods giant beat first-quarter estimates.

The S&P 500 value index was flat compared to a 2.2% drop in its growth counterpart.

Brent crude was hovering near its five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions and a wider Middle East conflict. [O/R]

A flight to safety pushed the 10-year yield down ‌to around 5.0025%.

Meanwhile, weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fell, pointing to a resilient labor ​market and supporting expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged ​at its meeting next week.

Story Continues

On the earnings front, S&P 500 ​third-quarter profit growth is forecast at 32.3%, up from 30.7% previously, according to LSEG data.

Blackstone gained nearly 6% after ‌the alternative asset manager beat third-quarter profit expectations, while ​Chief Operating Officer Jon Gray said ​widening credit spreads on AI-linked debt could create opportunities to secure higher returns.

Lockheed Martin climbed 5.9% after the defense contractor raised annual sales and profit forecast.

Spotify rose 9% after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting ​on its AI-powered features to drive user growth.

Declining ‌issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.06-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by 1.23-to-1 on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 35 new ​52-week highs and three new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 70 new highs and 247 new lows.

(Reporting by ​Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar)

news.Title: Stocks drop as Meta dampens AI optimism; Treasury yields fall
news.Content:
By Caroline Valetkevitch and Amanda Cooper

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Major stock indexes dropped on Thursday as a report from Meta Platforms fanned worries about the AI trade, while US Treasury yields fell sharply and oil prices jumped.

The Nasdaq was down more than 2% ‌and led declines on Wall Street. MSCI's All-World index was off 1%, and tech shares in Seoul, Tokyo, Amsterdam and Paris fell earlier.

Shares ‌of Meta fell more than 5%. The first of the so-called AI hyperscalers to publish quarterly results, Meta reported third-quarter revenue late on Wednesday that beat expectations, but the company also unveiled a plan ​to issue non-voting stock that revived concern over its mounting capital commitments.

An index of semiconductors, among the biggest beneficiaries of AI spending, was down more than 5%.

Shares of Tesla, which also reported earnings and cut its spending forecast, eased 0.8%. Meanwhile, Reuters reported that some Tesla insiders were concerned that CEO Elon Musk's public comments on a potential merger with SpaceX could invite shareholder scrutiny and complicate deal talks. Shares of SpaceX were down 5.6%.

CONCERNS OVER SPENDING

Investor worries about AI spending and ‌how long the AI trade can last have led to ⁠sharp swings in indexes. The Nasdaq was up more than 1% on Wednesday following upbeat forecasts.

"To the extent investors believe that those (AI) earnings are real... they are buyers of these stocks," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a ⁠family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey.

"But periodically, when they look at current earnings and the amount they're going to have to spend, they become concerned that these stocks are all overpriced," he said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 114.55 points, or 0.22%, at 52,741.54, while the S&P 500 fell 97.15 points, or 1.25%, to 7,660.02 ​and ​the Nasdaq Composite fell 590.94 points, or 2.21%, to 26,111.92.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the ​globe fell 15.27 points, or 1.34%, to 1,122.61. The pan-European ‌STOXX 600 index was off 1.01%.

US Treasury yields dropped, with the yield on the 10-year note falling below 5% for the first time since September 23. Equity declines related to the sustainability of the AI outlook boosted the safe-haven appeal of government debt.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes was last down 15.17 basis points at 4.994%, from 5.146% late on Wednesday.

But concerns over France's strained public finances and continuing street protests hit French markets again.

Story Continues

French bond yields climbed, and France's 10-year government bond yields rose above those of equivalent US Treasuries for the first time since 2013, reflecting growing investor concern over France's deteriorating ‌fiscal position and rising debt burden.

France's benchmark 10-year yield was last up 6.5 basis points ​at 5.06%, after earlier touching 5.1415%, its highest level since July 2002. This week, the yield ​rose above 5% for the first time since 2002.

Also, the premium ​investors demand to hold French government debt over safe-haven German Bunds widened to its highest in 15 years.

OIL JUMPS

Geopolitical concerns played ‌out in oil markets. Brent crude climbed to its highest ​level since May after further Houthi attacks ​in Saudi Arabia raised fears of an escalation in the Middle East conflict and more disruption to oil supplies from the key exporting region.

US crude was last up 1.22% at $98.35 a barrel and Brent was at $111.25 per barrel, up 2.23% on the day.

The yen was on track for ​its strongest daily gain in almost a month, as ‌investors sought safety amid fragile equity markets.

The Japanese yen strengthened 0.51% to 157.33 per dollar. The euro was down 0.3% at $1.1198.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin ​fell 3.20% to $81,929.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Amanda Cooper in London; Additional reporting by Alun John and Jiaxing Li; ​Editing by Kate Mayberry, Shri Navaratnam, Susan Fenton, Elaine Hardcastle and Aurora Ellis)

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Susquehanna is reshuffling price targets across the semiconductor sector ahead of earnings, raising its outlook for AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ), Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ) and Skyworks Solutions while cutting targets for Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ), Onsemi, Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed.

The firm raised AMD's target to $620 from $550 , Qualcomm's to $185 from $160 , and Skyworks' to $90 from $65 .

Intel's target was cut to $105 from $115 , while Onsemi was reduced to $120 from $150. Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed were also lowered.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland said AI remains the biggest source of upside, but the broader semiconductor cycle is also improving.

The firm's SemiSIGnals data showed lead times expanding by roughly two weeks for a second consecutive quarter , while pricing actions are becoming more aggressive.

Susquehanna also expects additional price increases in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

The problem is that not every end market is participating equally.

PC demand is tracking below expectations, which could leave second-half client results for both AMD and Intel below normal seasonal patterns.

In response, both companies are shifting wafer capacity away from PCs and toward servers, where demand tied to agentic AI remains much stronger.

Susquehanna also expects ARM-based hyperscale CPUs to keep gaining share as they increasingly serve as host processors for custom AI accelerators.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of Susquehanna's note is the widening split between AI-driven data center demand and weaker consumer electronics .

For AMD, that is relatively favorable because server demand gives the company another avenue to offset softness in PCs.

For Intel, the same shift helps, but weaker client demand still creates more pressure on the near-term setup.

Qualcomm benefits from the high end of the handset market holding up better, although Susquehanna remains cautious on smartphones overall because of memory constraints and deteriorating demand in China.

For investors, the key things to watch are server revenue, wafer reallocation, semiconductor pricing, hyperscaler capex and whether PC and handset weakness becomes more severe .

The chip cycle still appears to be improving.

But increasingly, the strongest part of that recovery is concentrated around AI infrastructure rather than broad-based consumer demand.

news.Title: SpaceX stock slips as tech trade tumbles
news.Content:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock slipped in early trading Thursday, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.

Shares jumped 7.8% on Wednesday following SpaceX's upbeat third quarter results and AI commentary.

The stock is under pressure today along with the broader tech trade, following Meta ( META ) earnings and more headlines suggesting new strikes in the US/Israeli war with Iran.

As for SpaceX, it guided fourth quarter capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion, up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, as more compute capacity comes online. The company ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years," MoffettNathanson analyst Julie Zhu wrote in a note to clients.

"We are investment grade, have a very strong balance sheet, and there are a number of available pools of debt capital," SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said on the earnings call.

Then there's the merger talk. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla ( TSLA ) have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a tie-up, and that he is recused as a conflicted party. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said .

That endorsement created a "mess" for the process, a person with direct knowledge of the talks told Reuters . Insiders worry the resulting shareholder scrutiny could delay talks by several weeks.

Bloomberg separately reported that the companies are aiming to announce a deal in the first half of 2027.

On the flipside, Wall Street is now more bullish on SpaceX's prospects. JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target to $500 from $240, citing AI infrastructure growth. BofA raised its target to $275 from $235.

Barclays analyst Dan Levy flagged Tesla's annual meeting, which must be held by Dec. 6, as the likely venue for a shareholder vote. He added that a deal announced in late October or early November could push approval out six to 12 months.

news.Title: Chip stocks break a bear trap after a $3 trillion rout — here are the levels bulls need to hold
news.Content: Chip bulls sprang a bear trap on Tuesday. Two sessions later, the floor under it has cracked. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is down about 6% Thursday, slicing below 11,000 — the support that rescued the group twice since September. A bear trap is a breakdown that quickly reverses, catching traders who bet on further losses. This one only worked as long as that floor held. The index is on track for its worst day since July and its lowest close since July 29. The damage is piling up. All 60 stocks in a Yahoo Finance chip basket are down since Oct. 6, erasing about $3 trillion in market value, more than $800 billion of it Thursday alone. Lam Research ( LRCX ) and Applied Materials ( AMAT ) have each lost nearly 30% in that span, and AMD ( AMD ) more than 20%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) has fallen less, but on its size that's more than $600 billion. Lam is leading Thursday's slide after reporting record revenue Wednesday night. The company said supply limits capped its outlook and that China sales will be "meaningfully down" in December. The selling isn't sparing the giants. Meta ( META ) is shedding about $100 billion in market value after its earnings, and SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) are sliding too. Still, the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) is down about 7% since Oct. 6. Chips are down nearly three times as much. The 11,000 floor is cracking The index closed near 11,130 on Sept. 14 and again on Oct. 16. Tuesday's dip into that zone reversed sharply, springing the trap. Thursday's break puts the 10,450-10,550 zone in focus. That's where the summer rally started on July 29. The 200-day moving average sits just above it. On the upside, bulls first need to win back 11,000, then 12,600-12,700. That area capped rallies in August and September. Dip buyers haven't given up Semiconductor ETFs saw record flows over the past week, Bloomberg senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas posted Thursday. "Buying the dip here has [a] pretty good record of working," he wrote. There's little room to hide from the AI trade. "Every index on the planet is basically an AI index," Matt Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, said on Yahoo Finance's live show Thursday. Watch whether buyers can pull the index back above 11,000 by the close. A close above it keeps the bulls' hopes alive, while a close below puts the 10,500 area in play. Growth stocks are attractive to many investors, as above-average financial growth helps these stocks easily grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. However, it isn't easy to find a great growth stock.

By their very nature, these stocks carry above-average risk and volatility. Moreover, if a company's growth story is over or nearing its end, betting on it could lead to significant loss.

However, the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects, makes it pretty easy to find cutting-edge growth stocks.

Lam Research (LRCX) is on the list of such stocks currently recommended by our proprietary system. In addition to a favorable Growth Score, it carries a top Zacks Rank.

Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And returns are even better for stocks that possess the combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy).

Here are three of the most important factors that make the stock of this semiconductor equipment maker a great growth pick right now.

Earnings Growth

Arguably nothing is more important than earnings growth, as surging profit levels is what most investors are after. And for growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is definitely preferable, and often an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.

While the historical EPS growth rate for Lam Research is 10.1%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 61% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 43%.

Cash Flow Growth

Cash is the lifeblood of any business, but higher-than-average cash flow growth is more beneficial and important for growth-oriented companies than for mature companies. That's because, high cash accumulation enables these companies to undertake new projects without raising expensive outside funds.

Right now, year-over-year cash flow growth for Lam Research is 36%, which is higher than many of its peers. In fact, the rate compares to the industry average of 1.5%.

While investors should actually consider the current cash flow growth, it's worth taking a look at the historical rate too for putting the current reading into proper perspective. The company's annualized cash flow growth rate has been 12.7% over the past 3-5 years versus the industry average of 4.6%.

Promising Earnings Estimate Revisions

Beyond the metrics outlined above, investors should consider the trend in earnings estimate revisions. A positive trend is a plus here. Empirical research shows that there is a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The current-year earnings estimates for Lam Research have been revising upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has surged 0.3% over the past month.

Bottom Line

While the overall earnings estimate revisions have made Lam Research a Zacks Rank #2 stock, it has earned itself a Growth Score of B based on a number of factors, including the ones discussed above.

news.Title: Dan Ives Makes Major Calls on Tesla, Meta Stocks
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives remains bullish on both Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) and Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) following their latest earnings reports, but the investment cases are diverging sharply.

Tesla shares fell after hours despite delivering a modest earnings beat, while Meta climbed as investors responded more positively to evidence that its massive AI spending is already improving the core advertising business.

Tesla reported $28.05 billion in revenue , roughly flat year over year and essentially in line with consensus. Adjusted earnings came in at $0.48 per share , topping the $0.45 estimate, while automotive revenue of $20.56 billion exceeded expectations.

Margins also came in stronger than expected.

Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits reached 18.1% , ahead of the 16.8% analysts expected.

But operating expenses jumped 39% year over year , reflecting Tesla's continued spending on AI, autonomy and robotics.

Ives remains focused on Tesla's longer-term optionality.

He assigns the stock an Outperform rating and $500 price target , implying roughly 29% upside, and said he believes there is an 80% to 90% chance Tesla and SpaceX merge by the end of 2027 .

Meta's quarter offered a more immediate AI payoff.

Revenue increased 26% to $64.60 billion , beating consensus, while advertising revenue reached $63.06 billion. Average ad prices rose 14%, ahead of expectations.

Excluding a $9.89 billion legal settlement charge, EPS reached $7.40 , above the $6.66 consensus, while operating income also topped estimates.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest distinction is timing .

Tesla's bull case still depends heavily on what autonomy, robotics and possibly a SpaceX combination could become.

Meta, by contrast, is already showing investors that AI is improving monetization inside an enormous existing advertising business.

Ives remains bullish on both, with a $500 target on Tesla and $900 on Meta , each implying roughly 29% upside from the levels cited in the report.

For investors, the key things to watch are Tesla's expense growth, FSD adoption and potential SpaceX merger progress versus Meta's ad pricing, AI-driven engagement and infrastructure spending .

Both companies are spending heavily on AI.

news.Title: 3 Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever
news.Content:
Dividend investing will never go out of style, and for good reason. Buying shares of companies that pay and consistently raise their dividends is a great way to earn long-term returns, as it allows investors to put the magic of compounding to work through dividend reinvestment. Of course, dividend stocks come in all shapes and sizes, and some of them aren't worth the trouble for long-term investors. Let's consider three that are worth investing in: Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Visa (NYSE:V).

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Coca-Cola

Coca-Cola boasts one of the most popular brands in the world. The company has a large beverage portfolio across multiple categories and generates consistent revenue and earnings. Coca-Cola has been doing it for a while, and over the long run, it has avoided becoming an irrelevant company by keeping up with changing consumer tastes and preferences.

Coca-Cola has introduced new products, innovative twists on old products, and acquired new brands. These efforts have allowed it to remain one of the top players in its industry, and there is more to come. Coca-Cola estimates that it accounts for 2.2 billion of the 65 billion daily beverage servings worldwide.

Increased sales volume and market share gains could help the company grow its revenue and earnings, and we have seen the consumer staples giant pull that off this year. In the second quarter, the company grew its share of the non-alcoholic ready-to-drink beverage market. That's just one quarter, but Coca-Cola appears well-positioned to maintain consistent revenue and earnings growth over the long run. Finally, the company has a fantastic dividend track record.

Coca-Cola is a Dividend King . These are companies with 50 or more consecutive annual dividend increases. Coca-Cola's streak is at 64, and it seems unlikely to end soon, making the stock a great pick for long-term income seekers.

2. Microsoft

Microsoft has rebounded over the past few months, after hitting a brand new 52-week low in June. Some investors worry that artificial intelligence (AI) will replace the company's services, even as it spends fortunes on the technology. But Microsoft's latest quarterly update showed signs that the company is adapting to the new AI world order.

Story Continues

The tech leader has integrated AI across its products and services, and its customers are buying it. AI is helping Microsoft's revenue and earnings grow at a good clip. That's particularly true for the company's cloud business, which is firing on all cylinders.

This highlights something important about Microsoft. The company has faced multiple major technological revolutions that threatened its business over its long and storied history, and it has come out on top every single time. My view is that the company will do the same this time around. Microsoft could capitalize on the AI and cloud industry's growth over the long term, while using its massive pile of cash to tap into new growth opportunities.

Finally, though it isn't known primarily as an income stock, Microsoft has a decent dividend program. The company increases its payouts regularly. Microsoft's 0.7% forward yield isn't particularly impressive, but the company could maintain healthy dividend growth while providing competitive returns to long-term investors.

3. Visa

Visa faces various legal and regulatory problems, including antitrust concerns, that have affected its stock performance in recent years. However, the core business remains solid. Visa has increased its revenue and earnings at a good clip in recent quarters, and its dominant position in the payment processing market remains mostly intact.

Visa has billions of cards in circulation, and its network gets more attractive to merchants with every new cardholder, and more useful to cardholders with every new merchant. This self-reinforcing cycle underpins its wide moat.

Even with recent challenges, the company's long-term prospects -- tied to the increased demand for digital forms of payment -- remain attractive. Secular tailwinds, such as the growth of e-commerce, will help increase the company's already large remaining addressable market.

So, the future still looks bright for Visa, and the company is also an impressive dividend growth stock. Despite a forward yield of just 0.7%, Visa has increased its payouts by 306% over the past decade.

news.Title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Soar After Oct. 29. Here Are 379 Billion Reasons Why
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock has fallen from grace in recent months after delivering a stunning performance in the first half of 2026.

Shares of the flash storage specialist have pulled back 32% since the beginning of July. For comparison, Sandisk stock rose by a stunning 858% in the first half of 2026. The recent slide in Sandisk stock has nothing to do with the company's financial performance. Investors have pressed the panic button and are booking profits in Sandisk amid concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, a closer look at the developments in the NAND flash industry suggests that the fears about a slowdown in Sandisk's growth are overblown. In fact, I won't be surprised to see the company deliver stronger-than-expected fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on Oct. 29.

Let's check the reasons why Sandisk stock could take off following its upcoming quarterly report.

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk's growth and potential don't justify its slide

The incredible demand for NAND flash storage in AI data centers has been Sandisk's biggest growth driver. The resulting supply shortage has led to a massive increase in NAND flash prices, which explains the red-hot growth in Sandisk's revenue and earnings.

The company expects fiscal Q1 revenue of $10.3-$10.8 billion, along with non-GAAP earnings of $45.00 per share. The guidance implies a year-over-year increase of 357% in revenue at the midpoint, along with a 37x jump in non-GAAP earnings per share. Market research firm TrendForce expects NAND flash prices to surge by 235% in 2026, which explains why Sandisk is anticipating such phenomenal growth in fiscal Q1.

Even better, analysts expect Sandisk to sustain its red-hot growth in the current quarter as well. Consensus estimates on Yahoo! Finance predict a 4x year-over-year increase in Sandisk's revenue in the current quarter to $12.2 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share could increase by 8x to $52.94. So, the recent slide in Sandisk's stock price isn't justified when we consider that the strong NAND flash demand and price environment will continue to remain a tailwind for the company.

Moreover, the NAND flash market is poised for further growth in 2027. TrendForce expects NAND flash industry revenue to reach $379 billion in 2027, up 40% from this year. Of course, the market's growth rate is expected to slow substantially next year compared with 2026's estimated 280%, but that's still a healthy number.

Story Continues

Importantly, Sandisk can make the most of this huge opportunity given that it controls 11% of the NAND flash market, according to Counterpoint Research. A similar share of this market at the end of 2027 could send Sandisk's revenue in calendar 2027 to almost $42 billion, double the revenue it has generated over the past twelve months.

So, Sandisk seems poised to grow at a robust pace over the next year and a half, given the incredible $379 billion addressable opportunity it is sitting on. Throw in the fact that the NAND flash industry will remain undersupplied in 2027 and 2028, according to Citi , and Sandisk should also be able to clock healthy earnings growth.

This probably explains why there has been a slight uptick in Sandisk's earnings per share expectations for the current and the next fiscal year.

SNDK EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

A stronger-than-expected outlook can supercharge the stock

One of the reasons why this AI stock has been under pressure lately is because of concerns that NAND flash supply growth will overtake demand next year. This could erase the pricing advantage that Sandisk has been enjoying.

However, the points discussed above suggest otherwise. Additionally, robust NAND flash demand from AI servers could lead to a sequential increase of 15%-20% in NAND flash contract prices in the current quarter, according to TrendForce. This is why I think Sandisk's guidance for the ongoing quarter may exceed expectations, giving the stock a much-needed boost.

Another reason why Sandisk seems like a no-brainer buy right now is that it trades at an extremely cheap 8 times forward earnings. The S&P 500 index, for comparison, has a forward earnings multiple of 19. Sandisk should ideally trade at a significant premium given its exponential growth rate. So, it makes sense for savvy investors to buy this growth stock before Oct. 29 as strong results and a sunny guidance could set it up for a strong finish to the year.

news.Title: Meta Makes Surprise Financial Move as AI Spending Soars
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) is restructuring its share setup to give the company more flexibility to raise capital for artificial intelligence without diluting existing voting power.

Shareholders controlling a majority of Meta's voting rights approved amendments creating a new Class C common stock , along with changes to the company's 2025 Equity Incentive Plan allowing Meta to issue either Class A or Class C shares.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The changes are expected to take effect on Jan. 19, 2027 , with the new Class C shares set to trade on Nasdaq.

The move comes as Meta warns it could need to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years , beginning as early as fall 2026, to fund AI investment, acquisitions and employee compensation.

Because the Class C shares would carry no voting power, Meta can potentially raise large amounts of capital without changing the existing balance of corporate control.

Meta also disclosed an unusual agreement with CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

The company said Zuckerberg had threatened to leave California if voters approve a proposed wealth tax next month. Under the agreement, he will receive non-voting shares that can be sold to help cover a potential multi-billion-dollar tax bill in exchange for committing to remain a resident of California, or wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, for eight years.

Meta said a special board committee concluded it was critically important that Zuckerberg remain in a leadership role during what the company described as an unusually competitive period driven by AI.

Zuckerberg could immediately sell 20% of the Class C shares he receives , equivalent to 10% of his overall economic stake, without giving up voting control.

Investor Takeaway

I think the bigger story here is control and capital .

Meta expects its AI ambitions to require an extraordinary amount of funding, and the new Class C structure gives it another way to raise that money without materially weakening Zuckerberg's voting influence.

That could be strategically useful if AI capex continues climbing into the hundreds of billions.

But investors will also want to watch dilution.

The structure may preserve voting control, but issuing more economic shares can still affect ownership percentages and per-share economics.

news.Title: Meta stock drops more than 6% despite strong Q3 results, stock split
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) stock plunged more than 6% on Thursday, despite reporting better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue results after the bell on Wednesday.

The declines come as i nvestors continue to pull back on semiconductor and other AI stocks amid ongoing concerns about data center spending and returns on massive AI investments.

Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimates to between $135 billion and $145 billion from $130 billion and $145 billion. The company also has $825 billion in various spending commitments related to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products.

Despite Wall Street's reaction to Meta's earnings, analysts were largely bullish on the company's outlook, owing to its prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg repeatedly pointed to Muse as a source of growth potential during the company's earnings call, saying "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years," as long as compute efficiency in AI systems continues to improve.

Meta posted an all-time high revenue of $64 billion in the quarter, well ahead of the $63.3 billion analysts anticipated. GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus expectations of $3.56, but would have been $7.40 without legal charges related to the company's teen mental health settlement.

The company also announced it will issue new non-voting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders , effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split. The move is meant to ensure Zuckerberg stays in California and retains voting control of the company if the state's Proposition 40 passes on Election Day.

Prop. 40 calls for a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

Ahead of Meta's earnings report, a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in connection with the state's consumer-harms case against the social media giant.

news.Title: Meta FCF Flips Negative: Why Investors Should Overlook It
news.Content:
Why Did Meta Move Up Its Earnings Date?

Just before the normal market trading hours concluded on Wednesday, investors finally got an answer on why Meta Platforms ( META ) moved up its earnings date. Meta plans to issue nonvoting shares to fund AI investments without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta also narrowed its FY26 CAPEX outlook to $130-$145B.

Meta Misses EPS Expectations Due to One-Time Charges

Meta Platforms reported mixed earnings after Wednesday's market close. Revenue of $64.60B beat Wall Street expectations of $63.33B (26% YoY growth). EPS of $3.83 fell well short of Wall Street expectations of $5.89 (+265% YoY growth). However, the EPS miss was driven by one-time, non-operating expenses, including a $2.4 billion legal settlement, restructuring costs, and aggressive AI infrastructure and CAPEX. Investors should take the headline EPS number with a grain of salt, as nothing has materially changed in Meta's core business. For instance, Ad revenue, Meta's most important number, jumped 28%. Additionally, Ad impressions and price per Ad each jumped double digits year over year as AI continues to optimize the Meta family of products, while the company's headcount plunged 15%.

Meta Free Cash Flow Flips Negative

The post-EPS headline Wall Street is focused on is that, in Q3, Meta posted its first negative free cash flow quarter since it went public in 2012.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

While this stat should normally raise concerns, investors must apply some nuance in their analysis.

Why Investors Should Overlook Meta's Negative Free Cash Flow

On Wall Street, CEOs generally fall into two categories: caretakers and visionaries. For instance, the CEO of a company like Pepsi ( PEP ) is going to operate completely differently than the CEO of a cutting-edge tech company like Meta. In Pepsi's case, the CEO's main goal is to ensure nothing "breaks," the company generates cash flow, and it stays stable. Conversely, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is hyper-focused on spotting the next big tech trends and turning them into growth opportunities. For instance, many Wall Street pundits scoffed when Zuckerberg purchased Instagram for $1 billion in April 2012. Today, Instagram is worth an estimated $70 billion.

Meta Muse Will Spur Future Growth

"Muse," Meta's agentic AI platform, is the answer to the spending question. On the conference call, Mark Zuckerberg said that he expects Muse to beat the Meta family apps average revenue per user over time. In just one month, Muse achieved 10 million setups. The app has also consistently topped the Apple App Store rankings. Most impressively, shopping is the #1 use case, and the average purchase size is over $200. While Muse is still in its early days, continued CAPEX spending is justified by the impressive early traction it's achieved.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

While negative free cash flow often signals trouble, Meta's temporary dip is a deliberate reinvestment into its high-growth future. With a thriving core ad business and early traction from agentic AI platforms like Muse, Mark Zuckerberg's aggressive CAPEX strategy is setting the stage for Meta's next multi-billion-dollar expansion.

news.Title: Vicor Corporation Shares Gain 4.5% on Strong Q3 Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Vicor Corporation VICR shares have gained 4.5% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 20. The uptick can be attributed to strong AI-driven demand and rising recurring royalty revenues, which lifted sales, margins and profitability.

The company reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.33 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.32%. The figure increased 111.1% year over year.

Revenues surged 78.5% year over year to $197.11 million and surpassed the consensus estimate by 5.4%. Strong Advanced Products sales and higher royalty income supported growth. The company's order backlog increased 166% year over year to $406 million, reflecting robust demand.

VICR's Advanced Products Revenues Accelerate

Advanced Products revenues, including royalties, increased 47.5% sequentially to $138.9 million. The business accounted for 70.4% of total revenues, up from 65.7% in the preceding quarter.

Vicor Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

Brick Products revenues increased 18.4% sequentially to $58.3 million and represented 29.6% of total revenues.

Shipments to stocking distributors increased 24.8% sequentially and 16.2% year over year. Exports accounted for approximately 36.1% of revenues, down from 46% in the second quarter of 2026.

Vicor Benefits From Expanding Royalty Income

Product revenues totaled $130.5 million, up 47.1% year over year. Royalty revenues surged 206.6% year over year to $66.6 million from $21.7 million. Sequentially, royalty revenues increased 119.1%, supported by licensing agreements.

The company granted its first vertical power delivery (VPD) license to a leading artificial intelligence (AI) original equipment manufacturer at Stage 2-unit royalty rates. Management noted that part of the quarterly royalty contribution reflected initial payments, while the underlying licensing arrangements provide recurring income.

Vicor also received inquiries from hyperscalers regarding broader licensing agreements. Management expects royalty income to grow as additional customers adopt its intellectual property, although the timing of payments and new agreements could create quarterly fluctuations.

VICR's Backlog Reflects Strong Market Demand

The book-to-bill ratio remained above 1, while backlog increased 7% sequentially to $380 million. Management highlighted approximately $100 million in bookings during the first two weeks of the fourth quarter, including a substantial order for second-generation VPD modules.

Demand remained strong across AI computing, automatic test equipment (ATE), industrial, aerospace and defense markets. The company's ATE business, which serves semiconductor and memory testing applications, now generates more than $100 million in annual revenues.

Management highlighted growing customer interest in second-generation VPD technology following demonstrations at Open Compute. The technology aims to address increasing power density and efficiency requirements for advanced AI processors.

Story Continues

Vicor's Margins Expand Despite Rising Expenses

Gross profit increased sequentially to $134.7 million from $83.1 million. Gross margin expanded 1,030 basis points to 68.3%, benefiting from higher royalty revenues, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and increased volumes.

Operating expenses increased 29.6% sequentially to $62.5 million. Legal expenses, a substantial portion of which are linked to royalty revenues, increased approximately $11.1 million to $16.1 million. Management expects legal expenses to average approximately 20% of royalty revenues in the near term.

Operating income surged 245.1% year over year to $72.1 million from $20.9 million in the year-ago quarter.

VICR Strengthens Cash Position and Expands Capacity

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $513.1 million compared with $453.6 million in the previous quarter.

Operating activities generated $69.7 million in cash compared with $34 million in the second quarter.

Vicor acquired two additional manufacturing sites within 30 miles of its existing Andover facility. The planned Fab-2 and Fab-3 facilities could increase manufacturing capacity nearly fivefold relative to Fab-1.

Management expects initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 in the second quarter of 2027. The expansion will initially target capacity-constrained manufacturing processes. The company expects to fund its expansion plans without raising additional capital.

Vicor Expects Further Product Revenue Growth

Vicor expects fourth-quarter 2026 product revenues to increase approximately 10% sequentially. The outlook assumes another double-digit sequential increase in Advanced Products hardware revenues.

Management also expects at least $43 million in fourth-quarter royalty revenues, assuming no additional licensing agreements. Existing arrangements could generate incremental royalties beyond this baseline.

The company anticipates further margin expansion as revenues increase and manufacturing utilization improves. However, near-term capacity constraints at Fab-1 remain a consideration as Vicor works to expand production capabilities and meet growing customer demand.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Watch

Vicor currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Alkami Technology ALKT, ASE Technology ASX, and Entegris ENTG are some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. While ASE Technology sports a Zacks Rank #1, Alkami Technology and Entegris carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Alkami Technology, ASE Technology and Entegris are expected to report their quarterly results on Oct. 28, Oct. 29 and Oct. 29, respectively. While Shares of ASE Technology and Entegris have surged 163.5% and 75.3%, respectively, Alkami Technology shares have plunged 34.5% in the year-to-date period.

news.Title: Can Semiconductor Systems Drive AMAT's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
Applied Materials AMAT is gaining from rising demand for advanced chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, especially in its Semiconductor Systems business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Systems generated revenues of $7.04 billion, up approximately 27% year over year.

Growing investment in leading-edge foundry-logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging is creating opportunities for the company's wafer fabrication equipment, while rising manufacturing complexity supports demand for differentiated process technologies.

Applied Materials is expanding its technology portfolio to capitalize on these opportunities. Its Centris Spectral SiN ALD system supports advanced logic manufacturing, while enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD systems target DRAM performance and higher-layer-count high-bandwidth memory.

Beyond revenue growth, Semiconductor Systems is strengthening Applied Materials' profitability. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 55.4% in the third quarter from 53.5% a year earlier. The operating margin expanded to 38% from 33.2%, reflecting the value of its technology portfolio and operating leverage.

AMAT anticipates fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Semiconductor Systems revenues to be approximately $7.9 billion, suggesting 62% year-over-year growth. The outlook indicates that demand across leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging could sustain strong near-term momentum.

How Competitors Fare Against AMAT

Applied Materials faces competition from Lam Research (LRCX), KLA Corporation (KLAC) and other semiconductor equipment suppliers, although their primary areas of specialization differ. Lam Research secured multiple critical etch wins at a major DRAM manufacturer with its new Akara etch system, which supports 3D DRAM architectures. This was supported by LRCX's customer investments in DDR5, LPDDR5 and high-bandwidth memory.

Lam Research's Aether dry-resist technology was recently selected as the production tool of record for a leading DRAM customer, securing a foothold in this high-growth segment. Although KLA does not compete directly with AMAT across its entire Semiconductor Systems portfolio, both companies can benefit from rising investment in advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

AMAT's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Applied Materials shares have climbed 59.1% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's appreciation of 15.9% and 18%, respectively.

news.Title: Can Strong Momentum in LoRa Boost Semtech's Long-Term Growth?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

How Competitors Fare Against SMTC

Semtech faces competition from Texas Instruments TXN and NXP Semiconductors NXPI across the broader industrial and Internet of Things (IoT) markets.

Texas Instruments offers Sub-1 GHz wireless microcontrollers and transceivers designed for applications such as smart meters, building automation and industrial sensors. These products provide long-range connectivity while using little power, making them an alternative for certain applications served by Semtech's LoRa technology. In the third quarter of 2026, TXN's revenues rose 28% year over year to $6.1 billion, while industrial revenues grew more than 40%. The company is expanding manufacturing capacity to support rising customer demand. These investments and its broad wireless product portfolio strengthen TXN's position in industrial and connected-device markets.

Story Continues

NXPI also offers low-power Sub-GHz wireless products for smart metering, home and building automation, asset tracking and industrial monitoring. Its OL2385 transceiver family supports multiple wireless protocols, including Sigfox and Wireless M-Bus, giving customers options for connected-device applications. NXPI's industrial and IoT business reported revenues of $755 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 38% year over year. Its newer processing products, including the i.MX, RT and MCX families, grew 40% year over year, reflecting strong demand for its industrial and IoT portfolio.

SMTC's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Shares of SMTC have jumped 92.2% in the year-to-date period compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's return of 38.4%.
